1Quick start

This chapter describes the shortest path from opening Cam Hub to the first live picture. Without a device at hand, the sample cameras can be used to try the app.

Before you begin

ItemDescription
NetworkCam Hub connects directly to the network address of the device and does not use a cloud service of the manufacturer. The iPhone or iPad must be on the same local network as the device, or must be able to reach its address.
IP address of the deviceThe address is listed in the connection list of the router or in the manufacturer's own app. It can also be found with the network scan; see “Finding devices with the network scan”.
Account of the deviceUsually the administrator account that was created when the device was first set up. On the device, the account needs the permissions for the functions to be used, for example live view, recording playback and PTZ control.
Local Network permissionOn first use, the system asks whether Cam Hub may find and connect to devices on the local network. Without this permission, Cam Hub cannot connect to devices. The permission can be turned on later under Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › Cam Hub.

Shortest path to a live picture

  1. Tap the Devices tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the device list. When no device has been added yet, it shows No Devices.

  2. Tap the ＋ button in the top-right corner.

    Check: A menu opens that contains Add Device.

  3. Select Add Device.

    Check: The screen shows the add-device form.

  4. Enter the address of the device in the IP address or hostname field.

    Check: The Add button in the top-right corner is available.

  5. Enter the account of the device in the Username and Password fields.

    Check: The Username field holds the typed name instead of the preset admin. The ports and Connect using stay folded under Advanced; with Auto-detect, no change is needed there.

  6. Tap Add in the top-right corner.

    Check: The form shows Connecting to device… with the step in progress, for example Looking for open ports…. When the connection succeeds, the form closes and the new device appears in the device list. For a network storage device that can report the health of its disks, the optional SNMP Settings sheet opens first; Not Now closes it, and it can be set up later, see “Disk Health”.

  7. Tap the newly added device in the device list.

    Check: The device page shows the device information and a thumbnail for each channel.

  8. Tap the thumbnail of a channel that is enabled.

    Check: The screen shows the live picture of that camera.

If the connection fails, see “When adding fails: the checklist”. If a thumbnail does not open, see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels” and Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”. To watch several cameras at once, see Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”. Where they are offered, the menu of step 2 also adds a YouTube live stream or Twitch channels as cameras; see “Adding YouTube live streams and Twitch channels”.

Trying the app without a device

At the bottom of the add-device form, Add Demo Cameras creates two sample cameras that draw their own picture. No device and no sign-in are needed, so they can be used to try live view and LiveView Mix. The sample cameras have no recording playback. The button is not shown when the form was opened from a scan result that already identified the device.

Delete the sample device before connecting real equipment

The sample device counts as a recorder. It uses up the recorder allowance and the enabled-channel allowance of the free plan. For deleting a device, see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”; for the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

2The tabs and basic behaviour

The bottom of the screen holds five tabs, from left to right: LiveView Mix, Live, Devices, Tools and Settings. This chapter describes the purpose of each tab, how the app starts and behaves, and how it uses the displays of an iPhone Duo.

The tabs at a glance

TabPurposeDetails
LiveView MixPlaces cameras from different devices on one wall, with optional clocks, pictures and control buttons.Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”
LiveShows the live wall with all enabled channels of one device.Chapter 5, “The Live tab and the Full Screen Wall”
DevicesAdds and manages devices. Opening a device shows its channels. Where they are offered, YouTube live streams and Twitch channels are added here as cameras too.Chapter 3, “Adding a device”, Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”, “Adding YouTube live streams and Twitch channels”
ToolsScans the network to find cameras and recorders. Depending on the region and the language setting, it also holds a speedometer with compass.Chapter 12, “The Tools tab”, “Finding devices with the network scan”
SettingsPlans, default quality, picture, LiveView Mix, backup and restore, sharing cameras, language, reset, the legal pages and a link to this manual.Chapter 13, “Settings”

The last row of the Settings tab, User Manual, opens this manual on the Cam Hub website. Beyond the iPhone and the iPad, Cam Hub runs on Apple TV, see Chapter 14, “Apple TV”, and an Apple Watch app sends the requests of the LiveView Mix control-panel buttons from the wrist, see “Buttons on Apple Watch”.

What opens when the app starts

The app always starts on the LiveView Mix tab. It does not return to the tab that was open when the app was last closed. To start on the live wall of one device, or directly on the full-screen LiveView Mix wall, change Open on launch in the Settings tab; see “LiveView Mix, its pages and Open on launch”.

Appearance and language

The app uses a dark appearance only; there is no light or dark setting. The language follows the system language by default and can be changed in Settings to one of ten languages: English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, German, Spanish, Spanish (Mexico) and French. The row that chooses it is always labelled in English, and in Arabic the screens are laid out from right to left. See “Language”.

Turning the device

The app does not lock the screen orientation. On an iPhone it works upright and in both landscape orientations; on an iPad it works in all four orientations. The full-screen wall lays itself out again when the shape of the screen changes; see “The full-screen wall”. How the app follows the folding of an iPhone Duo is described in the next section.

iPhone Duo

On iPhone Duo, Cam Hub uses the outer display while the phone is closed and the larger inner display while it is open. The screens lay themselves out again whenever the phone is folded, unfolded or turned.

How the phone is heldWhat the app showsDetails
Closed (outer display)The same screens as on other iPhones.—
Open flat (inner display)The camera walls of the Live tab and of the device pages show two columns, as on an iPad. The full-screen LiveView Mix wall fills the whole inner display. A camera can open in a window of its own with Open in New Window, so that one window keeps a wall and another the camera with its recordings.“A camera in a window of its own”
Half-folded, hinge across the screenThe camera page puts the picture on the upper half and the controls, the recordings and the PTZ pad on the lower half. With Two canvases switched on in Settings, LiveView Mix is cut at the hinge into an upper and a lower canvas, each with its own cameras and control panels.“The view on a folded iPhone Duo”, “Two canvases on iPhone Duo”
Half-folded, held upright like a bookFor a camera with recording playback, the camera page shows the live picture on one half and the same camera at the same time of day yesterday on the other. The device page shows its camera wall on one half and the camera that was tapped on the other.“The view on a folded iPhone Duo”

The Two canvases switch appears only on iPhone Duo. Opened flat or closed, the phone shows one LiveView Mix wall again.

Screen, background and notifications

While live or recorded video is on the screen, the display does not switch itself off. When the app leaves the foreground, every live stream stops and no sound plays in the background. When the app returns, the tiles connect again and a recording that was playing resumes where it stopped. The app sends no notifications and asks for no notification permission.

3Adding a device

Adding a camera or recorder requires its address and its account. Cam Hub finds out by itself how to connect to the device; a connection method and ports can be chosen under Advanced instead. YouTube live streams and Twitch channels are added from screens of their own.

The Add Device form

Path: Devices › ＋ › Add Device

FieldDescriptionDefault
Name (optional)The name under which the device is shown in Cam Hub. When left empty, the model reported by the device is used. A camera connected over plain RTSP whose brand is not known is named after its address, and a device added through a brand from the list is named after that brand.Empty
IP address or hostnameRequired. The network address of the device. A YouTube or Twitch link entered here leads to the screen for that service instead; see “Adding YouTube live streams and Twitch channels”.Empty
UsernameThe sign-in account of the device.admin
PasswordThe sign-in password of the device. The password is stored in the keychain of the iPhone or iPad.Empty
Advanced › Connect usingAuto-detect, ONVIF, RTSP, the own protocol of one device family, or a brand from the list. For the choice, see “Choosing the connection method”.Auto-detect
Advanced › HTTP PortThe port of the control interface of the device. With Auto-detect, Cam Hub finds the open ports by itself and tries a port entered here first. With ONVIF, the field must hold the ONVIF service port of the device, for example 2020 or 8899 on some devices.80
Advanced › RTSP PortThe port of the video stream. Auto-detect tries a port entered here first. Selecting a brand whose RTSP port is not 554 fills in that brand's port, as long as the field still holds the previous default.554
Advanced › Device PortShown instead of the two ports above when the own protocol of a device family is selected: the port on which the device answers that protocol.34567

  1. Tap the Devices tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the device list.

  2. Tap the ＋ button in the top-right corner. When the list is empty, the Add Device button in the middle of the screen opens the form directly.

    Check: A menu opens that contains Add Device, and, where they are offered, YouTube Live Stream and Twitch Channels.

  3. Select Add Device.

    Check: The screen shows the add-device form with the sections Device and Credentials, and the folded Advanced section.

  4. Optional: enter a name for the device in the Name (optional) field.

    Check: The field shows the name, which is later shown in the device list.

  5. Enter the address of the device in the IP address or hostname field, for example 192.168.1.64.

    Check: The Add button in the top-right corner is available.

  6. Enter the account of the device in the Username and Password fields.

    Check: Both fields are filled in. The password is masked with dots.

  7. Tap Add in the top-right corner.

    Check: The form shows Connecting to device… with the current step below it, for example Looking for open ports… or Trying ONVIF on port 8899…. When the connection succeeds, the form closes and the new device appears in the device list.

While the connection is made, a progress indicator replaces the Add button and the form cannot be closed with a downward swipe. Cancel stops the attempt, and nothing is saved. After connecting, Cam Hub identifies whether the device is a recorder or a single camera, reads the channel list and stores the device.

When the new device is a network storage device (NAS) whose disks Cam Hub can read over SNMP, the SNMP Settings sheet follows. This step is optional: Not Now closes the sheet, and SNMP can be set up later on the Disk Health page; see “Disk Health”. The device is stored either way.

The free plan enables only the channels within its allowance; the remaining channels are shown as Disabled. When the number of recorders allowed by the plan has been reached, the plans page opens. When the demo devices hold the recorder place of the free plan, the page says so; deleting the demo devices frees the place. YouTube live streams and Twitch channels never count toward a plan. For the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

The address of a stored device cannot be edited

A stored device can be renamed, and its username and password can be changed with Edit Credentials; see “Changing the user name and password of a device”. Its address cannot be changed. When the IP address changes, the new address is treated as a different device, and a recorder also counts against the recorder allowance. In that case, delete the old device first (see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”) and add the new address. Adding a device again with the same address, port and username updates the stored device in place instead of creating a second one.

Adding without choosing a brand

With the default Auto-detect, the address and the account are all that Cam Hub needs. The add runs in two stages:

  1. Port check. Cam Hub checks which of the usual ports of cameras and recorders are open at the address: ports of web and control interfaces, ONVIF, RTSP, and the own protocol of a device family. The check sends no username and no password, so it cannot count toward locking the account. When nothing answers, the check is repeated once with longer waits.
  2. Connection attempts. Cam Hub then tries each way of connecting on the ports that answered, in this order: the manufacturer protocols that are built in, the own protocol of a device family, ONVIF, and plain RTSP. For RTSP, it tries the stream paths of a brand that the device revealed, then the paths that most cameras use, then the paths of every brand in the list. The first way that connects is kept, together with the port on which it connected.
  • Ports entered under Advanced are tried first. A port that differs from the default (80 or 554) and is open is used alone, because at an address that forwards several devices another port may belong to another device.
  • To protect the account, the attempt ends at once with Wrong username or password. when a manufacturer protocol refuses the sign-in. ONVIF and RTSP may use an account of their own, so they end the attempt after the second refused sign-in. After a refusal, stream paths are tried one at a time.
  • A camera that is reached only over RTSP is always added as a single camera. To add a recorder that offers only RTSP, select its brand and enter the number of cameras; see “Choosing the connection method”.
  • The own protocol of a device family is tried automatically only at addresses in the local network and on its default port. For such a device outside the local network or on another port, select its connection method under Advanced; see “Connection methods”.
  • Trying many stream paths takes time. For a camera that leaves wrong paths unanswered, the add can take more than a minute before it succeeds or fails.
  • When adding fails, the open ports that were found are listed below the error message, for example Open ports found: 80, 554, or the form shows No open ports were found at this address. The first means that the device answered but would not connect; the second, that nothing answered at all.

For the brands that Auto-detect recognizes and the exact order of the attempts, see “Connection methods”.

Choosing the connection method

Auto-detect suits most devices. When it cannot find the device, or when a particular protocol is wanted, select the connection method under Advanced.

  1. In the add-device form, tap Advanced.

    Check: The section opens and shows Connect using, HTTP Port and RTSP Port.

  2. Tap Connect using.

    Check: The Connect using list opens with a search field. At the top are Auto-detect, ONVIF, the own protocol of one device family and RTSP; below them, Brands lists the supported brands in alphabetical order.

  3. Optional: type part of a brand name in the search field.

    Check: The list shows only the matching choices. A brand is also found by other names under which its cameras are sold.

  4. Tap the connection method.

    Check: The form shows the method in the Connect using row, with an explanation below the section. A brand from the list, and RTSP, add a section with Cameras and a path field; the own protocol of a device family replaces the two ports with Device Port.

  5. When the device does not use the default ports, change the port fields.

    Check: The fields show the ports that the device uses.

The choices:

  • Auto-detect (default): Cam Hub finds the ports and the protocol by itself, as described in “Adding without choosing a brand”.
  • ONVIF: skips the detection and uses only the open ONVIF protocol, on the port in HTTP Port. Use it for a camera that Auto-detect does not find, or to use ONVIF on a device that also supports its own protocol. ONVIF must be turned on at the device; when the device has a separate ONVIF user list, a user must be created there. Whether recording playback and PTZ control are available depends on what the device offers.
  • RTSP: connects over plain RTSP to a camera of any brand and tries the stream paths that most cameras use. When none of them works, enter the path shown in the manual or on the web page of the camera.
  • The own protocol of a device family: connects over that protocol on Device Port, 34567 unless the port was changed or forwarded. Use it for a recorder that Auto-detect does not find, or for one that is reached from outside the local network. For an address outside the local network, the form shows a warning in orange: the protocol does not encrypt the video, and many devices protect the password only weakly; use a VPN where possible. The device family is named in “Connection methods”.
  • A brand from the list: connects directly over RTSP, using the stream paths documented for that brand. Use it when ONVIF is turned off at the device, or to add a recorder that offers only RTSP. The added section has two fields:
    • Cameras: a number from 1 to 64. With 1, the device is added as a single camera; with 2 or more, it is added as a recorder and counts against the recorder allowance. A network scan that learned the number of channels fills it in.
    • The path field: when left blank, Cam Hub tries the documented paths of that brand in turn and keeps the one that the device answers. The field shows the first path that is tried. Fill it in only to specify a particular path.

The brands whose devices have a manufacturer protocol built into Cam Hub are not in the list; Auto-detect finds them, as the note below the list states. Some brands need a dedicated camera or ONVIF account, created in the manufacturer's app or web interface, before RTSP works; the administrator account alone may be refused. For some brands, the paths vary by model or firmware, so the first attempt may not match. The form shows these notes below the path field. For the list of brands and the notes on each, see “The brands in the list”.

RTSP and a brand from the list provide live view only

These connection methods have no recording playback, no PTZ control and no snapshot. SD uses the second stream of the brand where the device serves it; otherwise SD shows the same stream as HD.

Device control uses HTTP only

Device control (identifying the device, reading the channel list, searching recordings) uses http://address:port; the device family with its own protocol uses that protocol instead. A device that accepts HTTPS only cannot be added at present.

Failure messages differ for RTSP and a brand from the list

When the device cannot be reached or times out, only Something went wrong. Please try again. is shown. With these connection methods, Not a supported device. means that none of the candidate paths returned a stream. Common causes are a wrong RTSP port or a video stream that is turned off at the device.

When it is unclear whether a device can be used, tap Compatibility reference in the form to see the supported and unsupported devices. The entry is not shown, and neither is Add Demo Cameras, when the form was opened from a scan result that named the brand of the device and the address has not been changed.

Adding YouTube live streams and Twitch channels

A YouTube live stream or a Twitch channel can be added to the device list and shown like a camera. It is played by the service's own player, needs no account and never counts toward a plan. It has no recordings, no PTZ control and no snapshot. Streams play on iPhone and iPad; Apple TV shows them by name only. YouTube and Twitch are not available in some countries and regions, and there these options do not appear.

The first time a screen for YouTube or for Twitch is opened, a notice appears: Before YouTube streams play or Before Twitch channels play. It explains that the service's own player plays the streams, that the service receives the IP address and information about the device and may use cookies and show ads, and that Cam Hub itself collects nothing. It links the service's terms of service and privacy policy and the Cam Hub Privacy Policy. Nothing of the service loads before Agree and Continue is tapped; Cancel closes the screen. The notice appears once for each service.

Adding a YouTube live stream

  1. In the Devices tab, tap the ＋ button in the top-right corner.

    Check: The menu shows Add Device, YouTube Live Stream and Twitch Channels.

  2. Select YouTube Live Stream.

    Check: On first use, the notice Before YouTube streams play appears. Otherwise, the YouTube Live Stream screen opens.

  3. On first use, read the notice and tap Agree and Continue.

    Check: The screen shows the fields YouTube link and Name (optional).

  4. Paste a link into YouTube link: the link of a live stream (in YouTube: Share, then Copy Link), or the link of a channel in the form youtube.com/channel/… to follow that channel.

    Check: YouTube's player shows the stream below the fields, with Checking that this is a live stream… under it. For a live stream, the LIVE badge and the title of the stream appear.

  5. Optional: enter a name in Name (optional).

    Check: The field shows the name. When it is left empty, the stream is named after its title.

  6. Tap Add in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen closes and the stream appears in the device list.

  • Add becomes available only when the player reports the stream as live. A recorded video, a broadcast that has ended, and a video whose owner does not allow playback in other apps are refused; the player shows the reason and Try Again.
  • For the link of a channel that is not live at the moment, the screen shows You can follow this channel anyway: it plays here whenever it goes live., and Add is available. The tile of a followed channel checks again every minute and starts by itself when the channel goes live.
  • A link to a channel name that starts with @ cannot be used; the screen shows Use the link of the live stream itself: open it on YouTube, tap Share, then Copy Link. A playlist cannot be added either.
  • Adding the same stream again only renames it.

Adding Twitch channels

  1. In the Devices tab, tap the ＋ button and select Twitch Channels.

    Check: On first use, the notice Before Twitch channels play appears. Otherwise, the Twitch Channels screen opens.

  2. On first use, read the notice and tap Agree and Continue.

    Check: The screen shows the field Channel names or links.

  3. Enter one or more channel names or links, separated by spaces, commas or new lines.

    Check: The list below the field shows each channel that will be added. A channel that is already in the device list shows Already followed; an entry that is not a channel shows a line such as Not a Twitch channel: twitch.tv/directory.

  4. Tap Add in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen closes. Each new channel appears in the device list as a camera named after the channel.

  • Add is available when the list holds at least one channel that is not followed yet.
  • Nothing is checked online. A channel plays in its tile whenever its streamer is live and shows Offline otherwise; a misspelled channel name stays Offline.

A link entered in the Add Device form

When a YouTube or Twitch link is entered in IP address or hostname, the Add button is unavailable and the form offers Add as a YouTube Live Stream or Add as a Twitch Channel. Tapping it opens the screen for that service with the link already entered; after the stream has been added, both screens close. Where the two services are not offered, the link is treated as an ordinary address.

When adding fails: the checklist

When adding fails, the form shows the error message in red. With Auto-detect, the open ports that were found are listed below it. Below that, the form lists Things to check first. The order of the list depends on the kind of failure, with the most likely cause first. Work through the items from top to bottom, then tap Add again.

Error messageChecks (from top to bottom)
Device unreachable. Check the address and your network.
  1. Check the IP address. Look it up on the router or in the manufacturer's own app, or use the scan in the Tools tab.
  2. Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi network as the device. Guest networks, a separate VLAN, or client isolation on the router block the connection.
  3. Allow Local Network access: Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › Cam Hub
  4. Turn off any VPN on the phone while adding a device on the home network.
  5. Make sure the device is powered on and its network cable or Wi-Fi is connected.
  6. Check the HTTP and RTSP ports. The usual ones are 80 and 554; some devices use 8000, 8080, 8899 or 37777.
  7. In the device settings, turn on ONVIF and RTSP. When the device has a separate ONVIF user list, create a user there.
Wrong username or password.
  1. Sign in once on the web page of the device itself to check the username and password. They are case-sensitive.
  2. A brand-new device must be activated first, usually by setting an administrator password, before any app can sign in; see “Activating a new device”.
  3. Too many wrong attempts can lock the account for a while, often about 30 minutes. Wait, then try once with the correct password.
  4. Set the clock of the device to the correct time, for example with network time. A clock that is off by minutes makes ONVIF sign-in fail.
  5. In the device settings, turn on ONVIF and RTSP. When the device has a separate ONVIF user list, create a user there.
  6. Try a different Connect using option under Advanced: ONVIF, or the brand of the camera from the list.
Not a supported device.
  1. Try a different Connect using option under Advanced: ONVIF, or the brand of the camera from the list.
  2. In the device settings, turn on ONVIF and RTSP. When the device has a separate ONVIF user list, create a user there.
  3. Check the HTTP and RTSP ports.
  4. Some devices work only through the cloud app of the manufacturer and offer no local connection. Cam Hub cannot connect to those devices.
Too many requests just now. Try again in a minute.
  1. Wait a minute, then try once more.
  2. When the request is still refused, the account may be locked temporarily after too many wrong attempts, often for about 30 minutes. Wait, then try once with the correct password.
Something went wrong. Please try again. and any other message not listed above
  1. Check the IP address.
  2. Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi network as the device.
  3. Check the HTTP and RTSP ports.
  4. Sign in once on the web page of the device itself to check the username and password.
  5. Try a different Connect using option under Advanced: ONVIF, or the brand of the camera from the list.
  6. Some devices work only through the cloud app of the manufacturer and offer no local connection. Cam Hub cannot connect to those devices.

When the failure persists after all items have been worked through, the experimental device report can be used; see “Device report (experimental)”.

Device report (experimental)

Experimental feature, no guarantee of support

The device report is an experimental feature. It may change or be removed at any time. Sending a report does not mean that the developer will add support for the device, and there is no guarantee of a reply, a fix or a timeline. Some devices cannot be supported by design, for example because of closed or proprietary protocols, cloud-only operation, licensing or encryption restrictions, or hardware limits. The feature is not a customer-support or urgent-help channel.

Collecting the details signs in to the device with the account and password that were entered. Failed sign-ins are counted, and may be logged, by the device. When the password may be wrong, correct it first as described in “When adding fails: the checklist” instead of trying repeatedly.

The Send details to the developer button, marked Experimental, appears below the checklist only after adding has failed; it is not shown when adding succeeds. The feature runs only when the button is tapped. It checks the device with read-only requests and assembles a text report for review. Cam Hub never uploads the report by itself; the report is sent only if the person chooses to email it from their own mail account.

Prerequisite: the checklist in “When adding fails: the checklist” has been worked through, and the address, username and password in the form are the ones that the device uses.

  1. In the form of the failed attempt, scroll to the checklist and tap Send details to the developer below it.

    Check: On first use, the screen shows the Device Report page with the full notice Before you collect details.

  2. Read the notice and tap I understand — collect details.

    Check: The screen shows Collecting details… and the progress of each check.

  3. Wait until the collection is complete.

    Check: What we found lists the likely causes and what to try first, in plain language. When nothing stands out, the screen shows Nothing obvious stands out.

  4. Under What to include, switch off the items that should not be sent.

    Check: The text in the The report section updates immediately.

  5. Review the full text in the The report section.

    Check: The report is plain text and is always in English. Data that was masked automatically is replaced by a mask marker.

  6. Tap Email to developer.

    Check: The screen opens the mail composer with the report in the message.

  7. Check the message and send it.

    Check: The mail composer closes and the report page is shown again.

  8. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The report page closes and the add-device form is shown again.

  • After the notice has been confirmed once, the report page shows only a short reminder at the top, with About this feature to read the full notice again.
  • During the collection, Stop in the top-left corner ends it early. What has been found so far is kept, the screen shows You stopped the collection, so this report is partial. Nothing has been sent. and offers Collect again.
  • What to include has five items: Network, HTTP fingerprint, Protocol probes, RTSP and video and App trace, each marked with a letter. The findings and the report header are always included.
  • Besides Email to developer, the report can be copied with Copy or passed on with Share…. A copy stays on this device only and expires after about 2 minutes.
  • When no mail account is set up, the screen shows Mail isn't set up on this device: the full report is copied to the clipboard, the mail app opens with the start of the report, and the full report must be pasted into the message.
  • The report leaves the device only when it is sent. Nothing is sent unless you choose to send the email. Your password is never included.

Sign-in behavior

During the collection, requests that need a sign-in are sent one at a time until the device has accepted or refused the credentials. After the device has refused them, the report sends no further sign-ins. When the failed attempt that led to the report was itself a refused sign-in (Wrong username or password.), the report does not try to sign in at all, so that the account is not locked by the device. The collection sends only read-only requests and does not change any setting on the device.

What the report contains and does not contain

  • Contains: the versions of the app and the system, the model identifier of the phone, the language setting, the selected connection method, the device address (the last part of a private network address is masked with x; for a public address only its class is given), the ports, the error code of the failed attempt, the detected brand and model, open ports, the headers and structure of the answers of the device (masked), the encoding and parameters of the stream, the difference in clock and time zone, and the steps that were run with their results.
  • Does not contain: the password, the username, the name given to the device, a public address or dynamic domain name, the hardware address of the network adapter, email addresses, tokens and other identifying data, pictures and video. Of a long serial number, only the last four characters are kept.
  • Masking is automatic, and each masked item leaves a marker. The report should still be reviewed before it is sent, and any item can be switched off.
Questions in the email

The body of the email contains several questions, among them the brand and model as printed on the label of the device, the firmware version, the kind of device, the difference between what was expected and what happened, whether the manufacturer's own app or a media player shows the device, and an RTSP address that opens in a media player (with the username, password and address removed first). Answering them helps the developer to assess the device.

Saved reports

Each report is saved on this device, and the five most recent are kept. An entry that shows the saved date, for the previous report, appears below the error message; tapping it opens the report again. A saved report shows its content as it was saved and cannot be switched item by item; to choose the content again, collect the details again.

To delete the saved reports:

  1. At the bottom of the report page, tap Delete saved reports.

    Check: The screen shows the dialog Delete all saved reports?, which explains that every device report saved on this device is removed and that a report that was already emailed is not affected.

  2. Tap Delete saved reports in the dialog.

    Check: All saved reports are deleted. The report on the screen is only shown there and is not saved again.

Finding devices with the network scan

Location: the Tools tab at the bottom of the screen.

When the IP address of a device is not known, the Tools tab can scan a network range. The scan probes the six ports 80, 554, 2020, 8000, 34567 and 37777 and lists the addresses that answer. Then it asks the devices it found who they are, over the discovery methods that many cameras and recorders answer without a sign-in. A device that answers this question but was not found by the port probe is added to the list.

  1. Tap the Tools tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: In the Subnet section, the This device row shows the current network address and mask, for example 192.168.1.10/24. The address field and Range are filled in with the current network.

  2. Optional: to scan a different network, enter the network in the address field, for example 192.168.1.0, and select the range in the Range menu.

    Check: Below the field, a line shows the network and the number of hosts that will be scanned, for example Will scan 192.168.1.0/24 · 254 hosts.

  3. Tap Scan.

    Check: The screen shows the progress Scanned 120 of 254, and the button changes to Stop.

  4. Wait until the scan ends; to end it early, tap Stop.

    Check: Found Devices lists the addresses that answered, with the open ports of each address as badges in the row. While the devices are asked who they are, Identifying devices… is shown; then each row that a device answered for shows its name or model, its brand and model, the number of channels of a recorder, and Not activated for a device that still has to be activated. When nothing was found, the screen shows No devices found yet.

  5. Tap a row in the results.

    Check: The screen opens the add-device form with the address already entered in the IP address or hostname field, and with whatever the device reported about itself; continue with the steps in “The Add Device form”.

  • Besides the address, the form takes over what the device reported: its name or model as the name, the port of its management service as HTTP Port, and the number of channels as Cameras for a brand from the list. For a device of the family with its own protocol whose port is not the default, that connection method and its Device Port are selected and Advanced is opened.
  • When the scan reported that the device is not activated, the form starts with a notice that it must be activated first; see “Activating a new device”.
  • Range runs from /26 (smallest) to /16 (largest). When a range holds more than 1,024 addresses, the scan samples them evenly instead of probing each one.
  • When the address field or the range differs from the current network, Use my subnet appears; tapping it restores the current network.
  • When the address field has an invalid format, the screen shows Enter a subnet like 192.168.1 or 192.168.1.0.
  • After the device has been added, the screen returns to the Tools tab, not to the device list.
Limits of the scan results

The scan finds only devices that answer on camera ports or to the discovery request. A device that does not identify itself can be a camera or a recorder; the type is confirmed when the device is added. Its open ports and any server name give a hint about the manufacturer.

When a scan has finished completely without any result, the screen shows If your cameras are on this network, check that Cam Hub is allowed to find devices on your local network in the system privacy settings. When the Local Network permission is denied, the scan shows no error; its result is empty as well. Check that the permission is turned on: Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › Cam Hub.

4The Devices tab and channels

The Devices tab lists every recorder and camera that has been added, together with YouTube and Twitch streams added as cameras. Opening a device shows its channels as live thumbnails. From there, channels are renamed, disabled, paused or shown in a full-screen wall, the user name and password of the device are changed, and the disks of supported devices are checked. The limits of the plan decide which channels can show a picture.

The device list

Path: Devices tab at the bottom of the screen.

Each row shows the name of the device, its model and its address. The icon on the left marks a recorder or a camera. On the right, a connection indicator sits above a label that names the type: Recorder or Camera. The indicator reports whether the device accepts a connection on its HTTP port. The check starts every time the row appears on the screen and waits for an answer for about 4 seconds.

IndicatorMeaning
Small spinning circleThe check is running.
Green Wi-Fi symbolThe device answered (Reachable).
Red, crossed-out Wi-Fi symbolThe device did not answer (Can't reach this device — check the network or firewall). The device may be switched off, on a different network, or blocked by a firewall.
Red play symbol or purple TV symbolA YouTube stream or a Twitch channel. These have no device to test; see “YouTube and Twitch streams”.
The indicator tests the HTTP port only

A device that does not accept connections on the stored HTTP port can show the red symbol while its video works, for example a camera that was added through a brand from the list. The sample cameras use the address demo, which is not a device on the network, and always show the red symbol.

The plus button at the top right opens a menu. Add Device adds a recorder or a camera; see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”. Where the services are offered, the menu also holds YouTube Live Stream and Twitch Channels, which add a live stream as a camera; see “Adding YouTube live streams and Twitch channels”.

Opening a device

  1. Tap the Devices tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the device list. When no device has been added, the screen shows No Devices, the text Add your first camera or recorder to get started. and the Add Device button; see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.

  2. Tap a row in the list.

    Check: The device page opens; see “The device page”.

Changing the order of the devices

  1. Tap Edit in the top-left corner. The button is shown only while at least one device exists.

    Check: A drag handle appears on the right of every row, and the button now reads Done.

  2. Touch the handle of a row and drag the row to its new position.

    Check: The row stays at the new position.

  3. Tap Done.

    Check: The list leaves edit mode. The order is stored. The device selection list in the Live tab uses the same order.

Deleting a device

Deleting removes the device from Cam Hub. The device itself is not changed.

  1. Swipe left on the row of the device.

    Check: A Delete button with a trash symbol appears on the right of the row. Even a full swipe only opens the confirmation; nothing is deleted without it.

  2. Tap Delete.

    Check: The dialog Delete this device? appears. It names the device and the number of its cameras and states that the action cannot be undone. When a password is saved for the device, it also states that the password is removed.

  3. Tap Delete in the dialog. Tap Cancel instead to keep the device.

    Check: The row disappears. The device, its channels, its saved password, its SNMP settings and its disk readings are removed from this iPhone or iPad. The device is also removed from the LiveView Mix wall, and from the choices of the Live tab and of Open on launch when it was selected there.

A deleted recorder no longer counts against the number of recorders that the plan allows; see “Plan limits and enabling channels”. To add the device again, see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.

The device page

The device page shows an information card at the top, the Disk Health row for devices that support it, and, under the heading Cameras, the channels of the device as thumbnails. The title is the name of the device. The thumbnails are arranged in as many columns as fit on the screen.

  • Information card: shows the name and the type of the device and the rows Model, IP address, Port (the HTTP port), Serial number, Firmware and Cameras (the number of channels). The serial number and the firmware appear only when the device reports them. For a YouTube or Twitch stream, the row Link replaces IP address and Port.
  • Disk Health: opens the disk report of the device; see “Disk Health”. An orange triangle or a red symbol on the right of the row repeats the worst disk verdict of the last reading.
  • Thumbnails: a recorder shows one thumbnail per channel; a standalone camera has one channel and shows one thumbnail. The lower-left corner of every thumbnail shows the number and the name of the channel. The thumbnails use SD or HD according to Settings › Default quality › Multiple cameras (SD unless changed). A change in Settings applies to this page at once; the page has no SD/HD button of its own.
  • Refresh: Cam Hub reads the channel list from the device when the page opens, at most once a minute for the same device, and every time the page is pulled down. Names and online states are updated, channels that the device has added appear, and channels that the device has removed disappear. A new channel is enabled only when the plan allows it; otherwise it is shown as Disabled. Names that were set in Cam Hub are kept. When the device does not answer, or returns a list that looks incomplete (no channel at all, or a single channel in place of several), the list stays as it was and no message is shown.
  • Refused sign-in: when the device refuses the saved user name or password during the refresh, the message Wrong username or password. and the button Edit Credentials appear above the thumbnails; see “Changing the user name and password of a device”.
  • No channels: when the device reports no channel, the page shows No cameras found. and the button Refresh, which reads the channel list again.

The three buttons at the top right are, from left to right: the black-bar button, Full Screen Wall and the pencil. For a device that signs in with a user name and password, the pencil (Edit Device) opens a menu with Rename and Edit Credentials. For the sample cameras and for YouTube and Twitch streams, the pencil is the Rename button itself.

iPhone Duo held like a book

When an iPhone Duo is half open with the fold running from top to bottom, the device page shows the thumbnails on one half and the page of one camera on the other. A tap on a thumbnail shows that camera on the other half instead of opening a new page; at first, the first camera that can show a picture is shown. See “The view on a folded iPhone Duo”.

Hiding or showing the details

  1. Tap the arrow on the right of the information card (Hide details).

    Check: The rows below the name disappear, and the arrow changes direction (Show details). Tapping it again shows the rows. The choice is stored for each device.

Renaming a device

  1. Tap the pencil button at the top right of the device page.

    Check: For a device that signs in with a user name and password, a menu with Rename and Edit Credentials opens. For other devices, the dialog of the next step opens at once.

  2. When the menu is shown, tap Rename.

    Check: The dialog Rename Device opens, with the text Give this device a name you'll recognize. and the current name in the Name field.

  3. Enter the new name in the Name field.

    Check: The field shows the new name.

  4. Tap Save.

    Check: The title of the page and the device list show the new name. An empty name is ignored and the old name stays. The name is stored in Cam Hub only; the device is not changed.

Changing the handling of black bars on this page

The black-bar button is the left one of the three buttons. Each tap selects the next of three modes; after the third mode the first one returns.

ModeEffect
DefaultThe whole picture is shown. Black bars appear where the shape of the picture differs from the shape of the thumbnail.
Enlarge to fillThe picture is enlarged in proportion until it fills the thumbnail. The edges of the picture are cut off.
Stretch to fillThe picture is stretched until it fills the thumbnail. The picture is distorted.

  1. Tap the left button of the three buttons at the top right.

    Check: All thumbnails change to the next mode, and the icon of the button changes to match the current mode.

The first mode comes from Settings › Picture › Black bars. A change made on this page applies to this page only and is not stored.

Changing the user name and password of a device

When the password of a device is changed on the device itself, for example by an installer or after a reset, Cam Hub can no longer sign in, and the thumbnails show Wrong username or password. Edit Credentials stores the new user name and password for the same device. The cameras, their names, the enabled and paused choices and the places on LiveView Mix walls stay as they are; deleting the device and adding it again would lose them.

Edit Credentials is offered for every device that signs in with a user name and password. It is not offered for the sample cameras or for YouTube and Twitch streams. The address and the ports of the device are not changed here.

  1. Open the device page of the device.

    Check: The device page is shown. When the last refresh was refused, the message Wrong username or password. and the button Edit Credentials appear above the thumbnails; that button opens the same screen as step 3.

  2. Tap the pencil button (Edit Device) at the top right.

    Check: A menu with Rename and Edit Credentials opens.

  3. Tap Edit Credentials.

    Check: The screen Edit Credentials opens. Its section is headed with the name of the device and holds Username, filled in with the current user name, and an empty Password field, where the cursor is. The note below the fields reads The new credentials are checked on the device before they are saved. Its cameras, their names and your LiveView Mix walls stay as they are.

  4. When the user name has changed as well, correct it in Username.

    Check: The field shows the user name. Save is unavailable while Username is empty.

  5. Enter the new password in Password.

    Check: The field shows one dot per character. An empty password is accepted, as when a device is added.

  6. Tap Save.

    Check: A spinner replaces Save while Cam Hub signs in to the device once with the new credentials and reads its channel list. When the device accepts them, the screen closes, the thumbnails connect again with the new credentials, and the channel list is refreshed. When it does not, the screen stays open, nothing is saved, and the reason appears in red, for example Wrong username or password. or Device unreachable. Check the address and your network.

Tap Cancel to close the screen without saving; a check that is still running is stopped and nothing is changed. The new user name must not be one that another saved device at the same address and port already uses; in that case the screen shows Another device at this address already uses that username.

One sign-in per device

Many recorders and NAS units lock the account, or the address of the iPhone or iPad, after a few failed sign-ins, and the lock also affects other apps. Cam Hub therefore checks new credentials with a single sign-in through the connection the device was added with, instead of trying several connection methods. For most devices, the thumbnails of a wall also sign in once for the whole device: when the device refuses, every thumbnail of that device shows the failure at once, and Cam Hub tries the same credentials again only after about a minute or when Cam Hub returns to the foreground. Saving new credentials starts over at once.

Disk Health

Disk Health reports the state of the disks of a recorder or a NAS: whether each disk is healthy, its temperature and the drive's own S.M.A.R.T. data, so that a failing disk can be replaced before recordings are lost. Cam Hub only reads this information; nothing on the device is changed.

The row Disk Health appears on the device page of devices that can report their disks: devices added with a brand connection that supports it (see Chapter 16, “Supported brands and connection methods”), and NAS units that share their disk health over SNMP. Devices added through ONVIF or with a stream address, YouTube and Twitch streams, and the sample cameras do not show the row.

Opening Disk Health

  1. Open the device page of the recorder or NAS.

    Check: The row Disk Health appears below the information card. An orange triangle on the right means that a disk needed attention at the last reading; a red symbol means that a disk was failing.

  2. Tap Disk Health.

    Check: The page Disk Health opens and reads the device. For a NAS without SNMP settings, the page shows This NAS shares its disk health over SNMP. Set it up once to see S.M.A.R.T. data, temperatures and the state of its volumes. and the button Set Up SNMP; see "Setting up SNMP on a NAS" below. When the device cannot be read, the page shows the reason and Try Again, and for a NAS also SNMP Settings.

  3. Pull the page down to read the device again.

    Check: The page shows the new reading. When the new reading fails, the previous one stays on the page, with the reason above it and the note Showing the last reading. Pull down to try again.

What the page shows

SectionContent
One section per disk, headed with its name and typeThe verdict (see the next table); Status, the state that the device reports for the disk, in the language of Cam Hub (for example Normal, Sleeping, Not installed or From another recorder; a word that Cam Hub does not know is shown as the device sends it); Capacity; Temperature; Powered on in days and years; one sentence per finding; counters that have risen since Cam Hub first read the disk; and S.M.A.R.T. details, which lists every attribute with its current value, its worst value and its limit (value · worst · limit), in red when it has failed. When a device does not report S.M.A.R.T. data for a disk, the section says so and shows the state of the disk only.
Volumes (NAS)Each volume or disk array with its state (for example Normal, Degraded or Crashed) and its free space.
DeviceSystem temperature (NAS), Uptime, failed parts that the device reports (power supply, fan), and the last restarts that Cam Hub noticed (The device restarted around Oct 14, 3:12 AM.), in orange when they happened within the last week.
Performance (NAS)CPU, Load (1 min) and Memory (used of total, with a bar).
Network (NAS)Each network port with its state and speed, the incoming and outgoing traffic, a warning when a connected port runs below 1000 Mbps or has counted 100 errors or more, and a chart of the traffic over the last few minutes.
Disk activity (NAS)Reading, writing and how busy each disk is, with a chart of the writing over the last few minutes.

While the page of a NAS is open, the sections Performance, Network and Disk activity are read again every 5 seconds; the speeds are averaged over about the last half minute.

Verdict of a diskMeaning
Healthy (green)Nothing to do. A drive powered on for 5 years or more is noted with a hint to plan a replacement.
Needs attention (orange)The drive has not failed, but something is worth acting on: an attribute within a few points of its limit, sectors that were remapped, wait to be remapped or cannot be read, data errors between the disk and the device, retries to spin up, a temperature of 55 °C (131 °F) or more, or a disk state other than normal, for example not formatted.
Failing (red)The device or the drive reports a failure: a disk state such as failed or error, a failed self-assessment or self-test, or an attribute at its limit.

The symbol on the Disk Health row of the device page shows the worst disk verdict of the last reading. The state of volumes and failed parts are shown on the page itself, in the sections Volumes and Device.

Temperatures are shown in the unit set for the iPhone or iPad in the iOS Settings app under General › Language & Region: Celsius or Fahrenheit, following the region unless changed there. The warning about a hot drive uses the same unit, for example Running warm at 133°F. Years above 131°F shorten a drive's life; check ventilation.

Setting up SNMP on a NAS

A NAS reports its disks over SNMP, a read-only service that answers anyone who knows its community name. First switch on SNMP in the management interface of the NAS: turn on the SNMP service, choose SNMPv1/v2c and set a community name. The iPhone or iPad must be able to reach the NAS on the SNMP port, usually in the same local network. A NAS set to SNMPv3 only is not supported. The note on the SNMP Settings screen names the menu of the NAS where SNMP is switched on.

  1. On the Disk Health page of the NAS, tap Set Up SNMP. Once settings exist, tap SNMP Settings (the gear at the top right) instead.

    Check: The screen SNMP Settings opens, with the fields Community (public on the first visit) and Port (161), and a note on where to switch SNMP on.

  2. Enter the community name that is set on the NAS in Community.

    Check: The field shows the community name.

  3. Change Port only when the NAS answers SNMP on a port other than 161.

    Check: The field shows the port.

  4. Tap Save.

    Check: The screen closes, and Disk Health reads the NAS. When a field is empty or the port is not between 1 and 65535, the screen stays open with Enter a community name and a port from 1 to 65535. When the NAS does not answer, the page says so, names the port it asked on, and asks to check that SNMP is switched on and that the community name matches; a blocked port has the same effect. A NAS does not answer a community name it does not know, so a wrong name looks the same as a NAS that cannot be reached.

When a NAS is added with Auto-detect and has no SNMP settings yet, the same screen opens right after the device has been added, as an optional step: Save stores the settings, and Not Now closes the screen. The device is added either way, and SNMP can be set up later from Disk Health; see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.

The SNMP settings are stored for each device in the Keychain of the iPhone or iPad and are deleted with the device. They are included in share codes and iCloud backups, so Disk Health works after an import or a restore without being set up again; see Chapter 10, “Sharing and backup”.

YouTube and Twitch streams

A YouTube live stream or a Twitch channel that was added as a camera (see “Adding YouTube live streams and Twitch channels”) appears in the device list as a camera with one channel. Its row shows the name, the model (YouTube Live or Twitch) and the short link, for example youtu.be/… or twitch.tv/…. In place of the connection indicator, the row shows a red play symbol for YouTube or a purple TV symbol for Twitch.

  • Device page: the information card shows Model, Link (the short link) and Cameras. There is no Disk Health row and no Edit Credentials; the pencil renames the stream.
  • Thumbnail: the service's own player shows the stream, without sound and without a name label over it. A tap opens the stream full screen; see “YouTube and Twitch streams”. The long-press menu offers Rename Camera and Disable or Enable.
  • Plan: these streams never count toward the plan and never show Not in your plan. Their channel can always be enabled.
  • Terms not yet agreed: a stream that reached this iPhone or iPad without the add form, for example through a share code or a backup, shows only its name and Agree to YouTube's terms to play this stream. or Agree to Twitch's terms to play this channel. A tap opens the full-screen view, where Review Terms… shows the terms with Agree and Continue. Once agreed, every stream of that service plays.
  • Not available: YouTube and Twitch are not available in some countries and regions. There, a stream on the list shows only its name and Not available in this region or language.
  • Deleting: swipe left on the row and confirm, as for any device; see “The device list”. The dialog does not mention a password, because none is saved.

What a thumbnail shows

The content of a thumbnail depends on the state of the channel. The table lists the states in the order in which Cam Hub decides between them. A tap opens the single-camera view only for an online channel that is enabled, within the plan and not paused; see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view”. A tap on a disabled or paused thumbnail offers to switch it back on. YouTube and Twitch thumbnails are described in “YouTube and Twitch streams”.

ThumbnailMeaningTapping the thumbnail
Grey, with a pause symbol and PausedThe video of the channel was paused by hand. The channel does not stream, and it keeps its place in the plan.A dialog with the name of the channel offers Resume Video and Cancel.
DisabledThe channel is disabled. It does not stream and does not use a place in the plan.A dialog with the name of the channel offers Enable and Cancel; see “Plan limits and enabling channels”.
Not in your plan with a lockThe channel is enabled, but the plan does not cover it.The plans screen opens; see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
Live pictureThe channel is enabled, within the plan, not paused, and the device reports a signal. A spinner shows while the connection is made.The single-camera view opens.
Failure message on a dark backgroundThe channel is in order, but the stream could not be opened. Cam Hub tries again by itself, with growing pauses between the attempts. After a refused user name or password, Cam Hub tries at most once more and then stops, so that the device does not lock the account; the message stays until the page is opened again or Cam Hub returns to the foreground.The single-camera view opens.
Grey, with a crossed-out camera and No signalThe device reports that the channel has no signal.Nothing happens.

Not every device reports a missing signal for each channel. For channels of such devices, a stream that cannot be opened shows a failure message instead of No signal.

Hide offline cameras affects the walls only

The setting Hide offline cameras removes cameras without a signal from the live walls. The device page always lists every channel and shows the ones without a signal in grey. LiveView Mix walls are not affected by the setting.

Channel options (long press)

A long press on a thumbnail opens a menu with the options below.

Menu itemEffectUses a place in the plan
Open in New WindowOffered on iPad and on the inner display of iPhone Duo. Opens the camera in a window of its own; see “A camera in a window of its own”.None.
Rename CameraSets a name of your own for the channel.None.
Your plan › Disable or EnableOnly the item that matches the current state is offered. A disabled channel does not stream and shows Disabled.A disabled channel releases its place.
Bandwidth › Pause Video or Resume VideoOffered for channels of a recorder only. A paused channel stops streaming, which saves bandwidth, and shows Paused.A paused channel keeps its place.

Renaming a channel

  1. Long press the thumbnail of the channel.

    Check: The menu of the channel opens.

  2. Tap Rename Camera.

    Check: A dialog opens with the current name in the Name field and the buttons Cancel, Use Device Name and Save.

  3. Enter the new name and tap Save.

    Check: The lower-left corner of the thumbnail shows the new name. The same name is used on the Live tab, on LiveView Mix walls and as the title of the single-camera view.

  4. To return to the name that the device reports, repeat the first two steps and tap Use Device Name.

    Check: The thumbnail shows the name of the device again.

A name set in Cam Hub is not overwritten when the channel list is refreshed, and it is included in backups; see Chapter 10, “Sharing and backup”.

Pausing and resuming the video of a recorder channel

  1. Long press the thumbnail of a channel of a recorder.

    Check: The menu shows the section Bandwidth.

  2. Tap Pause Video.

    Check: The thumbnail turns grey and shows Paused. Every screen that shows this channel treats it as paused.

  3. To resume, tap the paused thumbnail and then Resume Video.

    Check: The live picture returns. Resume Video is also in the long-press menu.

Plan limits and enabling channels

A channel is either enabled or disabled. An enabled channel uses one place of the plan. Only enabled channels within the limits of the plan show a picture; an enabled channel beyond the limits shows Not in your plan. The limits are listed below; the plans themselves are described in Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

PlanStandalone camerasChannels of recordersRecorders that can be added
FreeAt most 2 enabled channels in total, counting cameras and recorder channels together. Enabled recorder channels must all belong to the same recorder.1
Camera planEnabled cameras up to the limit of the plan: 8, 16 or unlimited.As on the free plan: 2 enabled channels, all on one recorder.1
NVR planAs on the free plan: 2 enabled cameras.Every channel of the recorders that the plan covers.2, 4 or unlimited
  • Both plans can be held together. The two limits apply independently: the camera plan raises the limit for standalone cameras, and the NVR plan raises the number of recorders whose channels are all usable.
  • Each control panel on a LiveView Mix page that is shown counts as one camera against the camera limit. Real cameras keep their picture first; panels beyond the limit show Not in your plan. See Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”.
  • A recorder counts toward the number of recorders as soon as it has been added, whether or not any of its channels is enabled. The sample cameras count like real devices.
  • YouTube and Twitch streams are not counted and are never locked; see “YouTube and Twitch streams”.
  • When a plan ends or its limits fall below the number of enabled channels, the stored choices are kept. The channels beyond the limits show Not in your plan: standalone cameras keep their picture first, then recorder channels, each in the order in which the devices were added and in the order of the channel numbers.
  • When both limits are unlimited, every channel is enabled automatically, and the page Choose which cameras to show is not offered.

Enabling a disabled channel

Prerequisite: the thumbnail of the channel shows Disabled.

  1. Long press the thumbnail of the disabled channel.

    Check: The menu shows Enable below Your plan. A tap on the disabled thumbnail offers Enable as well.

  2. Tap Enable.

    Check: When the plan has a free place, the thumbnail starts to show the live picture; the procedure ends here. When the limit has been reached, the plans screen opens with a message and the channel stays disabled. For a standalone camera the message is You've reached the Free plan's limit of 2 enabled cameras. on the free plan, or, on a camera plan, You've reached your plan's limit of 8 enabled cameras. with the number of the plan. For a recorder channel it is Unlock every channel with an NVR plan.

  3. Close the plans screen.

    Check: The device page is shown again.

  4. Long press the thumbnail of an enabled channel that is not needed and tap Disable.

    Check: The thumbnail shows Disabled, and its place in the plan is free.

  5. Repeat the first two steps for the channel that should be shown.

    Check: The thumbnail shows the live picture.

Choosing which cameras show

Path: Settings › Choose which cameras to show

This page lists the channels of all devices in one place, so that the places of the plan can be assigned across devices without opening each device page. The item is offered only while at least one of the two limits of the plan applies.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings.

  2. In the Subscription section, tap Choose which cameras to show.

    Check: The page Choose which cameras to show opens. The section Your plan shows the rows Cameras (for example 2 cameras or Unlimited) and Recorders, and the note Turn on the cameras you want to watch. The Free plan shows 2 cameras on a single recorder. Below it, one section per device lists every channel with its number, its name and a switch.

  3. Turn off the switch of a channel that is not needed.

    Check: The switch is off. The channel is disabled and its place in the plan is free. Turning a switch off is always possible.

  4. Turn on the switch of the channel that should be shown.

    Check: The switch is on when the plan has a free place. When it has not, the plans screen opens with a message and the switch stays off. On the free plan, the message On the Free plan, the cameras you show must all be on one recorder. appears when a channel of a second recorder is turned on.

  5. Tap the back button in the top-left corner to leave the page.

    Check: The choices apply everywhere: walls and the device pages show a picture for the enabled channels within the plan only.

When no device has been added, the page shows No Devices, Add a device first, then choose its cameras here. and the Add Device button.

The full-screen wall of a device

The full-screen wall shows all enabled channels of one device edge to edge. It opens from the device page and from the Live tab (see “The Full Screen Wall”), and it follows the way in which the iPhone is held: upright, the thumbnails keep their 16:9 shape and are stacked in rows of one or two (see the Layout button below); sideways, two rows fill the height. A device with only one enabled channel shows that camera over the whole screen.

  1. Tap the Full Screen Wall button (second of the three buttons) at the top right of the device page.

    Check: The wall covers the screen. It shows the enabled channels of the device; channels beyond the plan show Not in your plan. When no channel is enabled, the screen shows No Enabled Cameras and Enable cameras on the device page.

  2. When more channels exist than fit on the screen, scroll the wall vertically in upright orientation, or swipe sideways in landscape orientation.

    Check: The next channels or the next page appear. When the wall is divided into pages, dots at the bottom show the current page.

  3. Tap a thumbnail that shows a picture.

    Check: A close-up of that camera opens over the wall, with Back and the camera name at the top.

  4. Tap Back at the top left of the close-up.

    Check: The wall is shown again.

  5. Tap Close (the cross at the top left of the wall).

    Check: The screen returns to the device page or to the Live tab.

Button at the top of the wallFunction
Close (top left)Closes the wall.
SD or HDSwitches all cameras of the wall at once (Switch all cameras to HD or Switch all cameras to SD). The text on the button is the current quality. The wall starts with the quality of Settings › Default quality › Multiple cameras. The change is not stored.
LayoutSwitches between one and two thumbnails per row. This choice is stored.
Black-bar buttonCycles through Default, Enlarge to fill and Stretch to fill, as on the device page. The change is not stored.
  • Close-up: the picture uses the quality of Settings › Default quality › Single camera (HD unless changed), and the buttons of the wall are not shown. Spread two fingers to enlarge the picture up to 5 times, drag to move it while it is enlarged, and double-tap to switch between normal size and 2 times.
  • Speaker (lower left): appears when the camera sends sound; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
  • Camera control (lower right): appears when the camera can be moved or zoomed; see “PTZ control: moving the camera”.
  • Recordings (top right): appears for devices that support playback. It opens the single-camera view of the camera over the wall, with Done in the top-right corner to return; see Chapter 7, “Recording playback and speed”.
  • The setting Edge-to-edge video and the setting Hide offline cameras apply to the wall. A tap on a thumbnail with Not in your plan opens the plans screen.
  • For a YouTube or Twitch stream, the wall shows no SD/HD button and no black-bar button, because the service's player decides both.

SD and HD on device screens

SD is the lighter picture and HD the sharper one. Which of the two is used depends on the screen. The starting values come from Default quality in the settings.

ScreenStarting qualitySwitching on the screen
Thumbnails on the device pageMultiple cameras (SD unless changed); follows the setting at once.None.
Full-screen wallMultiple cameras.The SD/HD button switches all cameras. The change is not stored.
Live tabMultiple cameras.The SD/HD button in the top bar switches all cameras; see “SD and HD on a wall”.
Close-up in the full-screen wallSingle camera (HD unless changed).None.
Single-camera viewSingle camera.The SD/HD switch below the picture, when the device offers two streams. The change is not stored; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
LiveView Mix wallEach camera slot has its own choice, SD unless changed, set while the wall is arranged. The close-up of a camera on the wall always uses HD.See Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”.
Recording playbackThe recorded stream is played. There is no choice between SD and HD.None.

Some devices provide only one stream for a channel. For those, SD and HD show the same picture, and the SD/HD switch of the single-camera view is not shown. YouTube and Twitch streams have no SD/HD choice: the service's player chooses the quality from the size of the picture.

5The Live tab and the Full Screen Wall

The Live tab shows the enabled channels of one device as a wall of live pictures. On this tab the quality of the wall is switched, single cameras are opened, and the wall is extended to the Full Screen Wall. Cameras without a signal can be hidden from both walls. YouTube and Twitch streams appear on the walls like cameras.

The Live tab

Path: Live tab at the bottom of the screen.

The tab shows one device at a time: a recorder with all of its enabled channels, or one standalone camera. The title of the screen is the name of that device. To show cameras of different devices on one wall, use LiveView Mix; see Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”.

  • Enabled channels only: channels that are disabled never appear on this tab. They are enabled on the device page; see “Channel options (long press)”.
  • Silent tiles: the tiles of a wall play no sound, YouTube and Twitch tiles included. Sound is available in the single-camera view and in the full-screen viewer of a stream; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
  • YouTube and Twitch: a stream that was added as a device is shown as one tile with the player of the service. A tap on the tile opens the stream full screen; see “YouTube and Twitch streams”.
  • No refresh on this tab: the channel list of a device is read from the device when its device page opens; see “The device page”.
  • Leaving the app: when the app leaves the foreground, all streams stop. When the app returns, the tiles connect again.

Opening the Live tab

  1. Tap the Live tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the live pictures of the enabled channels of one device. The title is the name of the device. As long as no other device has been selected, the first device of the Devices tab is shown.

ControlPositionFunction
List button (Select Device)Top leftOpens the list of devices, in the order of the Devices tab. The device on the wall is marked.
SD or HDTop right, firstSwitches the quality of the whole wall at once (Switch all cameras to HD or Switch all cameras to SD). The text on the button is the current quality. See “SD and HD on a wall”. Not shown for a YouTube or Twitch stream.
Black-bar buttonTop right, secondCycles through Default, Enlarge to fill and Stretch to fill, as on the device page; see “The device page”. The change applies to this wall only and is not stored. Not shown for a YouTube or Twitch stream.
Full Screen WallTop right, thirdOpens the Full Screen Wall; see “The Full Screen Wall”.

While no device has been added, the SD/HD button and the Full Screen Wall button are unavailable. The black-bar button starts with the mode of Settings › Picture › Black bars. The Live tab reads that mode when the app starts, so a change in Settings reaches the Live tab at the next start of the app.

Showing another device

  1. Tap the list button (Select Device) in the top-left corner.

    Check: A menu lists all devices in the order of the Devices tab. The device that is shown is marked.

  2. Tap the name of the device.

    Check: The wall shows the enabled channels of the selected device, and the title changes to its name. The choice is stored and is still valid after the app has been closed.

The device for the Live tab can also be chosen in Open on launch; see “LiveView Mix in Settings”. When the selected device is deleted, the wall shows the first device of the list.

How the wall is arranged

ScreenPictures side by side
iPhone held upright1
iPhone held sideways2
iPad, in both orientations2

The tiles keep the 16:9 shape. When they do not fit on the screen, the wall scrolls vertically; the Live tab has no pages. The lower-left corner of each tile shows the number and the name of the channel. A device with only one enabled channel shows that camera over the whole area. Turning the device re-arranges the wall at once.

What a tile shows

TileMeaningTapping the tile
Live picture (a spinner while the connection is made)The channel is enabled, within the plan and online.Opens the single-camera view.
Failure message on a dark backgroundThe stream could not be opened. Cam Hub tries again by itself at growing intervals. After a refused sign-in, an unsupported device or too many requests, it does not; the message then stays until the app returns to the foreground or the wall is opened again.Opens the single-camera view.

Not in your plan with a lockThe channel is enabled, but the plan does not cover it; see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.Opens the plans screen.
