Opening a camera

  1. Tap a tile that shows a live picture.

    Check: The single-camera view opens with the name of the camera as its title; see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view”. The back button returns to the Live tab. A tile of a YouTube or Twitch stream opens the stream full screen instead.

  2. Tap a tile that shows Not in your plan.

    Check: The plans screen opens with a message at the top: Unlock every channel with an NVR plan. for a channel of a recorder, and You've reached the Free plan's limit of 2 enabled cameras. for a standalone camera on the Free plan. Close the screen with Done.

When the tab is empty

  • No device has been added: the screen shows No Devices and Add a device in the Devices tab first. See Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.
  • The device has no enabled channel, or every channel is hidden by Hide offline cameras: the screen shows No enabled cameras and Enable cameras on the device page. See “Choosing which cameras show”.

SD and HD on a wall

SD is the lighter picture and HD the sharper one. The button at the top of the Live tab and the button on the Full Screen Wall switch all cameras of the wall together.

  1. Tap the quality button at the top right of the Live tab (SD or HD).

    Check: The text on the button changes to the other quality, and the tiles connect again with the new quality.

  2. Tap the button again.

    Check: The wall returns to the first quality.

  • Starting quality: Settings › Default quality › Multiple cameras (SD unless changed). A change in Settings reaches the Live tab at once, until the button has been tapped on the Live tab; from then on the wall keeps that choice until the app is closed. The Full Screen Wall starts with the setting every time it opens.
  • Not stored: a quality chosen with the button is never saved.
  • One stream per channel: some devices provide only one stream for a channel. For those, SD and HD show the same picture.
  • Close-up: the close-up of a camera in the Full Screen Wall uses Single camera and has no switch; see “The full-screen wall of a device”.
  • For the quality on all other screens, see “SD and HD on device screens”; for the settings, see “Default quality”.

The Full Screen Wall

The Full Screen Wall shows all enabled channels of the device edge to edge on a black background. The status bar is hidden, and the picture reaches the edges of the screen as set by Edge-to-edge video; see “Picture: black bars and edge-to-edge”. The wall opens from the Live tab and from the device page; for the device page, see “The full-screen wall of a device”.

Opening the wall

  1. Tap the Full Screen Wall button (diagonal arrows) at the top right of the Live tab.

    Check: The wall covers the screen. At the top, the close button is on the left and the buttons for the quality, the layout and the black bars are on the right. The buttons are round or capsule-shaped with a white ring, so that they stay visible on any picture. For a YouTube or Twitch stream, only the close button and the layout button are shown. When the device has no enabled channel, the screen shows No enabled cameras.

How the wall is arranged

ScreenArrangementMoving through the cameras
Held uprightThe tiles keep the 16:9 shape and are stacked in rows of two, or in rows of one after a tap on Layout.Scroll vertically. There are no pages and no dots.
Held sidewaysThe tiles are stretched so that the rows fill the height of the screen. On an iPhone with two tiles per row, a page holds four cameras; with one tile per row, one camera.Swipe sideways between pages. When there is more than one page, dots at the bottom show the current page.
One enabled channelThe camera fills the whole screen.None.

The same rule applies to an iPad: it follows the shape of the screen. Turning the device while the wall is open re-arranges the wall at once.

  1. Turn the iPhone sideways. Prerequisite: the rotation lock is off, and the device has more than four enabled channels.

    Check: The tiles fill the height of the screen, and the wall divides into pages. Dots at the bottom of the screen show the number of pages.

  2. Swipe to the left, then to the right.

    Check: The next page is shown, and then the previous page. The dots follow.

The buttons of the wall

ButtonFunctionStored
Close (top left)Closes the wall.No.
SD or HDSwitches the quality of all cameras at once; see “SD and HD on a wall”. Not shown for a YouTube or Twitch stream.No. The wall starts with Multiple cameras.
LayoutSwitches between two tiles per row (the starting value) and one tile per row. The symbol shows the arrangement that the next tap selects.Yes. The Full Screen Wall of the device page uses the same choice.

Changing the number of tiles per row

  1. Tap Layout at the top right of the wall.

    Check: The tiles are arranged one per row or two per row, and the symbol of the button changes. The next time the wall opens, it uses the same arrangement.

Opening a camera and closing the wall

  1. Tap a tile that shows a live picture.

    Check: A close-up of the camera opens over the wall, with Back and the name of the camera at the top. Its zoom, speaker, camera control and recordings are described in “The full-screen wall of a device”. The other cameras of the wall pause while the close-up is open. A tile with Not in your plan opens the plans screen, a tile with No signal does nothing, and a tile of a YouTube or Twitch stream opens the stream full screen (see “YouTube and Twitch streams”).

  2. Tap Close (the cross at the top left of the wall).

    Check: The Live tab is shown again.

Hiding cameras without signal

The setting Hide offline cameras removes cameras without a signal from the Live tab and from the Full Screen Wall. It is off by default. The device page still lists every channel and shows the channels without a signal in grey; see “What a thumbnail shows”. LiveView Mix walls are not affected: a slot without a signal keeps a plate with No signal.

  1. Tap the Settings tab, then scroll to Hide offline cameras. The row is in its own section below Picture.

    Check: The switch is off. The text below the row reads Cameras with no signal are hidden from the live walls. The device page still lists them, grayed out.

  2. Turn on Hide offline cameras.

    Check: The switch is on. All cameras are checked again.

  3. Tap the Live tab.

    Check: Cameras without a signal no longer appear on the wall. When no camera of the device remains, the screen shows No enabled cameras.

  • Which cameras are hidden: channels that the device reports as having no signal, and cameras whose stream could not be opened twice in a row. Cam Hub tries once more before a camera is hidden.
  • When a hidden camera returns: a hidden camera is not tried again until the app returns to the foreground, or until the switch is turned off and on again. The camera is then tried once more: it stays on the wall when it shows a picture, and it is hidden again when it fails again. A channel that the device reports as having no signal returns when the device reports a signal again; the report is updated when the device page reads the channel list.
  • Where it applies: to the Live tab and to the Full Screen Wall, including the Full Screen Wall of the device page. The setting is part of the backup of the app settings and is reset by Restore Default Settings; see “Reset: defaults, delete all data, delete iCloud backup”.

6Single-camera view

The single-camera view shows one camera at full width, live or from recordings. It offers zoom and pan, a snapshot, sound, two-way talk for cameras that support it, the choice between SD and HD and, for cameras with a movable head, PTZ control. For devices that support playback, the view also holds the recording timeline; see Chapter 7, “Recording playback and speed”. On an iPad and on iPhone Duo, a camera can have a window of its own. YouTube and Twitch streams open in a full-screen viewer of their own.

Opening the view

The view opens from four places:

  • the Devices tab: a thumbnail on the device page (see “The device page”);
  • the Live tab: a thumbnail on the wall (see “The Live tab”);
  • the close-up of a camera on a full-screen wall or on a LiveView Mix wall: the Recordings button, shown for devices that support playback (see “The full-screen wall of a device”). The view then opens over the wall, and Done at the top right returns to the close-up;
  • a window of its own on an iPad or on the inner display of iPhone Duo (see “A camera in a window of its own”).

Prerequisite: the channel is enabled, within the plan and online. On the device page, a tap on a paused or disabled thumbnail offers Resume Video or Enable instead of opening the view; see “What a thumbnail shows”. The thumbnail of a YouTube or Twitch stream opens the stream full screen instead; see “YouTube and Twitch streams”.

  1. Tap the Devices tab, then tap the device.

    Check: The device page shows the thumbnails of the channels.

  2. Tap the thumbnail of a channel that shows a live picture.

    Check: The single-camera view opens. The title is the name of the camera, and the green badge LIVE is shown at the top left of the picture. The picture starts with the quality of Settings › Default quality › Single camera (HD unless changed).

Tap the back button in the top-left corner to leave the view.

The parts of the screen

PartContent
Navigation barThe back button and the name of the camera. On an iPad and on the inner display of iPhone Duo, the Open in New Window button is at the right; see “A camera in a window of its own”.
Picture (upright, 16:9)The badge at the top left names the mode: LIVE (green) or PLAYBACK 15:00:03, with the playback time (red). The round button at the lower right is the camera control for PTZ in live mode; see “PTZ control: moving the camera”. While a recording plays, it is the speed button; see “Playback speed”.
Controls barSnapshot at the left; next to it the speaker button when the camera sends sound, and the talk button for a camera that can be talked through; at the right the SD/HD switch in live mode or Back to Live during playback. See “Snapshot, sound and quality” and “Two-way talk”.
Recording panelThe heading Recordings with the day, the timeline and the list of recordings, and on supported devices the button for the recording calendar. The panel appears only for devices that support playback; for all other devices, the view consists of the picture and the controls bar. See Chapter 7, “Recording playback and speed”.

While a picture is shown, the screen of the iPhone or iPad does not dim.

Zoom and pan

The picture can be enlarged on the screen. This is a digital enlargement of the picture and works in live mode and during playback. It does not move the lens of the camera; for that, see “PTZ control: moving the camera”.

GestureEffect
Spread two fingers apart on the pictureEnlarges the picture up to 6 times. Moving the fingers together reduces it again; below normal size, the picture returns to normal size.
Drag one finger while the picture is enlargedMoves the picture. The edge of the picture never leaves a gap.
Double-tap the pictureEnlarges the picture to 2.5 times. When the picture is already enlarged, it returns to normal size.

  1. Spread two fingers apart on the picture.

    Check: The picture is enlarged. The badge at the top left keeps its place.

  2. Drag one finger across the picture.

    Check: The picture moves in the direction of the finger.

  3. Double-tap the picture.

    Check: The picture returns to normal size.

While aiming by touch is on, a drag on the picture draws a box for the camera instead of moving the enlarged picture; see “PTZ control: moving the camera”.

Snapshot, sound and quality

Taking a snapshot

  1. Tap Snapshot at the left of the controls bar.

    Check: The sheet Snapshot slides up. It shows a progress indicator and then the picture.

  2. Tap Share.

    Check: The sharing sheet of the system opens. From there, the picture can be saved, copied or sent with the actions that the system offers.

  3. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The sheet closes.

  • The snapshot is a current picture that Cam Hub requests from the device. It is taken from the live picture of the device also while a recording plays, and it is not a frame of the recording.
  • When the device does not supply a snapshot, the sheet closes again and the message Couldn't take a snapshot. Check the connection to the camera and try again. appears. Tap OK to close it. Some devices cannot supply a snapshot at all, for example a device that was added through a brand from the list.

Switching the sound on and off

The speaker button appears only when the camera sends sound in a format that Cam Hub can play. A camera without sound, or with an unsupported sound format, has no button.

  1. Tap the speaker button next to Snapshot (Unmute).

    Check: The symbol changes from a crossed-out speaker to a speaker with sound waves, and the sound of the camera plays.

  2. Tap the speaker button again (Mute).

    Check: The symbol shows the crossed-out speaker again, and the sound stops.

  • The speaker plays the sound of the camera. To speak through the camera, see “Two-way talk”.
  • The sound plays even when the ring/silent switch of the iPhone is set to silent.
  • The choice is one switch for the whole app. It is remembered and is off at first. Thumbnails and walls never play sound; only the single-camera view, the close-up of a camera and the full-screen viewer of a YouTube or Twitch stream do (see “YouTube and Twitch streams”).
  • While camera sound plays, other audio on the iPhone is lowered. Sound stops when the app leaves the foreground.
  • During playback, sound plays at normal speed only; see “Playback speed”.

Switching between SD and HD

  1. Tap SD or HD in the switch at the right of the controls bar.

    Check: The stream restarts, Connecting… shows briefly, and the picture continues with the selected quality. The change is not stored.

The switch is shown only in live mode and only when the device offers two streams for the camera. During playback, Back to Live takes its place. The starting quality comes from Settings › Default quality › Single camera. HD is sharper and uses more bandwidth and more resources of the iPhone. For devices that provide one stream per channel, SD and HD are the same picture. The rules for all screens are in “SD and HD on device screens”.

Two-way talk

A standalone camera with a speaker can be talked through. Talk works like a walkie-talkie: hold the button to speak, release it to listen. Cam Hub asks the camera for its talk channel when the view opens; the talk button (a microphone symbol) appears to the right of the speaker button when the camera reports one.

Prerequisites: a standalone camera of a supported brand that reports a two-way audio channel, live mode, and a channel within the plan. Channels of a recorder have no talk button: the talk channel of a recorder is the recorder's own audio output, not the speaker of the camera.

The first time the talk button is pressed, a dialog of the system asks for access to the microphone. Allow it, then press the button again.

  1. Press and hold the talk button (Talk) in the controls bar.

    Check: The button shows a spinner while the talk channel of the camera opens, then turns red with a sound-wave symbol. While the button is held, the voice comes out of the speaker of the camera, and the sound of the camera pauses.

  2. Release the button.

    Check: The button shows the microphone symbol again, the microphone stops, and the sound of the camera can be heard again when the speaker is on.

  • Microphone: the microphone is used only while the button is held. After a release, the talk channel of the camera stays open for about 15 seconds, so that the next press talks at once.
  • End of talk: talk ends when the view is left, when the app leaves the foreground and when playback starts. During playback, the talk button is hidden.
  • Landscape: in landscape, the talk button sits at the top right of the picture, next to the speaker button; see “Black bars, rotation and landscape”.
  • VoiceOver: a double tap on the button starts talking, and a second double tap stops it.
Message at the top of the pictureMeaning and action
Microphone access is off for Cam Hub. Turn it on in Settings to talk through the camera.Access to the microphone was refused. Allow it for Cam Hub in the Settings app of the iPhone or iPad.
The microphone could not be started. Another app may be using it.Another app uses the microphone, for example during a call. End the other use and try again.
Could not start talking to the camera., or a message that names the cause, for example Wrong username or password.The talk channel of the camera did not open. Check the connection and the account; see “When adding fails: the checklist”.
The camera stopped taking sound.The camera closed the talk channel. Press the button again.
A message that names the sound format of the talk channelThe talk channel of the camera uses a format other than G.711. Set the talk channel to G.711 in the audio settings of the camera.

Black bars, rotation and landscape

  • Black bars: the picture follows Settings › Picture › Black bars (Default, Enlarge to fill or Stretch to fill; see “The device page”). The single-camera view has no switch of its own; a change in Settings applies to this view as well.
  • Edge-to-edge video: in landscape, the picture extends into the area of the Dynamic Island and the rounded corners when Settings › Picture › Edge-to-edge video is on. When the setting is off, the picture stays clear of them, with black bars.
  • iPad: the layout does not change with the orientation. The view keeps the arrangement of the upright iPhone in both orientations, and the picture-only landscape layout below is not used.

Watching in landscape on an iPhone

Prerequisite: the rotation lock of the iPhone is off.

  1. Turn the iPhone sideways.

    Check: The picture fills the whole screen. The navigation bar, the tab bar, the status bar, the controls bar and the recording panel are hidden. The back button and the other buttons of the picture show for about 5 seconds and then fade out.

  2. Tap the picture once.

    Check: The back button appears at the top left, with the badge next to it. At the top right appear the speaker button when the camera sends sound and the talk button when the camera can be talked through. The camera control button is at the lower right when the camera can be moved. The buttons fade out again after about 5 seconds; another tap on the picture shows them again.

  3. Tap the back button at the top left, or turn the iPhone upright again.

    Check: The view leaves the landscape layout or closes. The back button returns to the page from which the view was opened.

Zoom, pan and PTZ control work in landscape as in upright orientation. Snapshot, the SD/HD switch, the day and the list of recordings are available in upright orientation only. For the strip that appears in landscape during playback, see “Playback in landscape”.

PTZ control: moving the camera

Prerequisites: a camera with a movable head (pan, tilt or zoom), a device that supports PTZ control, an account that may control PTZ on the device, and live mode. During playback, the camera control is hidden.

Cam Hub asks the device for the abilities of the channel when the view opens. The round button at the lower right of the picture appears when the answer arrives, which can take a moment. A camera that cannot move shows no button. Only the controls that the device reports are shown.

  1. Tap the round button at the lower right of the picture (Move camera).

    Check: The pad opens to the left of the button, and the button shows a cross (Hide camera controls). The pad holds a capsule with plus and minus for zoom, a disc with four arrows and a house symbol in the middle, and a star button. For a camera that supports aiming by touch, an aim button with a target symbol is added next to the disc, above the star.

  2. Press and hold an arrow of the disc (Tilt up, Tilt down, Pan left or Pan right).

    Check: The camera turns in that direction for as long as the finger stays on the arrow, and the picture follows. The camera stops when the finger is lifted.

  3. Press and hold plus or minus on the capsule (Zoom in or Zoom out).

    Check: The lens of the camera zooms in or out for as long as the finger stays, and stops when the finger is lifted.

  4. Tap the house symbol (Home position).

    Check: The camera moves to its home position.

  5. Tap the star button (Saved positions).

    Check: The star shows a spinner while the positions are read from the camera. Then a dialog lists the names of the positions that are stored in the camera. When the camera has none, the dialog shows This camera has no saved positions. When the positions cannot be read, it shows Could not load the saved positions. Please try again.

  6. Tap the name of a position.

    Check: The camera moves to that position, and the list closes. Tap outside the list to close it without moving the camera.

  7. Tap the cross button (Hide camera controls).

    Check: The pad closes, and a movement that is still running stops.

ControlShown when the device reports
Direction disc with four arrowsThe head can pan or tilt. The house symbol sits in the middle of the disc.
Capsule with plus and minusThe head can zoom.
Star buttonThe camera has saved positions.
Aim button with a target symbol (3D positioning)The head can be aimed at a point or an area of the picture. Shown in the single-camera view only.
House symbol next to the starThe head can go to its home position but cannot pan or tilt; the disc is not shown then.

Aiming by touching the picture

On cameras that support it, the camera can be turned toward a spot of the picture, or zoomed straight into an area drawn on the picture. Prerequisite: the pad is open and shows the aim button.

  1. Tap the aim button (3D positioning).

    Check: The aim button turns white, and the pad shrinks to this button so that it does not cover the picture. The hint Tap to center here. Drag a box to zoom in on it; drag up and to the left to zoom out. appears at the top of the picture.

  2. Tap a spot on the picture.

    Check: A ring marks the spot briefly, and the camera turns so that the spot moves to the middle of the picture.

  3. Drag a box over an area, from its top-left corner to its bottom-right corner.

    Check: A dashed box with a plus magnifier follows the finger. When the finger is lifted, the camera turns to the area and zooms in on it.

  4. Drag a box from the bottom right up to the top left.

    Check: The box shows a minus magnifier. When the finger is lifted, the camera zooms out.

  5. Tap the aim button again.

    Check: The full pad returns, and a drag on the picture moves the enlarged picture again.

  • The touch is measured on the picture itself: black bars, the black-bar mode and the digital enlargement of the view are taken into account. A tap on a black bar sends nothing.
  • When the camera refuses the new position, the hint is replaced for a few seconds by The camera did not take the new position.
  • Closing the pad with the cross button also ends aiming, as does the start of playback.
  • The close-ups on full-screen walls and LiveView Mix walls have the same pad without the aim button.

Notes on PTZ control

  • Speed: the app has no speed setting. A button moves the camera at one fixed speed, the highest that the app requests, for as long as it is held; a short tap makes a short movement.
  • Refused movements: when the device refuses a movement of the pad, no message is shown.
  • Saved positions: Cam Hub recalls positions that exist on the camera. Positions are created and changed on the device itself, not in Cam Hub.
  • Stopping: a movement stops when the finger is lifted, when the view is left, when the app leaves the foreground, when the pad is closed and when playback starts. The same pad is available in the close-up of a camera on full-screen walls and on LiveView Mix walls.

A camera in a window of its own

On an iPad and on the inner display of iPhone Duo, Cam Hub can show several windows. A camera can then be opened in a window of its own, for example to keep the wall in one window and a camera with its recordings and PTZ pad in another, or to place the camera next to another app. On other iPhones, the command is not shown.

  1. On the device page, touch and hold the thumbnail of a camera.

    Check: A menu opens with Open in New Window at the top.

  2. Tap Open in New Window.

    Check: A new window opens with the single-camera view of that camera.

In the single-camera view itself, the Open in New Window button at the right of the navigation bar does the same.

  • Each window is a viewer of its own, with its own timeline and playback. Two windows of the same camera share the live picture of the device.
  • The window is closed with the window controls of the system.
  • When the camera has been deleted, the window shows an empty black page.

The view on a folded iPhone Duo

On iPhone Duo, the single-camera view follows the fold of the inner display. Opened flat, the view looks as on any other iPhone. For the folding positions, see “iPhone Duo”.

Half folded, standing

Prerequisite: the iPhone Duo is held sideways and half folded, so that the fold runs from left to right across the screen, for example when it stands on a table like a small laptop.

  1. Open the single-camera view and fold the iPhone Duo halfway.

    Check: The picture fills the upper half. The controls bar, the recording panel and the PTZ pad are on the lower half, within reach and clear of the fold. The navigation bar, the tab bar and the status bar are hidden; the back button, the badge, the speaker button and the talk button float over the picture as in landscape and fade out after about 5 seconds. A tap on the picture shows them again.

  2. Open the iPhone Duo flat again.

    Check: The usual layout returns.

Held like a book

Prerequisite: a camera of a device that supports playback, and the iPhone Duo held upright and half open, so that the fold runs from top to bottom. For a camera without playback, the usual layout stays.

  1. Open the single-camera view and hold the iPhone Duo half open like a book.

    Check: One half shows the live view as usual, with its controls bar and recording panel. The other half shows the same camera at the same time of day yesterday, on the clock of the device, with a timeline of its own. When nothing was recorded at exactly that time, it starts at the nearest recording. In left-to-right languages the live view is on the left half; in right-to-left languages the halves are swapped.

  2. Drag the timeline of either half.

    Check: That half plays from the chosen time; the other half continues unchanged.

  3. Open the iPhone Duo flat again.

    Check: The usual layout returns.

On the device page held like a book, the camera wall fills one half and the view of the selected camera the other. A tap on a thumbnail shows that camera on the other half instead of opening a new screen, and the selected thumbnail has a colored frame. At first, the first camera that is online, enabled, within the plan and not paused is selected.

YouTube and Twitch streams

YouTube live streams and Twitch channels can be added like cameras; see “Adding YouTube live streams and Twitch channels”. They play in the official player of the service, not through the camera functions of Cam Hub. A stream does not count toward the plan and is never locked; see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

  • On a wall: the tile plays the stream without sound and takes no touches of its own. It has no number and name label in its corner. A tap on the tile opens the stream full screen.
  • Full screen: the picture is as large as the screen allows, on black. The player chooses its quality from the size of the picture, so full screen plays in a higher quality than a tile. The controls of the service work here. A tap on the logo or the title of the service in the player opens the stream in the YouTube or Twitch app or in the web browser.
  • Sound: only in full screen, and only while the speaker switch is on. The speaker button next to Close is the same app-wide switch as the speaker button of a camera (see “Snapshot, sound and quality”): when sound was switched on for a camera, the stream plays with sound as soon as it opens.

  1. On the Live tab or on the device page, tap the tile of a YouTube or Twitch stream.

    Check: The stream opens full screen; when the tile was already playing, the picture continues without loading again. The close button (Close) and the speaker button sit in a strip beside the picture: above it when the iPhone is upright, at its side when it is held sideways. Nothing covers the player.

  2. Tap the speaker button (Unmute).

    Check: The symbol changes to a speaker with sound waves, and the stream plays with sound.

  3. Tap Close.

    Check: The wall is shown again, and the tile plays on without sound.

Tile or full screen showsMeaning
The player of the serviceThe stream is live.
The name of the channel with OfflineThe Twitch channel is not live. It is checked again every two minutes while it is on screen and starts by itself when the channel goes live. A channel name that does not exist also shows Offline.
This channel isn't live right now, or it doesn't allow its live streams in other apps.The followed YouTube channel has nothing live, or does not allow its streams in other apps. It is checked again every minute while it is on screen and starts by itself when a broadcast begins.
This isn't a live stream, or the broadcast has ended. Only live streams can be shown.The YouTube video is not live, or its broadcast has ended. A single broadcast does not return; Try Again asks once more.
This video isn't available. It may be private or removed. or The owner of this video doesn't allow it to be played in other apps.YouTube does not play the video in Cam Hub.
YouTube's player couldn't load. Check your connection and try again. or Twitch's player couldn't load. Check your connection and try again.The player did not load, or did not answer within about 30 seconds. Check the internet connection and tap Try Again.
The name with Agree to YouTube's terms to play this stream. or Agree to Twitch's terms to play this channel.The terms of the service have not been agreed on this iPhone or iPad yet, for example for a stream that arrived through a share code or a backup. In full screen, Review Terms… opens the notice; Agree and Continue starts the player, and Cancel leaves the stream as it is. The terms are agreed once per service.
The name with Not available in this region or language.YouTube and Twitch are not available in some countries and regions. The stream keeps its name and can be deleted like any device.
  • The service may show its own ads or announcements in the player.
  • Streams have no snapshot, PTZ control, talk, zoom, recordings, SD/HD switch or black-bar mode. The Live tab and the Full Screen Wall show neither the SD/HD button nor the black-bar button for a stream.
  • In a window of its own (see “A camera in a window of its own”), a stream shows the player with the controls of the service and, below it, Open in YouTube or Open in Twitch and the link of the stream.
  • On Apple TV, a stream shows its name only; see Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.

Connection states and messages

The state of the stream is shown over the picture.

Over the pictureMeaning and action
Spinner with Connecting…The first connection is being made.
Spinner with Reconnecting…The stream was interrupted, or the picture stopped arriving for about 15 seconds while the connection stayed open, as with a frozen camera. Cam Hub tries again by itself at growing intervals of up to about 15 seconds, and about a minute apart after ten failed attempts in a row, until the view is left. An attempt that the device refuses ends at once, without waiting for a timeout.
Message with a warning symbol and RetryThe stream could not be opened. The message names the cause, for example an unreachable device; the wording is the same as when a device is added (see “When adding fails: the checklist”). Tap Retry to try again.
Wrong username or password. with RetryThe device refused the account. Cam Hub signs in once for all cameras of a device, and after a refusal it does not sign in to the device again for about a minute, so that the account is not locked; Retry within that minute shows the same message. After a password change on the device, enter the new one with Edit Credentials; see “Changing the user name and password of a device”.
Too many requests just now. Try again in a minute. with RetryToo many requests reached the device or its service in a short time. Cam Hub does not try again by itself in this case. Wait a minute, then tap Retry.
Could not load the saved password for this device. with RetryThe saved password cannot be read. Enter it again with Edit Credentials on the device page; see “Changing the user name and password of a device”.
This recorder encrypts its video, which Cam Hub cannot read over its own protocol. Add it again and choose ONVIF under “Connect using”.The recorder sends encrypted video over its own protocol. Add it again with ONVIF as the connection method; see “Choosing the connection method”.
The recorder would not play this recording. It may have been overwritten — choose another time.The recorder refused the recording, for example because it was overwritten. Choose another time on the timeline.
Locked — upgrade to enable with PlansThe channel is outside the plan, for example because the plan ended while the view was open. Tap Plans to open the plans screen, or free a place as described in “Plan limits and enabling channels”. When the plan covers the channel again, a recording continues where it had reached.
End of recording with Back to LiveThe recording that was playing has no continuation; see “While a recording plays”.
No recording at the selected time. with RetryNo recording exists at the time that was chosen on the timeline; see “Using the timeline”.

  1. Read the message over the picture.

    Check: The message names the cause.

  2. Tap Retry.

    Check: The spinner Connecting… appears. The picture follows, or the message appears again; in that case, work through the checks in “When adding fails: the checklist” and Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.

Messages are shown in the language of the app. A few that come from the stream itself can be shown in English whatever the language of the app, for example Connection closed, No video track in SDP or HTTP 404.

A picture that stays black without a message can mean that the device sends a video format that the iPhone cannot decode. Cam Hub plays H.264 and H.265 video only, and a picture size beyond the limit of the decoder of the iPhone is not displayed. A lower resolution or the H.264 format in the settings of the device can help.

When the app moves to the background or the iPhone is locked, the stream stops. When the app returns, the stream connects again by itself. A recording that was playing resumes where it had reached.

What is not available

  • Switching to the next or previous camera by swiping. Each camera is opened from its thumbnail.
  • A button for full screen. Turning the iPhone sideways takes its place.
  • Talk through the channels of a recorder, and talking and listening at the same time: the sound of the camera pauses while the talk button is held.
  • Controls for focus, iris and PTZ speed, and storing or changing saved positions.
  • A snapshot for devices that cannot supply one, and saving or sharing recordings; see “What is not available”.

7Recording playback and speed

For devices that support playback, the single-camera view switches from the live picture to recorded footage. A day is chosen, on supported devices from a calendar that marks the days with recordings, a 24-hour timeline is moved to the wanted time, and a recording or a detected person is played from the list. A recording can be played faster at 2×, 4× or 8×. Days and times follow the clock of the device.

Where playback is available

The recording panel appears below the picture of the single-camera view (see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view”) only for devices that support playback. For all other devices, the view shows the live picture and the controls bar only. Playback is reached from three places: the single-camera view itself, the Recordings button in the close-up of a camera on a full-screen wall (see “The full-screen wall of a device”), and the same button on a LiveView Mix wall.

OfferShown when
Recording panel with day, timeline and listThe device supports playback and the account may read recordings on it.
Button for the recording calendarThe device also keeps a daily index of its recordings; see “The recording calendar”.
Switch Continuous and EventsThe device also keeps an index of detected people. Without the index, only the list of continuous recordings is shown, with no switch.
Speed buttonDuring playback, when the device can play the recording faster. If it cannot, a notice appears; see “Playback speed”.
  • Recorder channel: the recordings of the channel come from the storage of the recorder. The single-camera view of a channel shows the recordings of that channel only.
  • Standalone camera: the recordings come from the storage of the camera itself, for cameras that offer a search for recordings. A camera without recordings shows an empty day. A camera that reports that it keeps no recordings of its own, for example because a recorder records it, shows This camera doesn't keep recordings of its own. If a recorder records it, play the footage back from the recorder. in place of the list.
  • The screen and the controls are the same for both. A recorder and a camera differ only in where the recordings are kept and in whether the device supports playback.
  • Playback is offered by devices that are connected through their own protocol or through ONVIF, when the connection supports it. Which brands and connection methods offer playback is listed in Chapter 16, “Supported brands and connection methods”.
  • A device that was added through ONVIF supports playback only when it offers the ONVIF services for searching and replaying recordings. Otherwise, the day shows an empty list.
  • A device that was added through a brand from the list provides live view only, without playback; see “Choosing the connection method”. The sample cameras and YouTube and Twitch streams contain no recordings.

Choosing a day

Prerequisite: the single-camera view of a camera that supports playback is open; see “Opening the view”. Below the controls bar, the heading Recordings shows the current day on its right, with the timeline below it and the list of recordings below the timeline.

  1. Tap the day on the right of the heading Recordings.

    Check: A calendar opens.

  2. Tap the wanted day.

    Check: The calendar closes, and the heading shows the new day. Loading recordings… appears briefly, then the timeline and the list show the recordings of that day. The picture does not change.

  • The cursor of the timeline starts at the current time of the device for today, and at 12:00 for any other day.
  • Choosing a day does not start playback by itself. Playback starts from the timeline or from the list.
  • The timeline shows the chosen day and the day before it, so that footage across midnight can be reached.
  • Any day can be chosen, including days without recordings. Such a day shows an empty list. To see which days have recordings, use the recording calendar where the device offers it.

The clock of the device

Days and times in playback are those of the device, not of the iPhone. For devices that report their time zone, "today" and "now" are the date and time of the device, also when the iPhone is in another time zone: seen from a place where it is still yesterday, the day picker opens on the day of the device and the cursor on its current time. The right day is also found when the iPhone uses another calendar than the Gregorian one. For devices that do not report a time zone, the time zone of the iPhone is used.

The recording calendar

On devices that keep a daily index of their recordings, a calendar button sits between the heading Recordings and the day. Its calendar marks the days that have recordings, so that a day does not have to be tried one after another. Without such an index, the button is not shown and the day is chosen as described in “Choosing a day”.

  1. Tap the calendar button (Recording calendar) next to the day.

    Check: The sheet Recording calendar opens on the month of the chosen day. A spinner next to the name of the month shows while the device is asked. Then the days with recordings appear in bold with a dot below them, and the line Days with a dot have recordings. appears below the month. The chosen day is in a filled circle. Days after today on the clock of the device are dimmed and cannot be chosen.

  2. Tap one of the arrows beside the name of the month (Previous month or Next month).

    Check: The calendar shows the other month and marks its days with recordings. The arrow to the next month is unavailable in the current month of the device.

  3. Tap a day.

    Check: The sheet closes, and the day is chosen as with the day picker: Loading recordings… appears, then the timeline and the list show the recordings of that day.

  • Tap Done to close the sheet without choosing a day.
  • Each month is asked once while the sheet is open.
  • The week starts on the day set by the region of the iPhone. Month and weekday names follow the language of the app.
Below the monthMeaning
Days with a dot have recordings.The device answered; the dots show its days with recordings.
This recorder cannot tell which days have recordings.The device did not describe this month. The days have no dots and can still be chosen.
Could not load this month. with Try AgainThe question failed on the way, for example because of the connection. Tap Try Again.

Using the timeline

The timeline shows the recordings of the chosen day along a ruler. The orange cursor stays in the middle, and the ruler moves under it. All times are the clock of the device, not the time zone of the iPhone; see “Choosing a day”.

ElementMeaning
Orange line with a bubble above itThe cursor, fixed in the middle. The bubble shows the time at the cursor, and the date as well while the cursor is on the day before the chosen day.
Blue barsContinuous recordings.
Red barsRecordings that the device made because of an event.
Thin red marksDetected people, for devices that keep a detection index.
Dark gapsNo recording exists at that time.
Dimmed part at the left, with a dashed line and a dateThe day before the chosen day. A dashed line with a date marks every midnight.
Hour labels below the barThe scale. The divisions become finer when the timeline is enlarged.
Two magnifier buttons at the rightZoom in (plus) and Zoom out (minus) change the span that the timeline shows.

  1. Touch the timeline and drag sideways.

    Check: The ruler moves under the cursor, and the time in the bubble changes. The picture stays live while the finger moves.

  2. Lift the finger when the cursor is at the wanted time.

    Check: The picture switches to the recording from that time. The badge turns red and shows PLAYBACK 15:00:03 with the time of the playback, and Back to Live replaces the SD/HD switch.

  3. Tap Zoom in (the plus magnifier), or spread two fingers apart on the timeline.

    Check: The timeline shows a shorter span, down to 10 minutes. The button is dimmed at that limit.

  4. Tap Zoom out (the minus magnifier), or bring two fingers together on the timeline.

    Check: The timeline shows a longer span, up to 48 hours (both days). The button is dimmed at that limit. The timeline opens with a span of 24 hours.

  • A drag shorter than about 6 points on the screen is ignored, so that touching the timeline does not leave the live picture by accident.
  • When the finger is lifted in a gap, the next recording after the gap plays. The badge and the cursor jump to the start of that recording. When no recording follows, the message No recording at the selected time. appears with Retry.
  • While a recording plays, the cursor follows the playback by itself. While the timeline is being touched, the cursor stays where the finger puts it.
  • With VoiceOver, the timeline is one element: swiping up or down moves the cursor, and a double tap plays from there.

The list of recordings and the search for people

Below the timeline, a list shows the recordings of the chosen day. When the device keeps a detection index, a switch above the list selects Continuous or Events.

  • Continuous: one row per continuous recording, newest first. Each row shows a blue dot, the start time and the length of the recording in hours, minutes and seconds. A row of the day before starts with the date. The row of the recording that is playing is highlighted and shows a speaker symbol.
  • Events: one row Person detected per detection, newest first, with the start time. Detections that follow each other within 2 seconds are merged into one row.

Playing a recording from the list

  1. Tap a row under Continuous.

    Check: The picture switches to that recording, from its start. The row is highlighted, and the cursor jumps to the start time.

Finding a person

  1. Tap Events above the list.

    Check: The list shows the rows Person detected. The timeline shows the detections as thin red marks.

  2. Tap a row.

    Check: Playback starts about 5 seconds before the detection, or at the start of the recording when the recording began later. The badge shows the playback time.

Only people are searched. Recordings that were triggered by other events appear as red bars on the timeline and are played by moving the timeline to them. Cam Hub reads at most about 2,000 recordings and 2,000 detections per channel and day; anything beyond that is not listed.

MessageMeaning
Loading recordings…The device is being searched for the day.
No continuous recordings on this day.The day has no continuous recording.
This camera doesn't keep recordings of its own. If a recorder records it, play the footage back from the recorder.The camera reports that it has no recordings of its own. Open the channel of the recorder that records this camera.
No people detected on this day.The day has no detection.
This device could not search its person-event index.Shown under Events when the device does not answer the search for people. The continuous list is not affected.
Message with a warning symbol above the timeline: This account cannot read recordings on this device., Could not reach the device., The device did not recognize this camera's recordings. or This camera is offline.The search for the day failed for the reason that the message names. The day can be changed, and another day tried, while the message is shown. For the account, check its rights on the device; for the connection, see Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.
Too many requests just now. Try again in a minute.The device or its service refused the search because of too many requests, or the device was still busy with an earlier search. Wait a minute and choose the day again.
Other messages in the same place, for example The device sent an unexpected reply., The connection timed out. or Something went wrong. Please try again.The search failed for another reason. Choose the day again. When the message persists, see Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.

While a recording plays

  • Badge: the red badge at the top left of the picture shows the playback time on the clock of the device, and the time moves with the picture. It matches the time that the camera prints into its picture, when the camera does so. When the playback time is on the day before the chosen day, the date precedes the time.
  • Continuing: when a recording file ends, playback continues into the next recording by itself, so that an evening can be watched without a stop at every file. Cam Hub looks for newer recordings first, because the device may still be writing.
  • Sound: the speaker button works at normal speed only; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
  • Snapshot: takes the current live picture of the device, not a frame of the recording.
  • Zoom and pan: work as in live mode; see “Zoom and pan”. The camera control for PTZ and the talk button are hidden during playback.
  • Refused recording: when the recorder does not play a recording, for example because it was overwritten, the picture shows The recorder would not play this recording. It may have been overwritten — choose another time. Choose another time on the timeline.
  • Recordings that arrive as a file: some devices deliver a recording as a file. The picture area then shows Downloading recording… 45% with a progress bar, and the recording plays in the video player of the system, which has its own controls. The timeline cursor does not follow in that case. The downloaded files are kept in a cache of up to 500 MB on the iPhone, so that the same recording does not have to be downloaded again; Delete All Data removes the cache.
  • Background: when the app leaves the foreground or the iPhone is locked, playback stops. When the app returns, playback resumes at the point it had reached.

Returning to the live picture

  1. Tap Back to Live in the controls bar.

    Check: The live picture returns with the quality that was used before. The badge shows LIVE, the day changes to today on the clock of the device, the cursor moves to the current time of the device, and the speed returns to 1×.

At the end of the last recording

When the playback passes the end of the last recording, the last picture stays on the screen, and a card with End of recording and Back to Live appears. This is not an error.

  1. Tap Back to Live on the card.

    Check: The live picture returns as described above.

Playback speed

The speed button is a round button at the lower right of the picture. It shows the current speed, 1× at normal speed. Each tap selects the next of four speeds, in the order 1×, 2×, 4×, 8× and back to 1×. The button is shown only during playback and only when the recording can be played faster; it appears a moment after the recording starts. Live pictures always run at normal speed.

  1. Start a recording, as described in “Using the timeline” or “The list of recordings and the search for people”.

    Check: The speed button at the lower right of the picture shows 1×.

  2. Tap the speed button.

    Check: The button shows 2× and is tinted. The picture reopens at the current position, and the time advances twice as fast. About one second of the picture is lost when the stream reopens.

  3. Tap the speed button again.

    Check: The button shows 4×, and the time advances four times as fast.

  4. Tap the speed button again.

    Check: The button shows 8×, and the time advances eight times as fast.

  5. Tap the speed button again.

    Check: The button shows 1×, and the recording plays at normal speed.

  • The speed stays selected when another recording or another time is chosen during the same playback. Back to Live returns it to 1×.
  • Sound plays at 1× only. Above 1×, the picture runs without sound.
  • A higher speed makes the device send the picture faster, which uses more bandwidth.
  • The button is not shown for devices that stream recordings in a way that does not allow a change of speed.
  • In landscape orientation, the speed button is part of the strip over the picture; see “Playback in landscape”. The notice for a device that cannot play faster is not shown there; the button only returns to 1×.
A device that cannot play faster

Not every device accepts a faster speed. When the device cannot play the recording faster, the notice This recorder can't play faster than normal speed. appears above the button for about 4 seconds, and the button returns to 1×. The notice can take a few seconds to appear, because Cam Hub tries several ways of requesting the faster speed before it gives up. The same happens when the device accepts the request but the picture does not run faster. The recording continues at normal speed.

Playback in landscape

Prerequisite: the rotation lock of the iPhone is off. On an iPad, the layout does not change with the orientation; the steps below apply to the iPhone. On a half-folded iPhone Duo, the timeline stays on the lower half; see “The view on a folded iPhone Duo”.

  1. Start a recording and turn the iPhone sideways.

    Check: The picture fills the screen. A strip over the lower edge of the picture holds the badge PLAYBACK 15:00:03, the speed button, Back to Live and the timeline.

  2. Drag the timeline in the strip and lift the finger at the wanted time.

    Check: The picture plays the recording from that time, as in upright orientation.

  3. Leave the strip untouched for about 5 seconds.

    Check: The strip and the buttons at the top of the picture fade out. A tap on the picture shows them again.

  4. Tap Back to Live in the strip, or turn the iPhone upright again.

    Check: The live picture returns, or the upright layout with the recording panel is shown again.

The strip appears only during playback, because a live picture has nothing to scrub. The day, the recording calendar, the list of recordings, Snapshot and the SD/HD switch are available in upright orientation only.

What is not available

  • Playback for devices that were added through a brand from the list, for the sample cameras and for YouTube and Twitch streams; see “Where playback is available”.
  • A recording calendar for devices that keep no daily index of their recordings.
  • A search for events other than people.
  • A timeline that spans more than the chosen day and the day before it.
  • Saving, exporting or deleting recordings. Recordings can be watched only; a snapshot always shows the current live picture.
  • A choice between SD and HD during playback, slow motion, reverse playback, and speeds other than 1×, 2×, 4× and 8×.
  • Sound at speeds above 1×.
  • A pause button, frame-by-frame stepping, jumps of a few seconds, a box for entering a time, buttons for the next or previous recording, and a free-text search.
  • Playback on Apple TV is described in Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.

8LiveView Mix

LiveView Mix places cameras from different devices on one wall. The wall can also hold pictures, clocks, labels, control panels and YouTube or Twitch streams, and each of them can sit in any tile. This chapter follows the order of the work: the tab and its preview, choosing cameras, layouts, arranging, the optional portrait page, the two canvases of iPhone Duo, the full-screen wall, and the effect of plan limits on the wall.

Terms used in this chapter

Tile: one numbered position on the wall. A tile can hold a camera, a picture, a clock, a label or a control panel, or stay empty. Any tile can be filled; the tiles before it do not have to be filled first.

Layout: the arrangement of the tiles on the screen, for example 2 × 3 or 1 + 5.

Wall page: the tiles that a layout shows at once. When the wall has more tiles than the layout holds, the full-screen wall is divided into wall pages, reached by swiping.

Landscape page and portrait page: two separate walls, one for the device held sideways and an optional one for the device held upright; see “The portrait page”.

The LiveView Mix tab and its preview

Location: the LiveView Mix tab, the leftmost tab at the bottom of the screen. Before setup, the screen shows an explanation and the Set Up LiveView Mix button; for the procedure, see “Building a first wall of six cameras”. Once the wall holds at least one tile with content (a camera, a picture, a control panel, a clock or a label), the tab shows the preview, with the note Preview only — full screen shows your layout. and the Arrangement: Automatic button below it.

Three buttons in the top-right corner are, from left to right:

ButtonPurposeDetails
Full screen (gold wall icon)Opens the wall in the selected layout.“The full-screen wall”
Choose Cameras (camera icon)Selects the cameras on the wall and their quality.“Choosing cameras and quality”
Adjust the Layout (grid icon)Selects the layout, the black-bar handling, the watermark and paging, and opens the arrangement.“Adjusting the layout”

The preview behaves as follows:

  • The preview shows the filled tiles in the order of their numbers, in an even grid. Empty tiles are left out, so a wall with cameras only in tiles 2 and 7 shows two pictures side by side. The preview does not take the shape of the selected layout; the layout takes effect on the full-screen wall only.
  • The preview uses the SD or HD setting of each camera, the black-bar setting of the wall and the watermark.
  • With Automatic (the default), an iPhone held upright shows two columns, and the number of rows depends on the height of the screen. Held sideways, the preview adds columns (typically four) so that two rows fill the screen. On an iPad, the preview normally keeps two columns. When the wall has only one filled tile, that tile fills the whole preview area. A fixed number of columns and rows can be chosen instead; see “The arrangement of the preview”.
  • When there are more tiles than fit, swipe left or right to change the page; page dots appear below the preview.
  • While the watermark is off, each camera shows its channel number and name in the bottom-left corner. When the watermark is on, the watermark replaces this label.
  • Tapping a camera picture opens the full-screen viewer; see “Opening a single camera”. Tapping a YouTube or Twitch tile opens that stream full screen; see “YouTube and Twitch streams on the wall”. Tapping a button of a control panel sends its request; when the button is set to ask for confirmation first, a confirmation dialog appears; see Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
  • A camera that cannot be shown keeps its tile and shows a status text; see “When a tile cannot show a camera”.
  • While the full-screen wall is open, the preview pauses its streams; they resume when the tab is shown again. On an iPhone, the preview also pauses while the Choose Cameras or Adjust the Layout page covers it.
  • When the portrait page is switched on, the tab shows the portrait page while it is taller than wide; see “The portrait page”. On an iPhone Duo with two canvases, the tab shows both canvases instead; see “Two canvases on iPhone Duo”.
  • When no tile has anything to show (for example when every tile points at a camera that has been removed), the screen shows LiveView Mix is empty with a pointer to Settings.
Hold the device sideways

The layouts are drawn for a wide screen. Held sideways, the tiles keep the wide shape of camera pictures; held upright, the layout is flipped about its diagonal (see “Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device”), unless a portrait page of its own is switched on (see “The portrait page”). The preview and the full-screen wall rearrange themselves with the angle of the device.

The arrangement of the preview

The Arrangement: Automatic button at the end of the preview note sets how many columns and rows of tiles the preview shows on each of its pages. The choice is one of the app settings, not part of the wall: it does not change the full-screen wall, and it travels with the app settings in a backup or a share code (see “What backups and codes contain”). The chosen columns and rows stay the same whichever way the device is held.

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Arrangement: Automatic below the preview.

    Check: A small window opens over the preview with the Automatic switch, which is on by default.

  2. Switch off Automatic.

    Check: The window shows Columns and Rows, each with − and +, set to 2 and 2, and the preview changes to a 2 × 2 grid.

  3. Tap − or + beside Columns and Rows until the wanted grid is shown. Each count runs from 1 to 4.

    Check: The preview follows every tap, and every tile fills its share of the screen.

  4. Tap anywhere outside the window.

    Check: The window closes, and the button shows the chosen grid, for example Arrangement: 2 × 4.

To return to the automatic grid, switch Automatic on again. When the last page of a fixed grid is not full, its remaining cells stay empty.

Building a first wall of six cameras

Purpose: place six cameras on one wall and view it full screen in the 1 + 5 layout. Time needed: about 5 minutes.

Prerequisites:

  • The devices have been added and offer at least six channels to choose from; for adding, see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.
  • All six channels are enabled and within the allowance of the plan. The Free plan allows only 2 enabled channels across the whole app; channels beyond that appear on the wall as Disabled or Not in your plan. For the allowances and for enabling channels, see “How plan limits affect the wall” and Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
  • The device is an iPhone or an iPad. For Apple TV, see “Differences on Apple TV”.

  1. Tap the LiveView Mix tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: When LiveView Mix has not been set up, the screen shows an explanation and the Set Up LiveView Mix button.

  2. Tap Set Up LiveView Mix.

    Check: The Choose Cameras page opens and lists all channels, grouped by device. The top of the page shows the Landscape page and Portrait page switch with Landscape page selected, and below it 0 cameras selected.

  3. Tap the circle in front of the first of the six channels.

    Check: The circle is ticked, and an SD and HD selector appears on the right of the row, set to SD.

  4. Tick five more channels, in the order in which they should appear on the wall.

    Check: The top of the page shows 6 cameras selected.

  5. Optional: tap HD beside each camera that should show a sharper picture.

    Check: The selector of that camera shows HD. The other cameras are unchanged.

  6. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes and the tab shows a preview of the six cameras.

  7. Tap Adjust the Layout (the grid icon) in the top-right corner.

    Check: The Adjust the Layout page opens. The top of the page shows This layout holds 4 · 6 placed. The default layout holds only 4 tiles per page, so six cameras would use two wall pages.

  8. In the Full-screen layout section, tap 1 + 5.

    Check: The layout is highlighted, and the top of the page shows This layout holds 6 · 6 placed.

  9. Scroll down to the Watermark section and switch on Show watermark.

    Check: The section shows the options for position, content and style. Device name and Camera name are on.

  10. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes. Every camera in the preview is marked with its device name and camera name.

  11. Turn the device sideways.

    Check: The preview rearranges itself for the new angle. No setting is needed.

  12. Tap Full screen (the gold wall icon) in the top-right corner.

    Check: The wall fills the screen: the first camera is in the large tile in the top-left corner (two thirds of the width and height), and the other five are to its right and below it. A ✕ button is in the top-left corner.

  13. Tap the picture of any camera.

    Check: The screen changes to the single-camera view of that camera, playing in HD, with a back button in the top-left corner.

  14. Tap the back button ‹ in the top-left corner.

    Check: The screen shows the full-screen wall again.

  15. Tap ✕ in the top-left corner.

    Check: The wall closes and the preview in the LiveView Mix tab is shown again.

Expected outcome: the LiveView Mix tab shows a preview of six cameras, and the full-screen wall shows them in the 1 + 5 layout, with the first camera in the large tile. To put a different camera in the large tile, see “Arranging the wall and its tiles”. When some tiles show a status text instead of a picture, see “When a tile cannot show a camera” and Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.

Choosing cameras and quality

Path: LiveView Mix › Choose Cameras. The page can also be opened from Settings › LiveView Mix, where the camera selection and the layout options are on one page; see “LiveView Mix in Settings”. When the page is opened from the tab, the switch at the top chooses whether the landscape page or the portrait page is being edited; see “The portrait page”.

ItemDescription
Count at the top of the page6 cameras selected updates as channels are ticked. It counts cameras only, not empty tiles, pictures, clocks, labels or control panels.
Channel rowsOne section per device and one row per channel: a circle, a thumbnail, the channel number and the name. The thumbnail shows a live picture only for channels that the plan covers; the others show Disabled or Not in your plan. YouTube and Twitch streams are listed with their name only.
Order of tickingA newly ticked camera goes into the tile after the last filled tile. To put a camera in a particular tile, use Put a camera here in Arrange the wall; see “Arranging the wall and its tiles”.
DuplicatesA channel can be placed on a wall only once.
SD | HDAfter a channel is ticked, a quality selector appears on the right of its row. A newly added camera is set to SD. YouTube and Twitch streams have no selector; their quality follows the size of their tile.
All SD, All HDTwo buttons at the top of the page that set the quality of all selected cameras at once.
No DevicesShown when no device has been added yet, with a prompt to add one first.

The quality rule of LiveView Mix

  • LiveView Mix has its own quality, set for each tile. It is not affected by Single camera and Multiple cameras under Settings › Default quality; those settings apply to the single-camera view and to the ordinary device walls only.
  • Each tile on the wall plays in SD or HD according to its own setting. When tiles are small, HD and SD look almost the same. Using SD for most tiles and HD only for the cameras that need to be seen clearly reduces the load on bandwidth and on the device.
  • A single camera that is opened from the wall or from the preview always starts in HD, whatever the setting of its tile. In the full-screen viewer of the preview, the quality can be switched for the current viewing; the switch is not saved. See “Opening a single camera”.
  • The thumbnails on the Choose Cameras page and on the arrange canvas always use SD.

To choose cameras:

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Choose Cameras (the camera icon).

    Check: The Choose Cameras page opens. Cameras that are already selected are ticked.

  2. Tap the circle in front of a channel to add it to the wall.

    Check: The circle is ticked, SD and HD appear on the row, and the count at the top increases by 1.

  3. To change the quality of that camera, tap HD or SD.

    Check: The selector shows the chosen quality. Only this camera is affected.

  4. Optional: to change the quality of all selected cameras at once, tap All SD or All HD.

    Check: The selectors of all selected cameras show the same quality.

  5. To remove a camera from the wall, tap the circle of a ticked channel again.

    Check: The circle is empty again, and the count at the top decreases by 1. The tile of that camera becomes empty; no other tile moves.

  6. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes and the preview is updated to the new selection.

Removing a camera leaves its tile empty

After a camera is unticked, its tile is left empty in place. Every other tile, including pictures, clocks, labels and control panels, keeps its number and its position on the wall. The empty tile can be filled again later in Arrange the wall; see “Arranging the wall and its tiles”.

When the page is opened with the button in the top-right corner of the LiveView Mix tab, Cancel in the top-left corner restores the wall to its state before the page was opened. Done keeps the selection.

Tiles that point at removed cameras

When a tile on the wall points at a camera that Cam Hub no longer has (for example after a restore on a device where that camera was not added), the top of the Choose Cameras page shows 2 slots point at cameras that were removed. and the Empty Those Slots button. These tiles do not appear in the list of ticks.

  1. Tap Empty Those Slots.

    Check: The note and the button disappear. These tiles become empty in place, and all other cameras keep their positions.

Adjusting the layout

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout. The top of the page shows This layout holds 6 · 6 placed: the first number is the number of tiles per wall page of the selected layout, the second is the number of tiles on the wall that hold content. Placed tiles include cameras and also configured pictures, control panels, clocks and labels, but not empty tiles.

The Full-screen layout section lists the ready-made layouts in order, with Custom last. Each layout is shown as a small diagram of its shape, with its name below. On the portrait page, the diagrams are drawn tall, because that wall is laid out for an upright screen.

LayoutTiles per pageShape
2 × 242 columns, 2 rows, tiles of equal size
2 × 362 columns, 3 rows, tiles of equal size
3 × 393 columns, 3 rows, tiles of equal size
3 × 4123 columns, 4 rows, tiles of equal size
4 × 4164 columns, 4 rows, tiles of equal size
1 + 34One large tile on the left (two thirds of the width) and three small tiles in a column on the right
1 + 56One large tile in the top-left corner (two thirds of the width and height) and five small tiles to its right and below it
1 + 78One large tile in the top-left corner (three quarters of the width and height) and seven small tiles to its right and below it
CustomUp to 64A layout drawn by hand; see “Drawing a custom layout”
  • Tile 1 is the first tile of the layout; in a layout with one large tile, tile 1 is the large one. The other numbers follow the order of the layout.
  • When a wall page cannot hold all tiles, the remaining tiles go to the next wall page. For example, 6 tiles in the 2 × 2 layout use 2 wall pages: 4 tiles on the first and 2 on the second, with the remaining positions black.
  • A layout with more than 16 tiles carries a TV icon (Best on a large screen) in the top-right corner of its diagram. It is hard to read on a phone and is better viewed on an iPad or an Apple TV.
  • On an iPhone and an iPad, the ready-made layouts offered are those with up to 16 tiles. Ready-made layouts with more than 16 tiles (5 × 4 to 7 × 7, 1 + 21 and 1 + 27) are offered only on Apple TV; see Chapter 14, “Apple TV”. A wall that is already set to one of them (for example after a restore) is still shown correctly, and its diagram appears in the list. To place more tiles on a phone or an iPad, use a custom layout.
  • The Custom diagram shows the layout that was drawn. Until one has been drawn, it shows the starting shape; tapping it selects that shape.

To select a layout:

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Adjust the Layout (the grid icon).

    Check: The Adjust the Layout page opens. The layout in use is highlighted.

  2. In the Full-screen layout section, tap the layout to use.

    Check: The selected layout is highlighted, and the number of tiles per page at the top is updated.

  3. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes. The preview keeps its even grid, and the selected layout takes effect on the full-screen wall.

The same page also holds the arrangement, the black bars, the watermark and the paging option, described in “Arranging the wall and its tiles”, “Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device”, “Watermark” and “LiveView Mix in Settings” respectively.

The scope of Cancel and Done

The Choose Cameras and Adjust the Layout pages that open from the LiveView Mix tab each have Cancel and Done. Cancel restores every wall to its state before the page was opened, including any arrangement, custom layout, work on the other page and the portrait page switch. Custom Layout, Arrange and Slot N each have their own Cancel and Done: Done only returns to the previous level, and Cancel restores only what was changed since that level was entered. To keep all changes, tap Done all the way back to the outermost page.

Drawing a custom layout

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout › Draw a custom layout. When none of the ready-made layouts fits, the number of rows and columns of the grid can be chosen freely, and neighboring cells can be merged into larger tiles. On the portrait page, the grid is drawn tall.

ItemDescription
Starting shapeA 3 × 3 grid whose top-left 2 × 2 block is already merged into one large tile: 6 tiles in all.
Rows, ColumnsSet with − and +, from 2 to 8. The maximum is 8 × 8, which is 64 tiles.
TilesThe total number of tiles after merging. With more than 16 tiles, a note appears below: That many tiles is best viewed on iPad or Apple TV.
MergingDrag a finger across several cells of the grid; the rectangle that is covered becomes one large tile. A large tile can only be a rectangle, not an L shape or any other irregular shape.
SplittingTap a merged tile to split it back into single cells. Tapping a single cell does nothing.
Split all merged tilesSplits all large tiles at once. The button is unavailable when there are none.
NumbersThe number on each tile follows reading order (left to right, top to bottom) and is the tile number used on the arrange canvas. A large tile takes the position of its top-left cell.
Use this layoutMakes the drawn layout the layout of the wall. When it is already in use, the button is replaced by Your wall is using this layout.

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Adjust the Layout.

    Check: The Adjust the Layout page opens.

  2. In the Full-screen layout section, tap Draw a custom layout.

    Check: The Custom Layout page opens: the grid is at the top, with Rows, Columns and Tiles below it.

  3. Set the size of the grid with − and + on the right of Rows and Columns.

    Check: The grid is redrawn with the new number of rows and columns, and Tiles is updated. When rows or columns are reduced, any large tile that no longer fits is removed.

  4. Drag one finger across the grid, from the first cell to be merged to the last.

    Check: During the drag, the covered area is highlighted. After the finger is lifted, the cells in that area are merged into one large tile, Tiles decreases and the numbers are reassigned.

  5. To split a large tile, tap it once.

    Check: The large tile is split into single cells, and Tiles increases.

  6. Tap Use this layout.

    Check: The button is replaced by Your wall is using this layout.

  7. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen returns to the Adjust the Layout page. The Custom diagram is selected and shows the shape that was drawn last.

  • When a drag touches existing large tiles, those tiles are split first, and then only the dragged rectangle is merged. The area is never enlarged automatically.
  • When a drag goes beyond the edge of the grid, the area stops at the cells on the edge.
  • Every change to the grid and the large tiles is stored immediately. Tapping Cancel in the top-left corner restores everything that was changed since the page was opened.
  • Drawing a layout without tapping Use this layout does not change the current wall; a shape that is not in use can also be tidied up here.
  • The drawn layout is kept even when a ready-made layout is selected for a while. Tapping the Custom diagram later returns to that shape.
  • The custom layout can also be selected in the layout row at the top of the Arrange page, but its shape can only be edited here.
  • When the device is held upright, a drawn layout is flipped like the ready-made ones, but each camera stays in the tile it was placed in; see “Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device”.

Special layouts: big and small tiles on one wall

A custom layout can merge neighboring cells into large tiles. This makes a layout like the video wall of a monitoring center: the important cameras are enlarged, the others are reduced to small tiles, and clocks, labels or control panels share the same wall.

Example: a grid of 4 rows and 4 columns, with a 2 × 2 large tile merged at the top left and at the bottom left, 10 tiles in all. The 2 large tiles and 6 of the small tiles on the right hold 8 cameras; the remaining 2 small tiles hold a control panel and a clock.

Prerequisites: 8 cameras have been selected for the wall as described in “Choosing cameras and quality”, and the drag operation in “Drawing a custom layout” has been read. Time needed: about 3 minutes.

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Adjust the Layout, then tap Draw a custom layout.

    Check: The Custom Layout page shows the starting shape: a 3 × 3 grid with a 2 × 2 large tile at the top left.

  2. Set Rows to 4 and Columns to 4.

    Check: The grid becomes 4 × 4, the large tile at the top left is kept, and Tiles shows 13.

  3. Drag one finger across the grid, over the 2 × 2 cells at the bottom left (the third and fourth rows, first and second columns).

    Check: The four cells are merged into a second large tile, and Tiles shows 10. The large tiles are numbered 1 and 6.

  4. Tap Use this layout, then tap Done.

    Check: The screen returns to the Adjust the Layout page, and the Custom diagram is selected.

  5. Tap Arrange the wall and drag the cameras to be enlarged onto the large tiles numbered 1 and 6.

    Check: The dragged camera and the content of the target tile swap places. For the arrangement, see “Arranging the wall and its tiles”.

  6. On the Arrange page, give the two unused tiles 9 and 10 a control panel and a clock: tap each tile, choose Picture, control panel, clock or label…, and set Shows to Control for one and to Clock for the other.

    Check: The canvas shows the control panel and the clock in the two tiles. For the setup, see “What a tile can show besides a camera”.

  7. Tap Done repeatedly to return to the LiveView Mix tab, turn the device sideways, and tap Full screen.

    Check: The wall shows two large tiles and eight small tiles of mixed sizes, as in the picture below.

Expected outcome: the wall follows the layout that was drawn, and the large tiles hold the important cameras. For control panels, see Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”. The tiles, the positions of the large tiles and the content of each tile are stored on this device; when changing devices, a backup and restore can carry them along; see “LiveView Mix in Settings”.

Arranging the wall and its tiles

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout › Arrange the wall. This page decides what goes into each tile. Its title is Arrange. From top to bottom, the page holds the layout row, the canvas, Tips and the Order list. Arrange the wall is available as soon as cameras have been selected or a device exists.

  • Layout row: the same layout diagrams as on Adjust the Layout; the layout can be changed here directly. The Custom diagram appears once a layout has been drawn or while it is in use, and can only be selected here.
  • Canvas: drawn in 16:9 landscape for the landscape page and in 9:16 portrait for the portrait page, showing the current wall page. The number of each filled tile is in its top-left corner. Camera tiles show a live picture (SD); a camera that is offline or outside the plan shows a black tile with a crossed-out camera icon, and a YouTube or Twitch stream shows its name.
