While the watermark is off, the channel name is in the bottom-left corner; when it is on, the watermark is previewed. Control panels on the canvas look as they do on the wall; tapping one opens its editor and does not send a request. On a device held upright, the real landscape wall is flipped, but each tile keeps its number.
  • Unused tiles: shown with a dashed outline and a +. They are tiles with nothing in them, either between filled tiles or after the last one. Tapping one offers what to put in it; see the table below.
  • Changing pages: when there are more tiles than the layout holds, arrows and Page 1 of 2 appear below the canvas. Swiping left or right also changes the page.
  • Tips: a note that can be folded away. The folded state is remembered.
  • Order list: the filled tiles only, each under its own tile number. A camera row shows the channel name over the device name. Other rows show the kind of content (Control, Clock, Label, Slot image or Empty slot for a tile that only has a color); a control panel row also shows the panel title, and a label row the text of the label, so tiles of the same kind can be told apart.
  • Toolbar: Cancel in the top-left corner, Edit and Done in the top-right corner.

Tapping an unused tile opens a menu titled with the tile number, for example Slot 7:

ChoiceWhat it does
Put a camera hereLists the cameras that are not on this wall yet, grouped by device. The camera that is tapped goes into this tile. When every camera is placed, the list shows Every camera is already on the wall.
Move another tile here…Moves a filled tile from any wall page into this tile; see “Moving a tile into an empty tile”. Offered when the wall has at least one filled tile.
Picture, control panel, clock or label…Opens the Slot N page, where the tile is given a picture, a control panel, a clock, a label or a color; see “What a tile can show besides a camera”.
Copy from the landscape page… or Copy from the portrait page…Copies a control panel, clock, label, picture or colored tile from the other page; see “The portrait page”. Offered on the portrait page, and on the landscape page while the portrait page is switched on.

To put a camera in a chosen tile:

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Adjust the Layout, then tap Arrange the wall.

    Check: The Arrange page opens.

  2. Tap an unused tile on the canvas, for example tile 7.

    Check: A menu titled Slot 7 appears.

  3. Tap Put a camera here.

    Check: The list of cameras that are not on the wall yet opens, titled Slot 7.

  4. Tap a camera.

    Check: The list closes. The camera appears in tile 7 on the canvas and in the Order list under number 7. Tiles 1 to 6 that hold nothing stay empty.

To swap the places of two tiles:

  1. Drag a filled tile on the canvas with one finger onto another tile. Pressing and holding first is not needed.

    Check: The dragged tile lifts and follows the finger, and the target tile shows a highlighted frame.

  2. Lift the finger.

    Check: The two tiles have swapped places, and the Order list is updated.

  • When a tile is dropped onto an unused tile, it moves there, and its old tile is left empty. No other tile moves.
  • When the finger leaves the canvas before it is lifted, the wall is unchanged.
  • A drag reaches only the tiles of the wall page on screen. To bring a tile from another wall page into an empty tile, use Move another tile here…; to swap two filled tiles on different wall pages, use the Order list.
  • Tapping a camera tile does nothing; cameras are removed in Choose Cameras or with the Order list. Tapping a tile that holds a picture, a control panel, a clock or a label opens its editor; see “What a tile can show besides a camera”.

To change places and empty tiles with the list:

  1. Tap Edit in the top-right corner.

    Check: Every row of the Order list shows a reorder handle and a remove button.

  2. Drag the reorder handle on the right of a row to a new position in the list.

    Check: The contents change places among the same filled tiles; the empty tiles stay empty. The numbers and the canvas are updated, across wall pages as well.

  3. To empty a tile, swipe its row to the left and tap Delete; in editing mode, the remove button of the row can be used as well.

    Check: The row disappears and the tile becomes empty; no other tile moves. When a camera tile is emptied, that camera is also unticked in Choose Cameras.

  4. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen returns to the Adjust the Layout page, and the arrangement is kept.

  • The canvas always shows a few unused tiles while the last wall page has room. When every tile of the layout is filled, select a layout with more tiles in the layout row, or empty a tile, before adding something new.
  • Tapping Cancel in the top-left corner restores the wall to its state when the Arrange page was entered.

Moving a tile into an empty tile

Move another tile here… moves any filled tile, from this wall page or another one, into an empty tile that was tapped. Its old tile is left empty, and nothing else moves. This is the way to fill an empty tile on the first wall page with a control panel that sits on the second wall page, which a drag cannot reach.

  1. On the Arrange page, tap the unused tile that should receive the content, for example tile 9.

    Check: A menu titled Slot 9 appears.

  2. Tap Move another tile here….

    Check: A list titled Slot 9 opens with every filled tile of the wall, from all wall pages, each under its tile number and described as in the Order list. The note below the list reads The one you pick moves into this tile, and its old tile is left empty. Nothing else moves.

  3. Tap the tile to move, for example the control panel in tile 12.

    Check: The list closes. The control panel is in tile 9, and tile 12 is empty. All other tiles keep their places.

To leave the list without moving anything, tap Cancel in its top-left corner.

What a tile can show besides a camera

A tile does not have to hold a camera. Tap an unused tile and choose Picture, control panel, clock or label…, or tap a tile that already holds one of these, to open the Slot N page, and choose the content with the Shows menu:

ContentOptions and description
EmptyA plain colored space. Color selects the color; the default is black. Choosing Empty removes any picture, control panel, clock or label that the tile held. A tile given a color other than black stays on the wall as a colored tile and shows Tap to fill on the canvas; a black tile with nothing in it counts as unused.
ImageChoose Photo picks a picture from the photo library, and Take Photo takes one with the camera (not shown when the device has no camera). After a picture is chosen, Fill sets how it fills the tile: Default (the whole picture, possibly with black bars), Enlarge to fill (fills the tile, the edges are cropped) or Stretch to fill (fills the tile, the picture is distorted). Best size shows the size in pixels that the tile covers on a 3840 × 2160 screen (2160 × 3840 for the portrait page). When a picture is already set, the button changes to Choose a Different Photo, and Remove Image appears. A picture is stored reduced to at most 512 pixels on its long side, so a picture in a large tile can look soft.
ControlA row of buttons; each button sends an HTTP request when it is tapped. For the setup of control panels and their buttons, see Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
ClockShows the current time. Options: 24-hour (on by default; when off, the convention of the app language applies), Show seconds, Show date (on by default) and Show day of the week. The names of days and months follow the language of the app, and their order follows the convention of that language.
LabelText on several lines. Text holds the content, Icon names a system symbol that is shown above the text (SF Symbol (optional); empty means no symbol), and Text color and Background set the colors. The defaults are white text on a black background.
Changing the kind of content removes the previous content

When another kind is selected in the Shows menu, the previous content is removed at once. For example, changing Control to Clock removes the button settings of the control panel. Cancel in the top-left corner restores them.

To place a picture in an unused tile:

  1. On the Arrange page, tap an unused tile on the canvas.

    Check: A menu titled with the tile number appears.

  2. Tap Picture, control panel, clock or label….

    Check: The Slot N page opens, with Shows set to Empty.

  3. Tap Shows and select Image.

    Check: The page shows the Image section with the Choose Photo button.

  4. Tap Choose Photo, then tap a photo in the photo selection screen of the system.

    Check: The page shows a preview of the picture, with Fill, Best size, Choose a Different Photo and Remove Image.

  5. In the Fill menu, select how the picture fills the tile.

    Check: The menu shows the chosen way.

  6. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The tile on the canvas shows the picture.

To place a clock in an unused tile:

  1. Tap an unused tile on the canvas, tap Picture, control panel, clock or label…, and select Clock in the Shows menu.

    Check: The page shows the Clock section with 24-hour, Show seconds, Show date and Show day of the week.

  2. Switch each option on or off as needed.

    Check: The clock on the canvas reflects the settings at once.

  3. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes, and the canvas shows the clock.

To place a label in an unused tile:

  1. Tap an unused tile on the canvas, tap Picture, control panel, clock or label…, and select Label in the Shows menu.

    Check: The page shows the Label section with Text, Icon, Text color and Background.

  2. Enter the text to be shown in the Text field.

    Check: The tile on the canvas shows the text.

  3. Optional: enter the name of a system symbol in the Icon field, and adjust the colors with Text color and Background.

    Check: The tile shows the symbol, and the colors change accordingly.

  4. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes, and the canvas shows the label.

When the Slot N page of a new tile is closed without giving the tile anything, the tile stays unused. Pictures, clocks and labels do not use the camera allowance of the plan; control panels do. See “How plan limits affect the wall”.

Watermark

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout, then scroll to the Watermark section. The watermark overlays text on the picture of each camera tile, showing which camera of which device the picture comes from. On the full-screen wall, pictures carry no label by default, so the watermark is recommended when cameras of several devices share one wall. Each wall (the landscape page, the portrait page and each canvas of an iPhone Duo) has its own watermark settings.

OptionDescriptionDefault
Show watermarkThe main switch. The options below appear only when it is on.Off
PositionTop left, Top, Top right, Center, Bottom left, Bottom or Bottom right.Bottom right
Device nameShows the name of the device.On
Camera nameShows the name of the channel.On
IP addressShows the address of the camera itself; when the device does not report one, the address of the device.Off
OpacityA slider from 0.2 to 1.0.85
ColorThe color of the text.White
Text sizeA slider from 8 to 28.11
FontSystem, Rounded, Monospaced or Serif.System
LegibilityKeeps the text readable over the picture: Shadow, Outline, Backdrop (a semi-transparent plate behind the text) or None. When the background is too bright or too busy, use Backdrop.Shadow
PreviewPreviews the watermark on a light and a dark swatch. The sample names come from the first camera on the wall.—

  1. On the Adjust the Layout page, scroll down to the Watermark section and switch on Show watermark.

    Check: The section expands and shows the options.

  2. Select the Position, and switch on the names to be shown: Device name, Camera name or IP address.

    Check: The two swatches of Preview show the selected content and position.

  3. Adjust Opacity, Color, Text size, Font and Legibility.

    Check: Preview reflects the adjustments at once.

  4. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes. The camera pictures in the preview, on the arrange canvas and on the full-screen wall show the watermark.

  • The watermark is drawn on camera tiles only, not on control panels, pictures, clocks or labels.
  • When all three names are switched off, no text is shown.
  • The watermark does not intercept touches; tapping a picture behaves as before.
  • While the watermark is off, camera tiles in the preview and on the arrange canvas show the channel number and name; the full-screen wall shows no label at all.

Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout › Black bars on this wall. When the shape of a camera picture differs from the shape of its tile, black bars appear. Black bars on this wall decides how all camera pictures on the wall handle them. There are three options:

  • Default: the whole picture is shown, and black bars may appear.
  • Enlarge to fill: the picture is enlarged in proportion until it fills the tile. The edges are cropped, and there are no black bars.
  • Stretch to fill: the picture is stretched to fill the tile. Nothing is cropped and there are no black bars, but the picture is distorted.

YouTube and Twitch streams always show the whole picture, whatever this setting is; see “YouTube and Twitch streams on the wall”.

  1. On the Adjust the Layout page, tap Black bars on this wall.

    Check: A menu lists Default, Enlarge to fill and Stretch to fill.

  2. Select an option.

    Check: The menu shows the selected option. The camera pictures in the preview and on the full-screen wall follow it.

  • This setting belongs to LiveView Mix only and is independent of the default under Settings › Picture › Black bars. Picture tiles have their own Fill option.
  • The single-camera view that opens from the full-screen wall always shows the whole picture. The full-screen viewer of the preview has its own switch; see “Opening a single camera”.
  • Settings › Picture › Edge-to-edge video is on by default. It lets full-screen video extend under the Dynamic Island and the rounded corners of the screen for the largest picture. When it is off, the picture keeps clear of these areas, at the cost of black bars. The setting applies to the full-screen wall of LiveView Mix as well.

The angle of the device

The full-screen wall is not locked to an orientation. It rearranges itself with the angle of the device; no setting is needed. What decides is the shape of the space the wall fills, so an iPad window narrowed in Split View counts as upright.

Angle of the deviceWhat the wall looks like
Held sideways (wider than tall)The layout is shown as it is.
Held upright (taller than wide), ready-made layoutThe layout is flipped about its diagonal: 4 columns by 2 rows becomes 2 columns by 4 rows, and a large tile on the left moves to the top. The tiles are numbered again in reading order (left to right, then top to bottom), and the content follows the numbers.
Held upright, drawn layoutThe layout is flipped about its diagonal as well, but each camera stays in the tile it was placed in, so a camera put in a large tile is still in that large tile.
Held upright, portrait page switched onThe portrait page is shown instead, as it was laid out; nothing is flipped. See “The portrait page”.
An area whose width equals its heightThe layout is not flipped.

The canvas of the landscape page on the Arrange page is always drawn in landscape; held upright, the real wall is flipped as described above.

The portrait page

LiveView Mix is laid out for a device held sideways. The portrait page is an optional second wall that is shown while the device is held upright, with its own cameras, layout, control panels, clocks, labels, pictures and watermark. It is off by default; while it is off, an upright device shows the landscape wall flipped (see “Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device”). On an iPad, the portrait page is shown while the iPad or its window is taller than wide.

  • The portrait page is laid out for an upright screen: its layout diagrams, its drawing grid and its arrange canvas are tall, and the wall is never flipped.
  • The tab, the preview and the full-screen wall swap between the landscape page and the portrait page as the device turns. While a camera opened from the wall is shown, the wall stays as it is until the camera is closed.
  • When the portrait page is switched on but has nothing on it yet, the upright tab shows Portrait page with the note This wall shows while the phone is upright. Pick its cameras, and lay it out for a tall screen. and the Set Up LiveView Mix button.
  • The Choose Cameras and Adjust the Layout buttons of the tab open the page that is on screen. At the top of these pages, the switch with Landscape page and Portrait page moves between the two pages. On the portrait page, the switch Show this page when the phone is upright (on an iPad, Show this page when the screen is upright) turns the portrait page on or off. The first change made to the portrait page turns it on, unless the switch was already used in this editor.
  • The portrait page can also be switched on and off with Settings › Portrait page, and set up there; see “LiveView Mix in Settings”.
  • While the two canvases of an iPhone Duo are shown, they are shown instead of the portrait page; see “Two canvases on iPhone Duo”.
  • The control panels of the portrait page count toward the plan while the portrait page is switched on; see “How plan limits affect the wall”. Their buttons also appear on the Apple Watch; see “Buttons on Apple Watch”.

To set up the portrait page from the LiveView Mix tab:

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Choose Cameras.

    Check: The Choose Cameras page opens with the Landscape page and Portrait page switch at the top.

  2. Tap Portrait page in the switch.

    Check: The page shows the cameras of the portrait page, and below the page switch the switch Show this page when the phone is upright, which is off.

  3. Tick the cameras for the upright wall.

    Check: The count at the top increases, and Show this page when the phone is upright switches on with the first tick.

  4. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes.

  5. Hold the phone upright.

    Check: The tab shows the preview of the portrait page. Held sideways, it shows the landscape page again.

  6. Hold the phone upright and tap Adjust the Layout.

    Check: The Adjust the Layout page opens on the portrait page, with tall layout diagrams. Choose a layout and arrange the tiles as for the landscape page; see “Adjusting the layout” and “Arranging the wall and its tiles”.

Copying control panels, clocks, labels and pictures between the pages

A control panel, clock, label, picture or colored tile that has been set up on one page can be copied to the other instead of being built again. Cameras are not copied; they are placed with Put a camera here.

  1. On the Arrange page of the portrait page, tap an unused tile.

    Check: The menu titled with the tile number shows Copy from the landscape page… among its choices. On the landscape page, the choice is Copy from the portrait page…, offered while the portrait page is switched on.

  2. Tap Copy from the landscape page….

    Check: A list opens under the heading Landscape page. Each row shows the kind of tile, a control panel's title or a label's text, and its tile number on that page. When there is nothing to copy, the list shows Nothing to copy.

  3. Tap the tile to copy.

    Check: The list closes, and the copy appears in the tile that was tapped.

The copy is independent of the original, as the note under the list says: The copy is set up on its own: changing it later leaves the other page as it is. A copied control panel counts toward the plan on its own, and a copied picture is stored twice, which adds to the size of the backup.

Two canvases on iPhone Duo

On an iPhone Duo held half-folded, with the fold across the screen, LiveView Mix can be split at the fold into two canvases: the upper canvas above the fold and the lower canvas below it. Each canvas is a wall of its own, with its own cameras, layout, wall pages, control panels and close-up; a typical use is cameras on the upper canvas and control panels on the lower one. The setting appears only on an iPhone Duo; for the iPhone Duo in general, see “iPhone Duo”.

Position of the iPhone DuoWhat LiveView Mix shows
Half-folded, fold across the screenThe upper canvas above the fold and the lower canvas below it, separated by a dark strip that lies on the fold.
Opened flat, closed, or held upright like a bookThe upper canvas alone. Swiping past its last wall page shows the lower canvas; swiping back past the first wall page of the lower canvas returns to the upper one. Two dots at the top of the screen show which canvas is on screen. With the portrait page switched on and the screen upright, the portrait page takes the place of the upper canvas.

To switch on the two canvases and set up the lower one:

  1. On the iPhone Duo, tap the Settings tab and switch on Two canvases.

    Check: The switch is on. The LiveView Mix section now lists Upper canvas and Lower canvas.

  2. Half-fold the iPhone Duo, and tap the LiveView Mix tab.

    Check: The tab shows the upper canvas above the fold and the lower canvas below it. An empty canvas shows its name and the Set Up LiveView Mix button. The top-right corner of the screen keeps only the Full screen button.

  3. Tap the round button with sliders in the top-right corner of the lower canvas.

    Check: A menu titled Lower canvas offers Choose Cameras and Adjust the Layout.

  4. Tap Adjust the Layout, then set up the lower canvas as any wall; see “Adjusting the layout” and “Arranging the wall and its tiles”.

    Check: After Done, the lower canvas shows its tiles below the fold.

  • Full screen opens both canvases edge to edge, with the ✕ button in the top-left corner of the upper canvas.
  • While the two canvases are shown, the editors have no Landscape page and Portrait page switch.
  • The control panels of the lower canvas count toward the plan, and appear on the Apple Watch, only while the two canvases are switched on.
  • The lower canvas travels in a backup. Restored on an iPhone or an iPad, it is kept but not shown; restored on an iPhone Duo again, it returns.

The full-screen wall

Path: LiveView Mix › Full screen. The full-screen wall places all tiles in the selected layout and fills the screen. The wall carries no labels unless the watermark is switched on.

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Full screen (the gold wall icon) in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen changes to the full-screen wall. The status bar is hidden, and a ✕ button (Close) is in the top-left corner.

  2. When the wall has several wall pages, swipe to the left.

    Check: The next wall page is shown, and the page dots at the bottom of the screen move to the next dot.

  3. Swipe to the right.

    Check: The previous wall page is shown again.

  4. Tap ✕ in the top-left corner.

    Check: The wall closes and the LiveView Mix tab is shown again.

  • Paging: when there are more tiles than the layout holds, the wall is divided into wall pages. The number of wall pages is the number of tiles divided by the tiles per page, rounded up. Positions that a wall page does not fill, and empty tiles, are black. With several wall pages, page dots appear at the bottom of the screen.
  • Opening page: the wall opens on the first wall page that has something to show. When a long wall begins with a run of tiles that point at cameras that do not exist, it does not stop on a page that consists only of status texts.
  • Streams: only the wall page that is being looked at plays; neighboring pages are not connected, which saves bandwidth. Keep cameras connected between pages changes this; see “LiveView Mix in Settings”.
  • Buttons over the picture: the close button, and the buttons over a camera opened from the wall, are large white symbols on a dark disc with a thin white ring, so they stay visible and can be hit reliably over a black or a bright picture.
  • Tapping a camera: opens the single-camera view of that camera; see “Opening a single camera”.
  • Tapping a YouTube or Twitch tile: opens that stream full screen; see “YouTube and Twitch streams on the wall”.
  • Tapping a button of a control panel: sends the request. When the button is set to ask for confirmation first, a confirmation dialog appears; see Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
  • Status texts: a tile that cannot be shown keeps its position and shows a status text; tapping it does nothing. See “When a tile cannot show a camera”.
  • The wall cannot be rearranged by dragging. To adjust the tiles, return to Arrange; see “Arranging the wall and its tiles”.
  • Turning the device: with the portrait page switched on, the wall changes between the landscape page and the portrait page as the device turns; see “The portrait page”. On an iPhone Duo with two canvases, see “Two canvases on iPhone Duo”.
  • Screen: while live pictures are on the wall, the device does not lock the screen automatically.
  • Nothing to show: when there are no tiles at all, the screen shows LiveView Mix is empty. When every tile points at a camera that is not on this device (for example after a restore from a backup before any device was added), the screen shows These cameras aren't set up here.

Opening a single camera

Tapping a camera on the wall or in the preview opens a large picture of that camera. The two entry points open different screens. A YouTube or Twitch tile opens its own full-screen view instead; see “YouTube and Twitch streams on the wall”.

From the full-screen wall

The screen is the single-camera view of that camera, always playing in HD. In the top-left corner are the back button ‹ (Back) and the camera name. When the device supports recording playback, the Recordings button (a clock icon) is in the top-right corner. When the camera supports PTZ, a PTZ pad is in the bottom-right corner. When the picture carries sound, a speaker button (Mute, Unmute) is in the bottom-left corner. This view has no SD and HD switch and no black-bar switch.

  1. On the full-screen wall, tap the picture of a camera.

    Check: The screen changes to the single-camera view of that camera.

  2. Spread two fingers apart on the picture.

    Check: The picture is enlarged, up to 5 times. While it is enlarged, dragging with one finger moves the picture.

  3. Double-tap the picture.

    Check: The picture is enlarged to 2 times; another double-tap returns it to its original size.

  4. When the device supports recording playback, tap Recordings in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen opens the picture and the recording playback of that camera, with Done in the top-right corner. For the operation, see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view” and Chapter 7, “Recording playback and speed”.

  5. Tap the back button ‹ in the top-left corner.

    Check: The screen shows the full-screen wall again. A camera head that is still turning stops. For PTZ control, see “PTZ control: moving the camera”.

From the preview

The screen is the full-screen viewer: one camera at a time, and swiping left or right changes to the next camera. The cameras that can be reached are those in the preview that can play (online, within the plan and not paused), in the same order as on the wall. Page dots are at the bottom of the screen.

  • ✕ (Close): closes the viewer and returns to the preview.
  • The camera name is at the top center.
  • The HD / SD button in the top-right corner switches the quality; the text on the button is the current quality. The viewer always opens in HD, and a switch applies to the current viewing only and is not saved.
  • The black-bar button in the top-right corner switches between Default and Stretch to fill, again for the current viewing only. When the black-bar setting of the wall is anything other than Default, the viewer starts on Stretch to fill.
  • The speaker button in the bottom-left corner appears only when the picture carries sound.

Tapping a camera in the preview that the plan does not cover (Not in your plan) opens the plans page; see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”. Tapping a camera that is offline, disabled or paused does nothing. Sound plays only in the single-camera view and in this full-screen viewer; for switching it on, see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view”.

YouTube and Twitch streams on the wall

A YouTube live stream or a Twitch channel that has been added to Cam Hub (see “Adding YouTube live streams and Twitch channels” and “YouTube and Twitch streams”) can be placed in a tile like a camera, through Choose Cameras or Put a camera here.

  • The tile plays the stream in the site's own player, without sound, so several tiles never compete for sound.
  • Tapping the tile, in the preview or on the full-screen wall, opens the stream as large as the screen allows; the picture carries on without loading the stream again. The site's own controls work there, and the ✕ button (Close) and a speaker button (Mute, Unmute) sit beside the picture, never over it. The speaker button follows the same sound switch as the cameras.
  • The stream has no SD and HD setting; its quality follows the size of the tile, and the full-screen view plays it at the size of the screen.
  • The stream is always shown whole, with black bars where its shape differs from the tile. Black bars on this wall applies to cameras only, because the site's own player may not be cropped.
  • Until the terms of the site have been agreed on this device, the tile shows the stream name and Agree to YouTube's terms to play this stream. or Agree to Twitch's terms to play this channel. Tapping the tile opens the full-screen view with Review Terms…; after Agree and Continue, the stream plays.
  • Where YouTube and Twitch are not available, a stream that arrives in a share code or a backup shows its name and Not available in this region or language.
  • YouTube and Twitch streams never count toward the plan and are never locked.
  • On Apple TV, these tiles show the stream name only; see “Differences on Apple TV”.

When a tile cannot show a camera

A camera that cannot be shown keeps its position on the wall, and its tile shows a dark plate with a status text. Because the position is kept, no other tile moves.

DisplayMeaningWhat to do
No signalThe device reports the channel as offline.Check the power and the network of the camera; see Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.
DisabledThe channel has not been enabled.Enable the channel on the device page or in Settings › Choose which cameras to show; see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”.
Not in your planThe channel is enabled but exceeds the allowance of the current plan.See “How plan limits affect the wall” and Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
PausedThe channel was paused with Pause Video; the tile shows a gray plate.Resume it with Resume Video on the device page; see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”.
Camera removedThe tile points at a camera that Cam Hub no longer has.Handle it with Empty Those Slots on the Choose Cameras page; see “Choosing cameras and quality”.
  • While a tile is connecting, it shows a spinning circle. When the connection fails, the tile explains the reason in a short text; a temporary failure is retried automatically.
  • While Keep cameras connected between pages is off, a tile first shows only the camera name at the moment its wall page comes into view, and the picture follows.
  • Hide offline cameras in Settings applies to the walls of the Live tab only. It does not remove tiles from LiveView Mix.
  • Deleting a device in the app empties the tiles that belong to it, on every wall. No other tile moves, and control panels keep their places too.

How plan limits affect the wall

LiveView Mix itself does not limit the number of cameras on the wall. The number of channels that can show a picture at the same time is decided by the plan; for the details of the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

  • Free plan: at most 2 enabled channels across the whole app (single cameras and recorder channels together), and at most 1 recorder. A channel beyond the allowance shows Disabled on the wall; a channel that is enabled but exceeds the allowance shows Not in your plan. In both cases, the position of the tile is kept.
  • Camera plans and recorder plans: these raise the number of single cameras that can be enabled and the number of recorders, respectively. With a recorder plan, all channels of the subscribed recorders can be used.
  • Enabling channels: after a plan is upgraded, channels that were disabled are not enabled automatically; they must be switched on on the device page or in Settings › Choose which cameras to show. A plan with no limit on either axis enables all channels automatically, and Choose which cameras to show is then not shown in Settings.
  • Control panels use the camera allowance, after the cameras: each control panel counts as one single camera against the camera allowance of the plan, and not against the recorder allowance. Panels only use what the cameras leave of that allowance (on the Free plan, what the cameras and recorder channels leave), so a control panel never takes a picture away from a camera. When the allowance is used up, the control panel stays in place, but its buttons are locked and the tile shows a lock, the panel title and Not in your plan. Pictures, clocks and labels do not use the allowance.
  • Each panel on each wall counts: the control panels of the landscape page always count; those of the portrait page count while it is switched on, and those of the lower canvas while the two canvases of an iPhone Duo are switched on. A panel copied to the other page counts on its own. Panels are covered in the order landscape page, lower canvas, portrait page, each wall in tile order.
  • YouTube and Twitch streams: never count toward the plan and are never locked.
  • Locked channels: tapping a camera in the preview that the plan does not cover opens the plans page. On the Choose Cameras page and on the arrange canvas, these channels show no live picture.
  • Custom layouts: at most 8 × 8, which is 64 tiles; see “Drawing a custom layout”.

LiveView Mix in Settings

Path: Settings › LiveView Mix. The LiveView Mix section lists one row per wall, each with the number of selected cameras at its end (6 cameras), or Not set up before setup:

  • LiveView Mix: the wall. While the portrait page is switched on, this row is called Landscape page; on an iPhone Duo with two canvases, Upper canvas.
  • Portrait page: shown while the portrait page is switched on.
  • Lower canvas: shown on an iPhone Duo while the two canvases are switched on.

Tapping a row opens a page that holds the camera selection, the full-screen layout, the watermark and paging of that wall on one page. The options work as described in the sections above. Cancel in the top-left corner restores everything changed since the page was entered, and Done in the top-right corner keeps the changes.

Below the LiveView Mix section, the Portrait page switch has a section of its own (see “The portrait page”), and on an iPhone Duo, so does the Two canvases switch (see “Two canvases on iPhone Duo”). Both are off by default.

Open on launch

Open on launch decides which screen the app shows when it starts:

  • Last viewed (the default).
  • LiveView Mix: opens the LiveView Mix tab.
  • LiveView Mix Full Screen: opens the LiveView Mix tab and goes straight into the full-screen wall after the start, once. Tapping ✕ returns to the preview in the tab.
  • Each device: opens the Live tab and shows that device.

The options LiveView Mix and LiveView Mix Full Screen appear only after the wall has been set up, or while the portrait page or the two canvases are switched on.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen and scroll to the LiveView Mix section.

    Check: The screen shows the LiveView Mix row and the Open on launch menu.

  2. Tap Open on launch.

    Check: The screen shows the list of options, with the current option ticked.

  3. Select LiveView Mix Full Screen.

    Check: The menu shows LiveView Mix Full Screen. The next time the app starts, it goes straight into the full-screen wall.

Keep cameras connected between pages

Keep cameras connected between pages in the Paging section is off by default. When it is on, wall pages that are not being looked at stay connected, so the picture appears at once when swiping instead of a black tile while the camera reconnects. The cost is more bandwidth and battery; the effect is largest for recorders that sign in with a session. At most 12 streams are kept. When the switch is turned off, the kept connections are closed at once. The switch applies to the streams of the whole app.

  1. On the Adjust the Layout page, scroll down to the Paging section.

    Check: The screen shows the Keep cameras connected between pages switch with its explanation.

  2. Switch on Keep cameras connected between pages.

    Check: The switch is on.

Backup and restore

The settings of every wall (the landscape page, the portrait page and the lower canvas, each with its cameras and tiles, layout, custom layout, watermark, control panels and pictures), the portrait page and two canvases switches and the arrangement of the preview belong to the app settings and are stored with an iCloud backup (see “Several named backups: renaming and deleting”); when cameras are exported, switching on Include app settings carries them along as well. On restore, tiles that belong to a device that does not exist on the new device are not kept. Pictures make a backup larger, and a picture copied to the other page counts twice. For the procedure, see Chapter 10, “Sharing and backup”.

Differences on Apple TV

Apple TV shows a wall that was built on an iPhone or an iPad. Arranging the wall, editing its tiles and drawing a custom layout are done on the iPhone or iPad; see Chapter 14, “Apple TV”. Apple TV shows the landscape page only: the portrait page and the lower canvas of an iPhone Duo are not shown, and their control panels do not count toward the plan there. YouTube and Twitch tiles show the stream name with the note that these streams play only on iPhone and iPad.

9Control panels and webhooks

A control panel is a tile on a LiveView Mix wall that holds a row of buttons. Each button sends an HTTP request to an address of choice when pressed, which suits a Home Assistant webhook or service call, a relay board, Node-RED, or any other HTTP service the phone can reach. The same buttons can also be pressed on an Apple Watch.

What a control panel does

A control panel consists of a title, a number of buttons and an optional clock. Each button stores one complete HTTP request: method, URL, headers and body. When a button is pressed, the request goes directly from this iPhone, iPad or Apple TV to the address, without passing through a Cam Hub server. A button pressed on an Apple Watch is sent by the watch itself or through the paired iPhone; see “Buttons on Apple Watch”.

  • Cam Hub only sends the request. The URL and the content are entirely the choice of the user. Cam Hub does not check what kind of service answers, and it is not a dedicated controller for any smart-home product.
  • A request is sent only when a button is pressed on the wall or on the watch. Tapping a panel on the arrange screen opens its editor and sends nothing.
  • Control panels are created and edited on iPhone and iPad. Apple TV displays and runs the panels of the landscape page; see “How a panel looks on the wall”. Apple Watch shows their buttons; see “Buttons on Apple Watch”.
A control panel uses one camera allowance

Each control panel uses one camera allowance of the plan, from what the cameras leave of it, so a panel never takes a picture away from a camera. When the allowance is not sufficient, the panel is locked and its buttons are unavailable, on the wall and on the watch. For details, see “How plan limits affect the wall” and “What uses allowance”.

Adding a control panel to the wall

Prerequisite: LiveView Mix has been set up and the wall holds at least one camera; for the setup, see “Building a first wall of six cameras”. While it has not been set up, Arrange the wall can also be reached through Settings › LiveView Mix as soon as a device has been added. A control panel can be placed on the landscape page, on the portrait page or on either canvas of an iPhone Duo; the steps are the same.

  1. Tap the LiveView Mix tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the preview wall, with three buttons in the top-right corner.

  2. Tap the Adjust the Layout button, the rightmost of the three buttons in the top-right corner.

    Check: The Adjust the Layout page opens.

  3. Tap Arrange the wall.

    Check: The Arrange page opens: the canvas of the wall is at the top, and the Order list below it lists every filled tile under its number.

  4. Tap an unused tile on the canvas, shown with a dashed outline and a +. When the unused tiles are on another wall page, use the arrows below the canvas or swipe sideways first.

    Check: A menu titled with the tile number appears, for example Slot 9.

  5. Tap Picture, control panel, clock or label….

    Check: The editor of the tile opens from the bottom of the screen, titled Slot 9. The first row is Shows, and its current value is Empty.

  6. Tap Shows and select Control in the menu.

    Check: The page shows the three sections Template, Panel and Buttons. The template is Gate / Shutter, the panel title is Gate (in the language of the app), and the button section holds three buttons, each with No endpoint set in orange below it.

  7. Tap Template and select the closest type.

    Check: The button section is replaced by the default buttons of that template. For the content of the templates, see “Templates”.

  8. In the Panel section, enter the name of the panel in the Title field.

    Check: The field shows the name, which is later displayed above the buttons of the panel.

  9. Optional: tap Color and select the color of the border and the buttons.

    Check: The color icon shows the selected color. The default is cyan.

  10. Optional: turn on Show the time.

    Check: Four switches appear: Seconds, Date, Day of the week and 24-hour. The clock is shown in the space below the buttons.

  11. Set the URL and the content of every button as described in “Setting up a button”.

    Check: Every row of the button section shows the host name of the URL below its label, instead of No endpoint set.

  12. Tap Done in the top-right corner of the tile editor.

    Check: The screen returns to the Arrange page, and the tile on the canvas shows the panel as it appears on the wall.

  13. Tap Done in the top-right corner of the Arrange page.

    Check: The screen returns to the Adjust the Layout page.

  14. Tap Done in the top-right corner of the Adjust the Layout page.

    Check: The screen returns to the LiveView Mix tab, and the preview wall shows the new control panel.

  • When every tile of the layout is filled, the canvas shows no unused tile. Select a layout with more tiles in the layout row at the top of the Arrange page, or empty a tile, first; see “Arranging the wall and its tiles”.
  • A panel that already exists on the other page can be copied instead of being built again; see “The portrait page”. A panel on another wall page can be moved into an empty tile; see “Moving a tile into an empty tile”.
  • Tapping Cancel in the top-left corner of the tile editor restores the whole wall to the state it had when the editor was opened, including every change to the buttons.
  • Changing Shows to another item clears the title and all buttons of the panel. To remove the panel, set Shows to Empty, or swipe its row to the left in the Order list on the Arrange page and tap Delete. Either way the tile becomes empty and no other tile moves.
  • For picture, clock and label tiles, see “What a tile can show besides a camera”.
  • When Arrange the wall is reached through Settings › LiveView Mix, the operation that follows is the same.

Templates

The Template menu offers eleven templates. A template only determines the default title, the number of buttons, their icons and the initial setting of Confirm before firing. No template contains a URL; every button needs its own URL.

TemplateDefault titleDefault buttonsButtons with “Confirm before firing” on by default
Gate / ShutterGateOpen, Stop, CloseOpen
Garage DoorGarageOpen, Stop, CloseOpen
LightLightOn, OffNone
Door LockDoorUnlock, LockUnlock
Curtain / BlindCurtainOpen, Stop, CloseNone
Scene / AutomationSceneRunNone
Alarm / SirenAlarmArm, Disarm, PanicArm, Panic
FanFanOn, OffNone
Smart PlugPlugOn, OffNone
Air ConditionerAir ConditionerOn, OffNone
CustomEmptyOne button labeled ButtonNone
  • The default title and button labels of a template appear in the language of the app, and they follow it when the language of the app is changed later, on the wall, in the editor and on the Apple Watch. A title or label that has been typed or edited stays exactly as it was typed. Default words of panels made earlier are recognized in every language of the app and follow the current language as well.
  • Changing the template replaces all existing buttons with those of the new template, and the URLs, headers and content already entered are cleared with them. The title is replaced only when it is still empty or still a default title; a title typed by the user stays unchanged. Select the template first, then adjust the details.
  • The initial template of a newly added control panel is Gate / Shutter.

The settings of a panel

ItemDescription
ShowsThe content of the tile: Empty, Image, Control, Clock or Label. Selecting Control turns the tile into a control panel.
TemplateSee “Templates”.
TitleShown above the buttons, to say what the panel controls, and used as the group heading on the Apple Watch. When empty, no title is shown.
ColorThe color of the border and of the buttons of the panel, also used for the icons on the Apple Watch.
Show the timeShows the current time in the space below the buttons. When on, Seconds, Date, Day of the week and 24-hour can be selected. Names of days and months follow the language of the app.
ButtonsThe list of buttons. Tap a row to edit that button, swipe a row to the left to delete it, and tap Add Button to add a blank button at the end. The list cannot be reordered; to change the sequence, delete a button and add it again. Each row shows the icon, the label and the host name of the URL; while no valid URL is entered, No endpoint set is shown in orange instead. When the label is empty, the row shows Button.

Setting up a button

Prerequisite: the editor of the tile is open as described in “Adding a control panel to the wall”, and Control is selected.

  1. In the Buttons section, tap the button to set up. To create a new button, tap Add Button first, then tap the new row.

    Check: The screen shows the editor of that button. Its title is the label of the button, and the top-left corner holds only a back arrow.

  2. In the row of icons below the Icon row, tap the icon to use, or type the name of an SF Symbols icon in the field on the right.

    Check: The Icon row shows the selected icon and its name, for example arrow.up.to.line.

  3. Enter the text to show below the icon in the Label field.

    Check: The field shows the text. The title of the page changes to the same text.

  4. For a button that must be confirmed before it runs, turn on Confirm before firing.

    Check: The switch is on. A confirmation box now appears when the button is pressed, on the wall and on the watch; see “Pressing a button and reading the result”.

  5. In the Request section, select GET, POST, PUT or DELETE in the Method menu.

    Check: The menu shows the selected method. With GET, the Body section is absent from the lower part of the page; the other three methods show it.

  6. Enter the complete URL in the field below Method, beginning with http:// or https://.

    Check: The field shows the URL.

  7. On an iPhone, optional: in the Apple Watch section, tap How it is sent and select Automatic, Watch directly or Through iPhone.

    Check: The menu shows the choice, and the note below it explains what the choice does. For the meaning of each choice, see “Buttons on Apple Watch”.

  8. When a header is needed, tap Add Header and enter the name and the value of the header in the Name and Value fields.

    Check: The Headers section gains a row, and both fields show the text entered. Repeat the step for further headers; swipe a row to the left to delete the header.

  9. When content must be sent, confirm the content type in the upper field of the Body section (application/json by default), then enter the content in the text box below it.

    Check: The text box shows the content. The content is sent exactly as typed.

  10. Tap the back arrow in the top-left corner.

    Check: The screen returns to the tile editor, and the row of the button shows the host name of the URL below its label.

FieldDescription
IconTwenty common icons below the row can be tapped directly. The name of any SF Symbols icon can be typed as well.
LabelShown below the icon, and used as the text of the red button in the confirmation box. When the label is empty, the button shows only the icon, and the red button of the confirmation box reads Confirm.
Confirm before firingWhen on, pressing the button first opens a confirmation box. Buttons that make physical equipment move, such as opening a door, unlocking and alarms, should have it on.
MethodGET, POST, PUT or DELETE; the default is POST. GET sends no body.
URLMust begin with http:// or https:// and contain a host name or address. Spaces at the beginning and the end are ignored. Query parameters are written in the URL itself. When the URL is empty or malformed, pressing the button shows a failure, and the button does not appear on the Apple Watch.
How it is sentShown on an iPhone only, in the Apple Watch section. Decides whether a press on the watch is sent by the watch itself or through the iPhone; the default is Automatic. See “Buttons on Apple Watch”.
HeadersAny number of names and values. Rows with an empty name are skipped. A Content-Type header entered here takes precedence over the content type field of the Body section.
BodyShown only for POST, PUT and DELETE. The upper field is the content type, application/json by default; the text box below it is the content. An empty content sends no body. The value of the content type field is attached only when the content is not empty and no Content-Type header has been entered.

Pressing a button and reading the result

Buttons can be pressed on the preview wall of the LiveView Mix tab and on the full-screen wall. A newly configured button has no separate test function; pressing it once serves as the test, followed by a check on the receiving side that the request arrived.

  1. On the preview wall or the full-screen wall, tap a button of the panel.

    Check: A button without Confirm before firing changes its icon to a spinner immediately, which means that the request has been sent. A button with it on opens a confirmation box beside the panel, titled with the panel title (or Run this action? when the panel has no title).

  2. When the confirmation box appears, tap the red button in it, which carries the label of the pressed button. To cancel, tap anywhere outside the box.

    Check: The box closes and the icon changes to a spinner. When canceled, no request is sent.

  3. Watch the icon of the button.

    Check: Depending on the result, the icon changes to a green check mark or an orange warning triangle, and returns to the original icon after about 1.6 seconds.

The button showsMeaning
The configured iconIdle, or the result has been displayed.
A spinnerThe request has been sent and the answer is awaited. When no answer arrives within 10 seconds, the request counts as failed.
A green check markThe receiving side answered with a status code from 200 to 299. Redirects are followed automatically, and the final answer decides.
An orange warning triangleThe request did not succeed. The cause can be an empty or malformed URL, no connection, a timeout, an untrusted certificate, or a status code outside 200 to 299, for example 401, 404 or 500. The screen does not show the cause, and no log is kept.
  • A green check mark only means that the receiving side answered successfully. It does not prove that the equipment moved. To verify the outcome, look at the log of the receiving side.
  • Every press sends one request, and nothing prevents repeated presses. Pressing twice in a row sends two requests. Buttons that make physical equipment move should have Confirm before firing on.
  • When the orange triangle appears repeatedly, check in this order: whether the URL is valid, whether the phone and the receiving side are on the same network or can reach each other, and whether the address of the receiving side can be resolved. When the receiving side is on the local network, Cam Hub must be allowed to access the local network; see “Finding devices with the network scan”. For other problems, see Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.
  • For pressing buttons on an Apple Watch, see “Buttons on Apple Watch”.

How a panel looks on the wall

  • Button layout: 1 button is placed in 1 column, 2 buttons in 2 columns, 3 buttons in 3 columns, 4 buttons as 2 × 2, and 5 or more buttons in 3 columns.
  • Small tiles: the panel shrinks automatically. The clock is hidden first, then the labels below the icons; the title and the icons remain.
  • Plan: each control panel uses one camera allowance, from what the cameras leave of it. A panel beyond the allowance shows a lock, its title and Not in your plan, and its buttons are unavailable; on the preview, the tile shows a lock and Not in your plan. Each panel on each wall counts on its own: the landscape page always, the portrait page while it is switched on and the lower canvas of an iPhone Duo while the two canvases are switched on; a copied panel counts separately from its original. Clock, label, picture and empty tiles use no allowance. A subscription to an NVR plan alone does not raise the allowance available to panels. For the counting rules, see “How plan limits affect the wall” and “What uses allowance”.
  • Apple TV: a panel is created on an iPhone or an iPad, and the panels of the landscape page are shown on the wall of the Apple TV; see Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.
  • Apple Watch: the buttons of every panel that the plan covers appear on the paired Apple Watch; see “Buttons on Apple Watch”.
  • Backup and sharing: the settings of a panel, including the values of headers, belong to the app settings. They enter every iCloud backup, and they also enter a sharing code when Include app settings is on during export; see Chapter 10, “Sharing and backup”.

Buttons on Apple Watch

Cam Hub on Apple Watch shows the buttons of the control panels that are set up on the paired iPhone, and fires a button with one tap. It shows nothing else: no video and no cameras. The watch app has no settings, sign-in or purchase of its own; the iPhone decides which buttons it shows.

  • Which buttons: every button with a valid URL, of every control panel that the plan covers: the landscape page, the portrait page while it is switched on, and the lower canvas of an iPhone Duo while the two canvases are switched on. A button of the portrait page that is identical to one on the landscape page (same panel title, label and request) is listed once.
  • The list: the screen is titled Controls. Buttons are grouped under the titles of their panels, in the order of the wall. Each row shows the icon in the color of the panel and the label of the button (the URL when the label is empty).
  • Keeping in step: when a panel or a button is changed on the iPhone, or the plan changes, the iPhone sends the watch a new list. A panel that the plan no longer covers disappears from the watch.
  • Working on its own: the list is kept on the watch. The watch app opens and shows it even when the iPhone app is not running or the iPhone is out of reach; buttons that the watch may send itself still work then.
  • Language: the watch shows its texts and the default words of the panels in the language of the iPhone app, not the language of the watch.
  • Before the first buttons arrive: the watch shows No buttons yet with a note that the buttons of a control panel added to LiveView Mix on the iPhone appear there.

How a press is sent

Each button has its own choice under How it is sent in the button editor on the iPhone (see “Setting up a button”):

ChoiceWhat happens on a press
Automatic (default)A public address is sent straight from the watch. A home-network or VPN address, for example 192.168.x.x or a name ending in .local, goes through the iPhone first, which can reach it.
Watch directlyThe watch always sends the request itself, over its own Wi-Fi or cellular connection or over the connection of the iPhone. This is the fastest way, but a home-network or VPN address may be out of reach of the watch.
Through iPhoneFor a server that can only be reached through a VPN on the iPhone, especially when its address looks public: the watch has no VPN of its own. The watch sends the request itself only when the iPhone is out of reach.
  • When a press goes through the iPhone, the watch first checks that the iPhone answers, waiting up to about 6 seconds; the iPhone app can be started in the background for this. The iPhone then sends the request in the same way as its wall does, after checking that the plan still covers the panel.
  • When the iPhone does not answer that check, the watch sends the request itself. When the iPhone took the request but its answer was lost, the press is shown as failed and is not sent again, so a switch is never toggled twice.
  • A request that the watch sent itself and that failed is not repeated through the iPhone. A request from the watch to a home-network address only works while the watch is on the same Wi-Fi network.

Pressing a button on the watch

Prerequisite: Cam Hub is installed on the Apple Watch that is paired with the iPhone, and at least one control panel with a valid URL is on the wall.

  1. Open Cam Hub on the Apple Watch.

    Check: The watch shows Controls and the buttons, grouped by panel.

  2. Tap a button.

    Check: A button without Confirm before firing shows a spinner at the end of its row at once. A button with it on asks Run this action?, with the panel title below, a red button carrying the label of the button and Cancel.

  3. When the question appears, tap the red button. To cancel, tap Cancel.

    Check: The question closes and the row shows a spinner. When canceled, nothing is sent.

  4. Watch the end of the row.

    Check: A green check mark means that the endpoint answered successfully; a red warning triangle means that the request did not succeed. The watch taps the wrist as well, and the row returns to normal after about 2.5 seconds.

A tap on a button that is still sending is ignored, so an impatient second tap does not send the request twice. As on the wall, a green check mark only means that the receiving side answered; it does not prove that the equipment moved.

Using Home Assistant

The following two approaches use Home Assistant as the example. The address homeassistant.local, the identifier gate-open-7f3c9a21 and the entity name cover.gate are sample values and must be replaced with the real ones. The behavior on the Home Assistant side is defined by its own documentation and can change between versions.

Prerequisites: Home Assistant runs on the home network and the phone can reach its address; a tile of the LiveView Mix wall has Control selected (see “Adding a control panel to the wall”). Home Assistant uses http and port 8123 by default. The sample text in the URL field of the app begins with https and must be changed to match the real setup.

Approach 1: webhook trigger (no token needed)

  1. In Home Assistant, create a new automation.

    Check: The screen shows the editor of the automation.

  2. Select Webhook as the trigger and enter an identifier that is hard to guess, for example gate-open-7f3c9a21.

    Check: The editor shows the identifier. The identifier works like a password: anyone who knows it and the address can start the automation.

  3. Set the action, for example the entity that opens the gate, and save the automation.

    Check: The automation appears in the list of automations of Home Assistant.

  4. In Cam Hub, open the editor of the button to use, as described in step 1 of “Setting up a button”.

    Check: The screen shows the editor of that button.

  5. Select POST as the Method and enter http://homeassistant.local:8123/api/webhook/gate-open-7f3c9a21 in the URL field. Headers and body can stay empty.

    Check: The field shows the URL, and after returning, the row of the button shows the host name homeassistant.local.

  6. Return to the wall and press the button.

    Check: The icon shows a spinner first, then a green check mark.

  7. In Home Assistant, open the run log of the automation.

    Check: The log shows the run that the press started. Home Assistant can also answer successfully for an identifier that does not exist, so the run log decides, not the green check mark.

The equivalent request is:

POST /api/webhook/gate-open-7f3c9a21 HTTP/1.1
Host: homeassistant.local:8123

The automation can also be written as a configuration file. The following example is for comparison only, and the syntax depends on the version of Home Assistant:

triggers:
  - trigger: webhook
    webhook_id: gate-open-7f3c9a21
    allowed_methods:
      - POST
    local_only: true
actions:
  - action: cover.open_cover
    target:
      entity_id: cover.gate

A webhook trigger accepts only POST and PUT by default, and by default only requests from the local network. Using it from an outside network needs separate measures; see “Security notes”. A button pressed on an Apple Watch reaches an address such as homeassistant.local through the iPhone when How it is sent is Automatic or Through iPhone; see “Buttons on Apple Watch”.

Approach 2: service call (token needed)

  1. On the profile page of Home Assistant, create a long-lived access token and copy it immediately.

    Check: The screen shows the token. A token is usually displayed in full only once, when it is created.

  2. In Cam Hub, open the editor of the button, select POST as the Method and enter http://homeassistant.local:8123/api/services/cover/open_cover in the URL field.

    Check: The field shows the URL.

  3. Tap Add Header.

    Check: The Headers section gains a row with the two fields Name and Value.

  4. Enter Authorization in the Name field, and Bearer, a space and the copied token in the Value field.

    Check: Both fields show the text entered. The value of the header is displayed in plain text.

  5. In the Body section, confirm that the content type is application/json and enter {"entity_id":"cover.gate"} in the text box.

    Check: The text box shows the content.

  6. Return to the wall and press the button.

    Check: The icon shows a spinner first, then a green check mark. The log of Home Assistant shows that the service was called.

The equivalent request is:

POST /api/services/cover/open_cover HTTP/1.1
Host: homeassistant.local:8123
Authorization: Bearer <long-lived access token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"entity_id":"cover.gate"}
Prefer the webhook trigger

When a webhook identifier leaks, the effect is limited to the one automation it belongs to. A long-lived access token can operate the whole of Home Assistant. For any action that approach 1 can perform, use approach 1.

Security notes

TopicDescription and recommendation
HTTP and HTTPSA request sent with http:// is not encrypted. Anyone on the same network path can read the URL, the token in a header and the body. Use HTTP only inside a trusted home network and for webhooks that carry no sensitive data. Whenever a request carries a token or leaves the home network, use https://.
HTTPS certificatesCam Hub has no option to trust a self-signed certificate. An https:// address with a self-signed certificate fails, and the button shows the orange triangle. Inside the local network, http:// can be used instead, or a certificate that the phone trusts can be installed on the receiving side.
Storage of tokens and identifiersThe values of headers are displayed in plain text in the editor and are stored in plain text in the app settings of this device.
Apple WatchThe buttons that reach the watch carry their whole request, including the URL, the headers and the body. They are copied to the paired Apple Watch and kept there, so a token in a header is stored on the watch as well.
Backups and sharing codesThe settings of a panel enter every iCloud backup, and every sharing code exported with Include app settings on. Treat such a code like a password and lock it with a PIN or a password; see “Locking a code”. When a token has been exposed, revoke it on the receiving side and create a new one.
Outside networksOpening port 8123 of Home Assistant directly to the internet is not recommended. When away from home, use a VPN or the official remote-access method of Home Assistant, and change the URL to the matching address.
Physical actionsTurn on Confirm before firing for buttons that open doors, unlock and sound alarms. Cam Hub has no further lock on panel buttons; anyone who can operate the unlocked device, or the watch, can press them.
Name resolutionNames ending in .local may not resolve on some networks. When connections fail, enter the fixed IP address of the receiving side instead.

10Sharing and backup

Devices with their passwords, and optionally the app settings (LiveView Mix pages and control panels), can be moved to another device or shared with other people as an encrypted code, or backed up to iCloud as several named backups and restored on one's own iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.

Comparing the two methods

TopicSharing codeiCloud backup
WhereSettings › Export Cameras and Settings › Import Cameras, in the Share Cameras sectionSettings › Back Up to iCloud and Settings › Restore from iCloud, in the Backup & Restore section
iCloud neededNo. The code travels by any means the user chooses.Yes. Both devices must be signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account.
Choice of devicesThe devices to export can be ticked.All devices.
App settingsOptional; included only when Include app settings is on, and applied only when the recipient agrees.Always included.
Copies keptEach export produces a separate code.My Backup keeps several backups, each with an optional name; the Apple TV destination keeps one copy.
LockNo lock, a six-digit PIN, or a password.No PIN. Encrypted with a key built into the app.
Devices that can use itCam Hub of other people, and one's own iPhone and iPad. Apple TV can only import.One's own iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.
Typical useSharing with other people, or two devices that do not share an Apple Account.Changing phones, keeping earlier states of the setup, or bringing the settings to Apple TV.

Exporting cameras (creating a code)

Prerequisite: at least one device has been added. While there is no device, Export Cameras is unavailable.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings list.

  2. In the Share Cameras section, tap Export Cameras.

    Check: The Export Cameras page opens: the Devices to export list (all ticked by default), Lock with a PIN, Include app settings, and a button such as Export 5 devices.

  3. Optional: tap a device row to clear or restore its tick. The Deselect all button at the right of the list title clears every tick.

    Check: The button shows the number of selected devices, for example Export 3 devices. While no device is selected, the button is unavailable and the button at the right of the list title reads Select all.

  4. Optional: turn on Include app settings.

    Check: The switch is on, and the explanation below it changes to say that the code also carries the app settings, the same as restoring from iCloud. For the items carried, see “What backups and codes contain”.

  5. Optional: set the lock as described in “Locking a code”.

    Check: After a lock has been set, Export 3 devices stays unavailable until the entry is complete. Without a lock, the code is open: anyone who has the code and Cam Hub can import it.

  6. Tap the export button, for example Export 3 devices.

    Check: The result page opens with the title Export Cameras. Its top part explains that the code contains the cameras and their passwords, encrypted. For an open code it adds, with an orange mark, that anyone with the code and Cam Hub can add them; for a locked code it reminds that the PIN or password must be sent separately. Below are the buttons Share and Copy, and below those the full text of the code.

  7. Tap Share and select a way to send, or tap Copy.

    Check: Tapping Share opens the system share sheet, with options such as Messages, Mail or AirDrop. Tapping Copy changes the button to Copied, and the complete text of the code is on the clipboard.

  8. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The result page closes and the Export Cameras page is shown again.

  • Share sends a link, Copy copies text. Share sends a link that begins with https://cam-hub.almx.cc/i#, with the code after the “#”, which browsers do not send to the web server. Copy places the complete text on the clipboard.
  • The recipient: when Cam Hub is installed, opening the link opens the import page directly with the code filled in. When it is not installed, the link opens a web page that points to the download page of the app and shows the code for copying.
  • The text of the code begins with a short English explanation and the install address, followed by the code, which begins with CAMHUB1:, CAMHUB1L: or CAMHUB2: and can be thousands of characters long. When importing, the whole text can be pasted, or the code alone.
  • A code contains the passwords of the devices. A code does not expire, and deleting the devices or the app on the source device does not invalidate a code that has already been shared. When a code may have been exposed, change the passwords of the devices concerned.
A code hands over the passwords of the devices

Anyone who obtains a code without a lock and has Cam Hub can import every device in it with its password. Send the code only to people who are trusted, and set a lock when needed.

Locking a code

A code can be open, locked with a six-digit PIN, or locked with a password (Complex encryption). The strength of the protection differs greatly between the three, and the choice depends on how the code is sent.

TopicOpenSix-digit PINPassword (complex encryption)
How to setBoth switches stay off (default)Turn on Lock with a PINTurn on Lock with a PIN, then turn on Complex encryption
What to enterNothingSix digits, on the numeric keypad8 characters or more, any characters, on the full keyboard, entered twice
The code begins withCAMHUB1:CAMHUB1L:CAMHUB2:
When importingImports directlyThe Enter PIN dialog appearsThe Enter Password dialog appears
StrengthThe encryption key is built into the app, so any Cam Hub of the same version can open the code. It only keeps the contents from being read at a glance. It does not protect against anyone who has both the code and the app.Encrypted with the PIN, using PBKDF2 (600,000 rounds) and AES-256-GCM. A PIN has only a million possibilities, so someone who obtains the code can try them all offline on their own computer. It protects against casual access, not against a determined person.The same encryption, with the key derived from the password. Only a long password that is not used elsewhere makes guessing impractical.
Older appsImports with an app of the same versionImports with an app of the same versionAn older app that does not know the format shows Update Cam Hub and must be updated first

Locking with a six-digit PIN

  1. On the Export Cameras page, turn on Lock with a PIN.

    Check: The field PIN (6 digits) appears below the switch, and the explanation changes to say that whoever imports must enter this PIN and that it must be sent separately from the code.

  2. Enter six digits.

    Check: The field accepts digits only, the keypad closes after the sixth digit, and the export button becomes available. With fewer digits, the export button stays unavailable.

Locking with a password (complex encryption)

  1. On the Export Cameras page, turn on Lock with a PIN.

    Check: The Complex encryption switch and the PIN (6 digits) field appear.

  2. Turn on Complex encryption.

    Check: The PIN field is replaced by the two fields Password (8+ characters) and Confirm password, and anything typed earlier is cleared.

  3. Enter the password in the Password (8+ characters) field.

    Check: The field masks the characters with dots. Any letters, numbers and symbols can be used, and a longer password is stronger.

  4. Enter the same password again in the Confirm password field.

    Check: When both entries match and have at least 8 characters, the export button becomes available. When they differ, the orange text The two passwords don't match. appears below the field and the button stays unavailable.

  • Send the PIN or the password separately from the code, never in the same message.
  • A forgotten PIN or password cannot be recovered. Cam Hub does not store it and does not send it to the developer. When it is forgotten, export a new code.
  • A password is case-sensitive, and spaces count. The same accented letter typed on different keyboards is treated as identical.
  • When a code is placed somewhere that is not private, such as a chat group or an e-mail, lock it with a password and send the password by another channel.
  • The person who imports does not need to know in advance which lock was used. After the code is pasted, Cam Hub recognizes the lock itself and shows the matching prompt and keyboard; see “Importing cameras”.

Importing cameras

Where: Settings › Import Cameras, or directly by tapping a received sharing link.

Pasting a code

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings list.

  2. In the Share Cameras section, tap Import Cameras.

    Check: The Import Cameras page opens. The section title is Paste the code, with the buttons Paste and Import Cameras and a text box.

  3. Tap Paste. Alternatively, touch and hold in the text box and paste manually.

    Check: The code appears in the text box. When the code is locked, a lock note appears below the buttons: Locked with a 6-digit PIN — you'll be asked for it. or Locked with a password — you'll be asked for it. An open code shows no note.

  4. Tap Import Cameras.

    Check: An open code without app settings is imported directly, and the screen shows Added 3 cameras. An open code that carries app settings opens the dialog This code also has the sender's app settings. A locked code opens the Enter PIN dialog (numeric keypad, field 6 digits) or the Enter Password dialog (full keyboard).

  5. For a locked code, enter the PIN or the password and tap Import.

    Check: The dialog closes. A code without app settings is imported, and the screen shows Added 3 cameras. A code that carries app settings opens the dialog This code also has the sender's app settings.

  6. When the dialog This code also has the sender's app settings appears, tap Add Cameras Only or Also Use Their Settings.

    Check: The dialog explains that the LiveView Mix walls, language and other preferences of the sender would replace those of this device and that this cannot be undone. After either choice the screen shows Added 3 cameras. Add Cameras Only leaves the settings of this device as they are; Also Use Their Settings applies the settings of the code. Cancel closes the dialog and imports nothing.

  7. Tap Done.

    Check: The screen returns to the settings list, and the added devices appear in the Devices tab.

When Paste is tapped, the system can ask whether Cam Hub may paste from another app; allow it. Alternatively, touch and hold in the text box and paste with the edit menu.

Importing from a link

  1. On an iPhone or iPad that has Cam Hub, tap the received sharing link.

    Check: Cam Hub opens the Import Cameras page with the code already in the text box. For a locked code, the matching lock note is shown.

  2. Tap Import Cameras and, for a locked code, enter the PIN or the password.

    Check: The screen shows Added 3 cameras, or, for a code that carries app settings, the dialog This code also has the sender's app settings.

  3. If the dialog appears, tap Add Cameras Only or Also Use Their Settings.

    Check: The screen shows Added 3 cameras.

Message when importingMeaning and action
Added 3 camerasThe import is complete. The number is the number of imported devices; a recorder counts as one.
Wrong PINThe PIN is not correct. Ask the sender for the six digits, then tap Import Cameras again and re-enter it.
Wrong passwordThe password is not correct. Capitals, spaces and symbols must match exactly.
Update Cam HubThe code was made with a different version of Cam Hub, or it uses a format that this version does not know. Update the app on both devices and try again.
Couldn't read that codeThe pasted content is not a code, the code is incomplete, or it has been damaged. Make sure the whole code has been pasted.
The cameras could not be saved. Try again.The code itself was readable, but writing the devices failed. Try again.
  • Importing merges. A device that matches a device already on this device has its name, address, account, password and channels replaced by the contents of the code, and, when the code carries them, the SNMP settings of a NAS (see “Disk Health”); the other devices are added. Other devices already on this device are not deleted.
  • The enabled state of channels is checked against the plan of this device. When a plan is held, channels beyond its allowance are imported as Disabled. On the free plan, the enabled state is kept as it is in the code, and channels beyond the free allowance show Not in your plan and a lock until a plan covers them. For the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
  • App settings are applied only when the code was exported with Include app settings on and Also Use Their Settings is chosen. They then replace the matching settings on this device, including the LiveView Mix pages and the language. A tile that shows a camera not imported with the code becomes an empty tile, and every other tile keeps its place. With Add Cameras Only, or for a code without app settings, the settings of this device stay unchanged.
  • YouTube and Twitch streams in a code are imported like the other devices and use no plan allowance. Before the first stream of a service plays on this device, the terms of that service are shown for agreement; see “YouTube and Twitch streams”.

What backups and codes contain

ItemiCloud backupSharing code
