DevicesAll devices, including YouTube and Twitch streamsThe ticked devices, including YouTube and Twitch streams
Data of each deviceName, address, ports, username, password, connection method, model, serial number, firmware version, the position of the device in the list, and for a NAS the SNMP settings used by Disk Health (community name and port).
ChannelsChannel names and custom names, the enabled state, the paused state.
App settingsAlways includedIncluded only when Include app settings is on, and applied only when the recipient chooses Also Use Their Settings

The app settings comprise: the language; LiveView Mix, that is the landscape page, the portrait page with the Portrait page switch, and the two canvases of iPhone Duo with the Two canvases switch, each with its layout, tile pictures and control panels (with the values of their headers); the arrangement of the preview on the LiveView Mix tab; the option Keep cameras connected between pages; the choice in Open on launch; the device of the Live tab and the Layout of the Full Screen Wall; Default quality, Black bars, Edge-to-edge video and Hide offline cameras; the sound preference; and the range of the network scan. For the LiveView Mix pages, see “The portrait page”.

On a device other than iPhone Duo, the lower canvas and the Two canvases switch are kept but not used; they take effect again when the settings reach an iPhone Duo. Apple TV shows only the landscape page.

Not included: the plan and subscription state (it follows the Apple Account and is retrieved with Restore Purchases; see “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”), saved device reports, the agreement to the terms of YouTube or Twitch (each device asks for it once), and anything not listed above.

Backing up to iCloud

Prerequisite: this device is signed in to iCloud in the system settings. Without a sign-in, the backup stays on this device and does not reach other devices.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings list.

  2. In the Backup & Restore section, tap Back Up to iCloud.

    Check: The iCloud Backup page opens with My Backup selected in the Destination selector. Below it are the field Name (optional), the Back Up Now button and the Backups in iCloud list. While no backup exists, the list shows No backup in iCloud yet.

  3. Optional: tap Name (optional) and enter a name for the backup, for example Before moving.

    Check: The field shows the name. A name can have up to 60 characters; a longer entry is cut off.

  4. Tap Back Up Now.

    Check: A spinner appears beside the button. When the backup is complete, the page shows the green text Backed up 3 recorders · 2 cameras to iCloud., the name field is empty again, and the new backup appears at the top of Backups in iCloud. The earlier backups stay in the list.

Making the copy for Apple TV

  1. On the iCloud Backup page, select Apple TV in Destination.

    Check: The explanation below the selector reads A separate copy for Apple TV to restore. Apple TV can restore only this copy. The Current Backup section shows Last backed up and Devices of the Apple TV copy, or No backup in iCloud yet. The name field and the list are not shown.

  2. Tap Back Up Now.

    Check: The page shows the green success message, and Current Backup shows the new Last backed up time and the number of devices. The new copy replaces the previous Apple TV copy.

  • The two destinations are independent. Each Back Up Now to My Backup adds a backup and keeps the earlier ones until they are deleted (see “Several named backups: renaming and deleting”). The Apple TV destination keeps one copy, which each new backup replaces. Backing up to one destination does not change the other.
  • An iPhone and an iPad can restore any backup; an Apple TV can restore only the Apple TV copy. After devices or walls have been changed on an iPhone or iPad, back up to Apple TV again so that the television receives the new content.
  • The backup space is limited. All backups together, every backup of My Backup and the Apple TV copy, share about 1 MB of iCloud space. Tile pictures take most of it. When the space is full, the page shows Cam Hub's backup space in iCloud is full. Delete an older backup or remove some slot images, then try again.
  • When this device is not signed in to iCloud, the page shows the orange text Saved on this device only. Sign in to iCloud to keep a copy in the cloud. When the backup cannot be stored, it shows Couldn't save the backup. Check that you're signed in to iCloud. or Backup failed. Make sure you're signed in to iCloud and try again.
  • After a successful backup, the system can show a request for a rating, which can be dismissed.
  • Back up before deleting all data. Delete All Data removes every device and saved password from this device. iCloud backups are not affected and can be restored afterwards as described in “Restoring from iCloud”. Without an iCloud backup, the device passwords cannot be recovered. See Chapter 13, “Settings”.
How a backup is encrypted and protected

A backup is stored encrypted in the private iCloud of the user and is synced only to devices that use the same Apple Account. A backup has no PIN. The encryption key is built into the app and is the same in every installation, so every one of one's own devices can restore without a password to remember. The key only prevents the backup from being stored as plain text; it is not a secret kept from someone who obtains both the backup and the app. The protection of a backup rests on the security of the Apple Account and of iCloud, so the Apple Account must be kept secure.

Several named backups: renaming and deleting

The Backups in iCloud list under My Backup shows every backup, newest first. A named backup shows its name, with the date and time and the contents below it, for example Oct 28, 2026 at 9:41 PM · 3 recorders · 2 cameras. A backup without a name shows the date and time, with the contents below. The same list, with the same actions, appears on the Restore from iCloud page; see “Restoring from iCloud”. The Apple TV copy has no name and does not appear in the list.

Renaming a backup

  1. On the iCloud Backup page with My Backup selected, swipe left on a backup in Backups in iCloud.

    Check: The buttons Rename and Delete appear at the right of the row. Touching and holding the row opens a menu with the same two actions.

  2. Tap Rename.

    Check: The dialog Rename Backup appears, with the field Name holding the current name and the buttons Save and Cancel.

  3. Enter the new name and tap Save.

    Check: The row shows the new name. When the field is left empty, the name is removed and the row shows the date and time again.

Deleting one backup

  1. Swipe left on the backup to delete.

    Check: The buttons Rename and Delete appear.

  2. Tap Delete.

    Check: The dialog Delete this backup? appears and explains that the backup is removed from iCloud permanently, that other signed-in devices lose it when they next sync, and that the devices and settings on this device are not affected.

  3. Tap Delete in the dialog.

    Check: The backup disappears from the list. The other backups, the Apple TV copy and the devices on this device are unchanged.

  • Spaces at the start and end of a name are removed. Renaming changes only the name; the contents and the date of the backup stay the same.
  • Backups made, renamed or deleted on another device with the same Apple Account appear in the list when iCloud has synced them, also while the page is open.
  • A backup made with an earlier version of Cam Hub appears in the list as one of the backups.
  • When a new name cannot be stored, the alert Couldn't save the backup. Check that you're signed in to iCloud. appears.
  • To delete every backup at once, see “Deleting all iCloud backups”.

Restoring from iCloud

Prerequisite: this device is signed in with the Apple Account to which the backups belong, and a backup exists in iCloud. Right after a backup, it can take some time before it syncs to another device.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings list.

  2. In the Backup & Restore section, tap Restore from iCloud.

    Check: The Restore from iCloud page opens with My Backup selected in the Source selector, the Choose a Backup list and the Restore button. The newest backup is marked with a checkmark. When no backup is found, the list shows No backup found in iCloud. Back up from your iPhone first, signed in to the same Apple Account. and the Restore button is unavailable.

  3. Tap the backup to restore.

    Check: The checkmark moves to that backup.

  4. Tap Restore.

    Check: A spinner appears beside the button. When the restore is complete, the page shows the green text Restored 5 devices.

To restore the Apple TV copy on an iPhone or iPad, select Apple TV in Source: the iCloud Backup section shows the time of creation (From) and the number of Devices of that copy; then tap Restore. In the Choose a Backup list, backups can be renamed and deleted with a swipe, as described in “Several named backups: renaming and deleting”.

  • Devices are merged: a device that matches a device already on this device is updated, including the names and the enabled state of its channels and the SNMP settings of a NAS; the other devices are added. Other devices already present are not deleted.
  • App settings: the settings in the backup replace the matching settings on this device, including the LiveView Mix pages, Open on launch and the language. Settings that are not in the backup stay unchanged. A tile that shows a camera that was not restored becomes an empty tile, and every other tile keeps its place; empty tiles, control panels, clocks, labels and picture tiles are kept.
  • The enabled state of channels is checked against the current plan of this device. When a plan is held, channels beyond its allowance are shown as Disabled after the restore. On the free plan, the enabled state of the backup is kept, and channels beyond the free allowance show Not in your plan and a lock until the plan is restored or a plan is taken. For the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
  • The orange text Some passwords could not be saved on this device. Open those devices and use Edit Credentials. means that the passwords of some devices could not be stored. Enter them again as described in “Changing the user name and password of a device”.
  • This backup couldn't be read. Back up again to replace it. means that the backup is damaged, or that it was created by an older app with a PIN. Back up again on the original device.
  • No backup available to restore. and Restore failed. Please try again. mean that no readable backup exists, or that the restore failed. Check that iCloud is signed in and synced, then try again.

Deleting all iCloud backups

This action removes every backup at once. To delete a single backup, swipe it in the list as described in “Several named backups: renaming and deleting”.

  1. Tap the Settings tab, then tap Delete iCloud Backup in the Reset section.

    Check: The dialog Delete iCloud backup? appears and explains that all encrypted backups, including the Apple TV copy, are removed from iCloud permanently. While no backup exists, the row is unavailable.

  2. Tap Delete iCloud Backup in the dialog.

    Check: The dialog closes and the row Delete iCloud Backup becomes unavailable.

  • On an iPhone or iPad this action deletes every backup in iCloud: all backups of My Backup and the separate copy made for Apple TV. The same row on an Apple TV deletes only the copy made for Apple TV.
  • Other devices signed in with the same Apple Account lose the backups when they next sync. The devices and settings on this device are not affected.
  • When iCloud is not signed in, the action clears only the copy on this device, and the backups in the cloud can remain until the sign-in.

Moving devices and walls to a new phone

The LiveView Mix pages and their control panels belong to the app settings. Both methods below carry them: an iCloud backup always includes them, and a sharing code needs Include app settings to be on and Also Use Their Settings to be chosen on the new phone.

Method 1: moving with an iCloud backup (recommended)

Prerequisite: Cam Hub is installed on the new phone, which is signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account.

  1. On the old phone, open the Settings tab and tap Back Up to iCloud.

    Check: The iCloud Backup page opens. A name entered in Name (optional), for example Old iPhone, identifies the backup in the list later.

  2. Make sure Destination is My Backup and tap Back Up Now.

    Check: The page shows the green success message, and the new backup appears at the top of Backups in iCloud.

  3. On the new phone, open Cam Hub, tap the Settings tab, then tap Restore from iCloud.

    Check: The Restore from iCloud page opens. With Source set to My Backup, the Choose a Backup list shows the backups, and the newest one is selected. When the backup of the old phone has not synced yet, open the page again a little later.

  4. Make sure the backup of the old phone carries the checkmark, then tap Restore.

    Check: The page shows Restored 5 devices. The LiveView Mix tab shows the wall of the old phone.

  5. On the new phone, tap Restore Purchases in the Settings tab.

    Check: Purchases restored. appears. The plan is not part of the backup and is retrieved this way; see “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”.

Method 2: moving with a sharing code

  1. On the old phone, open the Settings tab and tap Export Cameras.

    Check: The Export Cameras page opens, with every device ticked by default.

  2. Turn on Include app settings.

    Check: The switch is on, and the LiveView Mix pages and the control panels travel with the code.

  3. Optional: set a PIN or a password as described in “Locking a code”.

    Check: The export button becomes available once the entry is complete.

  4. Tap the export button, then tap Share and send the link to the new phone.

    Check: The system share sheet has sent the link. Send the PIN or the password by another channel.

  5. On the new phone, tap the received link, tap Import Cameras and, for a locked code, enter the PIN or the password.

    Check: The dialog This code also has the sender's app settings appears.

  6. Tap Also Use Their Settings.

    Check: The screen shows Added 5 cameras. The LiveView Mix tab shows the wall of the old phone.

Neither method carries the plan. After signing in with the same Apple Account, retrieve it on the new phone with Restore Purchases; see “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”.

Bringing the setup to Apple TV

Apple TV neither creates nor edits walls, and entering a long code with the remote is laborious. The recommended approach is to finish the setup on an iPhone or iPad first. A backup made with Apple TV as the destination (see “Backing up to iCloud”) or a sharing code (see “Exporting cameras (creating a code)”) then brings the devices and the wall to the television. Apple TV restores only the Apple TV copy, not the backups of My Backup, and shows YouTube and Twitch streams by name only. The steps for the Apple TV, and what differs there, are described in Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.

11Plans and limits

Cam Hub comes with a free basic allowance. When more channels or recorders are needed at the same time, subscription plans extend it. All plans offer the same functions; they differ only in the number of camera channels and recorders that can be enabled at the same time. YouTube and Twitch streams are outside every plan and always free.

The allowance of each plan

PlanBillingWhat can be used at the same time
FreeNoneAt most 2 enabled channels in the whole app, counting the channels of standalone cameras and of recorders together. At most 1 recorder, and its enabled channels must all be on that one recorder.
Cam Home — 8 camerasYearlyUp to 8 standalone cameras can be enabled.
Cam Plus — 16 camerasYearlyUp to 16 standalone cameras can be enabled.
Cam Max — unlimited camerasYearlyAny number of standalone cameras can be enabled.
NVR Starter — 2 recordersMonthly2 recorders can be connected, and every channel of these 2 can be used.
NVR Pro — 4 recordersMonthly4 recorders can be connected, and every channel of these 4 can be used.
NVR Max — unlimited recordersMonthlyAny number of recorders can be connected, and every channel can be used.

Camera plans limit the number of enabled channels of standalone cameras, which are cameras that are not behind a recorder. NVR plans count recorders, not channels: every channel of a recorder that the plan covers is unlocked. The cost of each plan is shown on the plans screen of the app.

How the two groups of plans combine

Camera plans and NVR plans are two independent groups of subscriptions. Both can be held at the same time, and each decides the allowance of its own side.

Plans heldStandalone cameras (enabled channels)Recorders
None (free)At most 2, counted together with the channels of recorders1 recorder; its enabled channels must be on that one recorder, and together with standalone cameras the total stays at 2
A camera plan onlyAccording to the plan: 8, 16 or unlimitedStill the free allowance: 1 recorder with at most 2 enabled channels, no longer counted together with standalone cameras
An NVR plan onlyStill the free allowance: at most 2According to the plan: 2, 4 or unlimited recorders, with every channel of these recorders usable
BothAccording to the camera planAccording to the NVR plan
  • The two sides are counted separately. Unlocking recorders does not raise the limit for standalone cameras, and a higher camera plan does not add recorders.
  • Within one group only one plan is active at a time. A higher plan replaces a lower plan; they do not add up.
  • When both groups are raised to unlimited, Cam Hub turns on every channel once, at that moment, and the row Choose which cameras to show is hidden because nothing is left to choose. A channel that is disabled afterwards stays disabled.

What uses allowance

ItemHow it is counted
Enabled channels of standalone camerasEach channel uses 1 camera allowance.
RecordersCounted by number. While a recorder is within the number that the plan covers, every channel of it can be used. Without an NVR plan, the free allowance applies: at most 2 enabled channels on 1 recorder.
Disabled channelsThey use no allowance and do not stream.
YouTube and Twitch streamsThey use no allowance on any plan, including the free plan, and are never locked. A stream is switched on when it is added and can always be switched on again. See “YouTube and Twitch streams”.
Control panelsEach control panel uses 1 camera allowance, the same as a standalone camera, but only from what the standalone cameras leave free: a camera can always be switched on in the place of a panel, and the panel then locks. A subscription to an NVR plan alone does not add to this allowance. Clock, label, picture and empty tiles use no allowance. See Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
Control panels on several LiveView Mix pagesEach panel on each page in use counts on its own: the landscape page always; the portrait page while Portrait page is on (iPhone and iPad); the lower canvas on an iPhone Duo while Two canvases is on. A panel copied to another page counts again. On Apple TV only the panels of the landscape page count. See “The portrait page”.
Tiles of LiveView MixThe number of tiles of a wall is not limited; what is limited is the channels that can stream. LiveView Mix cannot show more cameras than the allowance of the plan.

When the allowance is not sufficient, items keep their picture in this order: first standalone cameras (in the order in which their devices were added, then by channel number), then the channels of recorders, and last control panels (those of the landscape page first, then those of the lower canvas, then those of the portrait page). On the free plan, only the first 2 of all these together are kept, so a control panel never displaces a camera. With a camera plan, control panels receive what the standalone cameras leave of the camera allowance. With an NVR plan, the first recorders in sequence keep all their channels, and the channels of the remaining recorders are locked.

A control panel beyond the allowance keeps its place on the wall and shows a lock, its title and Not in your plan; its buttons are unavailable.

When a recorder is added and the number allowed by the plan has been reached, the plans screen opens with the text Free includes 1 recorder. Add more with an NVR plan. and the recorder is not added. While the demo devices hold the free recorder, the text reads Free includes 1 recorder, and the demo devices are using it. Delete them to add your own recorder, or add more with an NVR plan.; see “Trying the app without a device”.

Examples of combinations

The examples apply the rules above. A channel is one picture of a camera; the channels of recorders and of standalone cameras are counted separately according to the plan.

Plan heldEquipmentResult
Free1 recorder (16 channels)At most 2 channels can be enabled, and both must be on this recorder. When a second recorder is added, the Plans screen opens with the reason and the recorder is not added.
Free2 standalone cameras and 1 recorderThe standalone cameras and the recorder channels count together, at most 2. With both standalone cameras enabled, no recorder channel can be enabled; after one standalone camera is disabled, 1 recorder channel can be enabled, and the total is still 2.
Free5 standalone camerasOnly 2 can be enabled and the other 3 stay disabled. To switch to another camera, disable an enabled one first and then enable the wanted one; see “Choosing which cameras show”.
Free1 recorder with 2 channels enabled, and 1 control panelThe 2 recorder channels show. The control panel ranks after the cameras, so it locks and shows Not in your plan.
Free1 recorder with 2 channels enabled, and 3 YouTube streamsEverything plays. The streams use no allowance.
Cam Home — 8 cameras10 standalone camerasUp to 8 can be enabled. To use the other 2, disable 2 of the enabled cameras first.
Cam Home — 8 cameras8 standalone cameras and 1 recorder (16 channels)The recorder is not affected by a camera plan and keeps the free allowance: 1 recorder with at most 2 enabled channels. Its channels no longer count together with the standalone cameras, so up to 8 standalone cameras plus 2 recorder channels can be used at the same time.
NVR Starter — 2 recorders2 recorders (16 channels each) and 4 standalone camerasEvery channel of the 2 recorders (32 in all) can be used. The standalone cameras keep the free allowance: at most 2 can be enabled. When a third recorder is added, the Plans screen opens and the recorder is not added.
Cam Plus — 16 cameras and NVR Pro — 4 recorders4 recorders and 12 standalone camerasEverything can be used: every channel of the 4 recorders, plus 12 standalone cameras (the limit is 16, so 4 are still free).
Cam Home — 8 cameras7 standalone cameras and 1 control panelThe control panel uses the eighth camera allowance, so the allowance is full. An added standalone camera can still be enabled: it takes that allowance, and the control panel locks and shows Not in your plan.
Cam Home — 8 cameras6 standalone cameras, a control panel on the landscape page and its copy on the portrait page, with Portrait page onEach copy counts: 6 cameras and 2 panels use all 8. When Portrait page is turned off, the copy on the portrait page no longer counts.
Cam Max — unlimited cameras and NVR Max — unlimited recordersAny number of cameras and recordersEvery channel is enabled automatically and nothing needs to be chosen. The row Choose which cameras to show is hidden.
A change from NVR Pro — 4 recorders to NVR Starter — 2 recorders4 recordersThe first 2 recorders keep every channel. The channels of the other 2 stop streaming, their tiles show Not in your plan and a lock, and the devices and settings are kept. After subscribing again or restoring purchases they work at once; see “When a plan ends or is reduced”.

Choosing which cameras show

Path: Settings › Choose which cameras to show. When the allowance of the plan is smaller than the total number of channels of the devices, the user decides which channels use it. This page, titled like the row, gathers the channels of all devices on one screen, with one switch per channel; for the steps, see “Choosing which cameras show”.

  • What it does: a switch controls whether a channel is enabled. A channel that is off does not stream and uses no allowance, and it can be turned on again at any time; a channel that is on uses allowance. The switches on this page are the same function as Enable and Disable after touching and holding a channel tile on the device page; see “Channel options (long press)”. YouTube and Twitch streams are listed as well; their switches never touch the allowance.
  • The Your plan section shows the limits of the current plan: Cameras is the number of channels of standalone cameras that can be enabled, and Recorders is the number of recorders whose channels can all be used; each is a number or Unlimited.
  • When the allowance is used up, turning a switch on is refused: the switch stays off, and the plans screen opens with the reason at the top, for example You've reached the Free plan's limit of 2 enabled cameras., You've reached your plan's limit of 8 enabled cameras., On the Free plan, the cameras you show must all be on one recorder. or Unlock every channel with an NVR plan. Turning a switch off is always possible.
  • When it is offered: the item is available only while at least one of the two limits of the plan is in effect. When both groups of plans are raised to unlimited, every channel is turned on automatically and the item is hidden. While no device exists, the page shows No Devices with Add a device first, then choose its cameras here. and the Add Device button.
  • To obtain more allowance, subscribe as described in “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”. Channels beyond the allowance show Not in your plan and a lock on the wall and on the device page; see “What a thumbnail shows”.

Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code

Prerequisite: this device is signed in with an Apple Account in the system settings, and purchases are permitted. A subscription follows the Apple Account and is shared across iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen, then tap Plans in the Subscription section.

    Check: The Plans page opens. Below the row Plans, the current plan is shown; without a subscription it reads Free.

  2. In the section Camera plans · billed yearly or NVR plans · billed monthly, find the plan to take and tap Subscribe on its card.

    Check: The system purchase confirmation appears. Each card shows the name of the plan, a short description and its cost; when the Apple Account is eligible, the length of a free trial is shown as well.

  3. Follow the prompts of the system screen to confirm the purchase with the Apple Account.

    Check: The card of the plan changes to Current Plan, and the allowance is updated immediately. The row Plans in the Settings tab shows the name of the plan.

  4. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The plans page closes and the settings list is shown again.

  • A subscription renews automatically until the user cancels it. Camera plans are billed yearly, NVR plans monthly.
  • The outcome of a purchase that does not complete is shown below the card of the plan: Purchase failed. Please try again.; Waiting for approval. The plan unlocks as soon as the purchase is approved. when the purchase needs approval, for example by a family organizer; or The App Store could not confirm this purchase. Try Restore Purchases.
  • When the plans cannot be loaded, the page shows Couldn't load plans. Check your connection and try again. The names and descriptions of the plans are supplied by the app itself, and the cost appears once the purchase service has answered.
  • Manage Subscription opens the system subscription page, where a plan can be canceled or changed and the renewal date can be seen.
  • While plans of both groups are held, the row Plans joins the names of the two plans with a plus sign.
  • The text at the top of the plans page states that every plan includes all functions, including live view, recording playback and the multi-camera wall; that video does not pass through a cloud and needs no account; and that the two limits are counted separately. At the bottom of the page are the links Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Restoring purchases

Use this on another device, after a reinstallation, or when a purchase is not reflected immediately.

  1. In the Subscription section of the Settings tab, tap Restore Purchases. The same button is at the bottom of the plans page.

    Check: The app synchronizes the purchase records with the system purchase service and shows a message.

  2. Read the message and dismiss it.

    Check: When purchases are found, the message reads Purchases restored. and the allowance is updated. When none are found, it reads No purchases to restore. After an error it reads Restore failed. Please try again. When the system sign-in screen is canceled, no message appears.

Redeeming a code

  1. In the Subscription section of the Settings tab, tap Redeem Code. The same button is at the bottom of the plans page.

    Check: The system screen for redeeming a code appears. When it cannot be opened, the alert Couldn't open code redemption. Check your connection, or redeem the code in the App Store. appears instead.

  2. Follow the prompts of the system screen to enter and redeem the code.

    Check: After a successful redemption, the plan and the allowance are updated. When they are not updated yet, synchronize with Restore Purchases.

On Apple TV, Manage Subscription and Redeem Code are not offered; they are used on an iPhone or an iPad. See Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.

When a plan ends or is reduced

  • Cam Hub checks the plan whenever the app returns to the foreground. When a subscription ends without renewal, or a lower plan takes its place, the allowance shrinks accordingly.
  • When the App Store cannot confirm the purchases, for example while the device is offline or signed out of the App Store, the last confirmed plan stays in effect for up to 14 days. A plan that Apple reports as ended, refunded or replaced by another plan of the same group ends at once.
  • The enabled state of channels is not rewritten, and the devices, names, wall layouts and settings are all kept. Channels beyond the new allowance stop streaming, and their tiles show Not in your plan and a lock. Tapping such a tile opens the plans screen with the reason. A locked channel cannot be used for recording playback either.
  • The order in which items are kept is the one described in “What uses allowance”: standalone cameras first, then the channels of recorders, and last control panels. A locked control panel shows a lock, its title and Not in your plan, and its buttons are unavailable. YouTube and Twitch streams are never locked.
  • After subscribing again or restoring purchases, the locked channels stream again, and no device has to be added again.
  • When a backup is restored or a code is imported while a plan is held, channels beyond its allowance are written as Disabled; such channels must be turned on again, as described in “Choosing which cameras show”, once the allowance is sufficient. On the free plan the enabled state is kept, and the channels beyond the free allowance stay locked until a plan covers them. See Chapter 10, “Sharing and backup”.

12The Tools tab

The Tools tab contains the network scan for finding devices, the speedometer with compass, and a section that adds sample devices. The scan is described step by step in the chapter on adding a device; this chapter gives an overview of the tab and describes the speedometer.

What the Tools tab contains

Path: Tools tab at the bottom of the screen. The tab is a single list. The sections follow each other in the order below.

SectionContentsDetails
SubnetThe row This device with the own address of the iPhone or iPad, the address field of the range, the selector Range, the line that states what will be scanned, the button Use my subnet (only while the range differs from the own network) and the button Scan or Stop.“Finding devices with the network scan”
Found DevicesThe progress of the scan, the addresses that answered with their open ports and, once the sweep is over, what the devices say about themselves: a name or a model and, for a recorder, the number of channels. A tap on a result opens the Add Device form with the address, and what the device said about itself, filled in.“Finding devices with the network scan”
SpeedometerThe row Speedometer, which opens the speedometer with compass. The section is offered depending on the region and the language setting of the device.“Speedometer and compass”
DemoThe button Add Demo Devices (App Review), which adds sample devices.Below on this page.

  1. Tap the Tools tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the sections of the tab, beginning with Subnet. The address field and the range are already filled in with the network of the device.

For the steps of a scan, see “Finding devices with the network scan”. The following points concern the behavior of the tab as a whole.

  • Stored range: the address and the range are stored. When the device joins another network, both fields are filled in again for the new network, unless the range was typed by hand; a range that was typed by hand is kept. The button Use my subnet hands the choice back to the app. Restore Default Settings forgets the stored range; see “Reset: defaults, delete all data, delete iCloud backup”.
  • While a scan runs: the address field and the range cannot be changed. Stop ends the scan. A running scan also ends when the screen is left.
  • No sign-in: the scan checks only whether connections to the ports can be made and reads the name that a device announces on its web port. When the sweep is over, the list shows Identifying devices… while the app asks the devices it found, through the discovery services of the local network, to name themselves. It does not sign in to any device. A device is added only after the credentials have been entered in the Add Device form.
  • Identified devices: when a result was opened for a device that stated its brand, and the address was not changed, the Add Device form leaves out the compatibility reference and Add Demo Cameras, which only help with an unknown device.
  • Local network access: the first scan can cause the system to ask whether Cam Hub may find devices on the local network. When the access is refused, the scan finds nothing. After a complete scan without results, the list adds the sentence If your cameras are on this network, check that Cam Hub is allowed to find devices on your local network in the system privacy settings.; see “Finding devices with the network scan” and “Permission requests and system dialogs”.

Adding sample devices

The section Demo is at the end of the tab. Its text states that the devices are meant for the review of the app and that everyday use does not need them. They can be used by anyone to try the app without equipment. The sample devices draw their own pictures and need no network and no sign-in.

  1. Scroll to the end of the Tools tab and tap Add Demo Devices (App Review).

    Check: The app adds five recorders and two cameras. Each recorder has three channels. The recorders are named Demo NVR 1 to Demo NVR 5, and the cameras Demo Camera 1 and Demo Camera 2.

  2. Tap the Devices tab.

    Check: The list shows the sample devices. Their channels are enabled only as far as the current plan allows; the other channels show Disabled; see “Plan limits and enabling channels”.

  • Added once: after a tap, the button is dimmed. When the sample devices already exist, it adds nothing.
  • Counted like real devices: the sample recorders count toward the number of recorders that the plan allows, and enabled sample channels use places of the plan. Delete the sample devices before a real recorder is added on the free plan; see “The device list”.
  • Follow the plan: the app sets the enabled state of the sample channels again whenever it starts and whenever the plan changes, so that they always show what the plan allows. A switch that was changed by hand on a sample channel is not kept.
  • Limited functions: sample devices have no recording playback, no camera control and no snapshot, and the device page cannot refresh their channel list.

Speedometer and compass

The speedometer shows the speed of the device and the direction in which it moves or points. The position comes from satellite positioning. Whether the Tools tab offers the speedometer depends on the region and the language setting of the device. When it is not offered, the Tools tab shows the other sections only.

Opening the speedometer and allowing location access

Prerequisite: the iPhone or iPad has a clear view of the sky. Indoors, the position can be delayed or missing.

  1. Tap the Tools tab, scroll to the section Speedometer and tap the row Speedometer.

    Check: The screen Speedometer opens. When Cam Hub has not been allowed to use the location before, a system dialog asks for permission.

  2. Tap Allow While Using App.

    Check: The screen shows Waiting for GPS… until the first position has been received. The message then disappears.

  3. Move with the device, for example in a vehicle.

    Check: The large number shows the speed, and the compass dial turns with the direction.

Reading the screen

ElementMeaning
Large numberThe speed in km/h, rounded to whole numbers. The number shows — until the first measurement. A device at rest shows 0.
km/h and the line with mphThe same speed in both units. Both are always shown. There is no setting for the unit. Before the first measurement, the line reads 0 mph.
Compass dialThe dial turns below a fixed pointer at the top. The direction in which the device moves or points is the one below the pointer. The ring has a tick every 5 degrees and the letters N, E, S and W.
Text in the middle of the dialThe name of the direction (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W or NW) and the heading in degrees, counted clockwise from north. The text shows – until a heading is available.

The heading comes from two sources. While the device moves at 8 km/h or faster, it is the direction of travel determined by satellite positioning. At lower speeds, it is the heading of the compass of the device. When no compass reading exists, the last direction of travel is shown.

Messages below the compass

MessageMeaning and action
Waiting for GPS… (grey)No position has been received yet. Wait a few seconds, or move to a place with a clear view of the sky.
Can't get a GPS fix. (orange)The position could not be determined. The message disappears as soon as a position arrives. When it remains, move to a place with a clear view of the sky, or leave the screen and open it again.
Location access is off. Turn it on in Settings to see your speed and heading. (orange), with the button Open SettingsCam Hub is not allowed to use the location. Allow it as described below.
No messageA position is known. Speed and heading are current.

Allowing location access afterwards

  1. Tap Open Settings below the orange message.

    Check: The system settings of Cam Hub open.

  2. Tap Location and select While Using the App.

    Check: The entry Location shows While Using the App.

  3. Return to Cam Hub, tap the back button of the speedometer and open the row Speedometer again.

    Check: The screen shows Waiting for GPS… and then the speed and the heading.

Announcing the speed by voice

The switch Announce speed at the bottom of the screen is on by default. Its text reads Says your speed aloud every 10 km/h, from 150 up to 450 km/h.

  1. Tap the row Announce speed.

    Check: The switch is off. No speed is announced. The choice is stored.

  2. Tap the row Announce speed again.

    Check: The switch is on. The voice announces speeds from now on.

  • What is said: only the number in km/h, without a unit. The voice speaks once each time the speed passes the next multiple of ten, from 150 up to 450. Nothing is said below 150 or while the speed falls.
  • No repetition: a number is not repeated while the speed fluctuates slightly around it. It is said again only after the speed has fallen clearly below it and then risen again.
  • Switching on at speed: when the voice is switched on at a high speed, numbers that have already been passed are not announced. The next multiple of ten is the first one.
  • Language of the voice: the voice follows the language of the app (Settings › Language). When the device has no voice for that language, the English voice is used.
  • Other audio: music or other audio that plays at the same time becomes quieter while a number is spoken and continues afterwards.
  • Backup and reset: the switch is not part of the backups, and Restore Default Settings does not change it.

Leaving the speedometer

  1. Tap the back button in the top-left corner.

    Check: The Tools tab is shown again. The use of the location and the announcements stop.

  • Screen stays on: while the speedometer is open, the device does not lock the screen automatically.
  • Location only while open: Cam Hub uses the location only while the screen is open, and only while the app is in use. The position is used for the display and is not stored.

Default quality

The two rows set whether a picture starts as SD (lighter) or HD (sharper). The text below the section advises that viewing one camera can use more resources for a sharper picture, that the capacity of the device matters when many cameras are viewed at once, and that SD and HD look almost the same when each tile is small.

RowUsed byDefault
Single cameraThe single-camera view, see “Snapshot, sound and quality”, and the close-up of a camera in a wall, see “The full-screen wall of a device”.HD
Multiple camerasThe Live tab and the Full Screen Wall, see “SD and HD on a wall”, and the thumbnails of the device page, see “The device page”.SD

LiveView Mix walls are not affected: each camera slot has its own quality; see “Choosing cameras and quality”. For all screens, see “SD and HD on device screens”.

  1. In the Settings tab, find the section Default quality.

    Check: Two rows show a selector with SD and HD. Without a change, HD is selected for Single camera and SD for Multiple cameras.

  2. In the row Multiple cameras, tap HD.

    Check: HD is selected. The thumbnails of the device page change to HD at once. The Live tab changes to HD at once as well, unless the quality button of the Live tab has been used since the app started.

  3. To return, tap SD in the same row.

    Check: SD is selected.

The quality can still be switched while viewing; that change is not stored, as the text below the section states.

Picture: black bars and edge-to-edge

Both rows decide how much of the screen the picture uses: one inside its tile, the other against the edges of the device.

  • Black bars (default Default): the starting mode for the handling of black bars. Default shows the whole picture with black bars where the shapes differ, Enlarge to fill enlarges the picture in proportion and cuts off its edges, and Stretch to fill stretches the picture and can distort it; see “The device page”. The setting is the starting mode of the device page, the Full Screen Wall, the single-camera view and the Live tab. The device page and the Full Screen Wall read it each time they open, the single-camera view applies it at once, and the Live tab reads it when the app starts. The change of mode on a screen is not stored. LiveView Mix has its own setting for each wall; see “Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device”.
  • Edge-to-edge video (default on): while the switch is on, full-screen video reaches into the area of the Dynamic Island and the rounded corners. While it is off, the picture stays clear of them, with black bars. The switch applies to the Full Screen Wall, to the full-screen wall of LiveView Mix and to the single-camera view held sideways; see “Black bars, rotation and landscape”.

  1. In the section Picture, tap Black bars.

    Check: A menu lists Default, Enlarge to fill and Stretch to fill. The current choice is marked.

  2. Tap Enlarge to fill.

    Check: The row shows Enlarge to fill. From now on, the screens named above start with this mode.

  3. Tap the switch of Edge-to-edge video.

    Check: The switch is off. Full-screen video keeps clear of the Dynamic Island and the rounded corners. Tap the switch again to turn it on.

Hide offline cameras

The row has no section title. While the switch is on, cameras without a signal do not appear on the Live tab and on the Full Screen Wall. The device page still lists them, grayed out. The switch is off by default; the effect, the cameras that are hidden and the way hidden cameras return are described in “Hiding cameras without signal”.

  1. Tap the switch of Hide offline cameras.

Two sections move devices to another iPhone, iPad or Apple TV. A backup in iCloud serves the same Apple Account. A code serves any other device, with no iCloud, and can be given to another person.

The two ways are compared in “Comparing the two methods”.

Language

14Apple TV

The Apple TV app shows the devices and the LiveView Mix wall that were set up on an iPhone or an iPad. The recommended order is to finish the whole setup on an iPhone or iPad first and to bring it to the Apple TV afterwards. This chapter gives the steps for that and lists what differs on the television. It is not an operating guide for the Apple TV app.

Set up on an iPhone or iPad first

The Apple TV is operated with a remote. Typing, drawing and choosing are laborious there, and several functions are not offered at all. These tasks are therefore done on an iPhone or an iPad before the Apple TV is used:

  • Adding the devices; see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.
  • Building the LiveView Mix wall, with a custom layout and control panels where wanted; see Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix” and Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
  • Choosing the plans and the cameras that show; see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

Bringing the setup to the Apple TV

Prerequisites: the iPhone or iPad and the Apple TV are signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account, and both run the same version of Cam Hub. A backup that an older version made does not appear on the Apple TV.

  1. On the iPhone or iPad, finish the setup: the devices, the LiveView Mix wall, the plans and the choice of cameras that show.

    Check: The devices and the wall appear on the iPhone or iPad the way they are to appear on the television.

  2. On the iPhone or iPad, back up to iCloud with Apple TV as the destination; see “Backing up to iCloud”.

    Check: The backup page shows the message that the backup was made, and Current Backup shows the time and the number of devices. A new backup to Apple TV replaces the previous Apple TV copy.

  3. On the Apple TV, open the Settings tab and select Restore from iCloud in the iCloud Backup section.

    Check: The page shows the time of the backup in From and its contents in Devices. When the section shows No backup found in iCloud yet instead of the row, see “Sharing, import and iCloud backup”.

  4. Select Restore. What a restore changes is described in “Restoring from iCloud”.

    Check: The page shows how many devices were restored. The Devices tab of the Apple TV lists them, and the LiveView Mix tab shows the wall.

  5. On the Apple TV, select Plans in the Settings tab.

    Check: The page shows the plan of the Apple Account. A plan that is not shown yet appears after Restore Purchases.

The Apple TV restores only the copy that was backed up for it. The named backups kept under My Backup are listed only on the iPhone and the iPad; see “Several named backups: renaming and deleting”.

When the two devices do not share an Apple Account, a sharing code replaces the backup. Create the code on the iPhone or iPad as described in “Exporting cameras (creating a code)” and copy it. On the Apple TV, select Share Cameras › Import Cameras in the Settings tab and enter the code; when the keyboard appears, a nearby iPhone can type it. A locked code asks for its PIN or password. A code can be hundreds to thousands of characters long, so an iCloud backup is preferable whenever the Apple Account is the same.

Later changes reach the Apple TV only with a new backup

After devices, the wall or the plans have been changed on the iPhone or iPad, repeat steps 2 to 4. The Apple TV does not follow changes by itself. A changed password of a device can also be entered on the Apple TV with Edit Credentials on the device page.

There is no scan, no list of brands, no checklist and no device report. A YouTube or Twitch link is refused. At the recorder limit, the form shows Free includes 1 recorder. The settings for the language, the default quality, the black bars and Hide offline cameras (in the Live walls section) are available on the Apple TV as well. Problems with a backup that does not appear on the Apple TV are covered in “Sharing, import and iCloud backup”.

15Troubleshooting

This chapter lists, by symptom, what the empty screens, messages, permission requests and notices of Cam Hub mean, the likely cause and what to do. Connection failures while adding a device are covered in “When adding fails: the checklist” and are not repeated here.

Where to start

Most connection symptoms trace back to one of four causes. Check them in this order before reading the sections below.

  1. The iPhone or iPad is on the same Wi-Fi network as the device. A guest network, a separate VLAN, client isolation on the router and a VPN on the phone all block the connection.
  2. Cam Hub is allowed to use the local network; see “Permission requests and system dialogs”.
  3. The device is powered on and still has the address that was entered in Cam Hub. After a restart, a router can assign a different address to a device; a fixed address prevents this.
  4. The account and the password are still valid on the device. After several wrong attempts, a device can lock the account for a while.
SymptomWhere to look
A device cannot be added, or its connection indicator is red“When adding fails: the checklist”, “A device is added, but it is not reachable”
A screen is empty and shows only a title and a sentence“What the empty screens say”
A camera shows no picture, a black picture, an error message or no sound, or talking through it does not work“Live view”
The list of recordings is empty, the times differ, or playback does not speed up“Recording playback”
A tile of the LiveView Mix wall shows a status text, or the wall has changed“LiveView Mix”
A YouTube or Twitch tile shows a name and a sentence instead of the stream“YouTube and Twitch”
A control panel button shows an orange triangle“Control panels and webhooks”
The Disk Health page shows a message instead of the disks“Disk Health”
A code or a backup cannot be imported or restored“Sharing, import and iCloud backup”
A lock, the plans screen or a plan message appears unexpectedly“Plans and purchases”
A message sentence is not listed above“Other error sentences”
The system asks for permission, or a permission was refused“Permission requests and system dialogs”
None of the above applies“Reaching the developer”, “Questions and answers”

A device is added, but it is not reachable

The checklist after a failed attempt and the device report are described in “When adding fails: the checklist” and “Device report (experimental)”. The symptoms below appear after a device has been added.

What is shownLikely causeWhat to do
A red, crossed-out Wi-Fi symbol in the device listThe device did not accept a connection on its HTTP port within about 4 seconds. It may be switched off, on another network, or blocked by a firewall. A device that was added with a brand chosen under Connect using, or one that uses another port for video, can show the red symbol while its video works.Check the power and the network. When the video plays, the symbol can be ignored. See “The device list”.
A device that worked yesterday is unreachable todayThe address of the device changed. A device keeps the address with which it was added.Look up the new address on the router, delete the old device and add the device again with the new address; see “The Add Device form”. A saved password no longer works, and the device page shows Wrong username or password. with the button Edit CredentialsThe password or the username was changed on the device.Tap Edit Credentials and enter the new account. It is checked on the device before it is saved; the cameras, their names and the walls stay as they are. See “Changing the user name and password of a device”.
The plans screen opens when a recorder is addedThe recorder allowance of the plan is used up. Sample devices count like real ones.See “Plans and purchases”.
A device cannot be added at all, and it only works in the app of its makerThe device offers no connection on the local network, or it accepts HTTPS only.See “Requirements and limits”.

Live view

What is shownLikely causeWhat to do
A grey tile with a crossed-out camera and No signalThe device reports that this channel has no video signal. The camera behind the channel is off, disconnected from the recorder, or has lost its network link.Check the power and the cable or network of the camera. When it is back, open the device page, or pull down on it, to read the channel list again. When a camera is missing from the Live tab altogether, check whether Hide offline cameras is on; see “Hiding cameras without signal”.
A message with a warning symbol and the button RetryThe stream could not be opened. The message names the cause, with the same wording as when a device is added.Find the sentence in “When adding fails: the checklist” or “Other error sentences”, correct the cause, then tap Retry.
Wrong username or password. for a device that worked beforeThe password was changed on the device, or the account was locked or removed. After one refusal, the other tiles of the same device fail at once without signing in, so that the device does not count a refused sign-in for every tile. The device is asked again after about a minute, or when the app returns to the foreground.Correct the account on the device, or wait until a lock ends, usually about 30 minutes. To store a new password, tap Edit Credentials on the device page; see “Changing the user name and password of a device”.
Connecting… for a long time, or Reconnecting… again and againThe network is weak, or the device does not answer. Cam Hub tries again at growing intervals of up to about 15 seconds, and after ten failed attempts in a row up to about a minute. A stream that delivers no picture for about 15 seconds is treated as interrupted and connected again, also when the camera still answers but its picture has frozen. A device can also serve only a limited number of viewers at the same time.Check the Wi-Fi signal. Close other viewers of the same camera. In a wall with many cameras, use SD instead of HD; see “SD and HD on device screens”.
A black picture without a messageThe camera sends a video format that the phone cannot decode. Cam Hub plays H.264 and H.265 only. An iPhone without hardware support for H.265, or a picture size above the limit of the decoder, shows no picture.In the stream settings of the camera, select H.264 and a lower resolution. A key frame interval of one to two seconds helps when the picture appears only after a long delay. See “Connection states and messages”.
The picture is blurred or blockyThe wall or the view uses SD, or the device offers only one stream. SD and HD are the same stream for some devices.Switch to HD in the single-camera view. Default values are set in the Settings tab; see “SD and HD on device screens”.
No speaker button, or no soundSound is off until the speaker button is tapped. The button appears only when the stream carries sound in a supported format (G.711 or AAC-LC). Sound plays only in the single-camera view and in the close-up of a wall, never on wall tiles and never in the background. Playback faster than 1× is muted. While someone talks through the camera, its own sound pauses.Tap the speaker button. When it is missing, the stream has no usable sound; turn on a supported audio format in the settings of the camera. For YouTube and Twitch, see “YouTube and Twitch”.
No talk button on the camera pageTalking is offered only in live view, for a camera that has a talk channel which Cam Hub can use, and not while the channel is beyond the plan. The channels of a recorder have none.See “Two-way talk”.
Microphone access is off for Cam Hub. Turn it on in Settings to talk through the camera.The microphone permission was refused.Turn the permission on in the system settings; see “Permission requests and system dialogs”.
This camera's talk channel is set to G.726. Set it to G.711 in the camera's audio settings to talk from Cam Hub. (the name of the format varies)The talk channel of the camera uses a sound format that Cam Hub does not send.In the audio settings of the camera, set the talk channel to G.711.
The microphone could not be started. Another app may be using it.Another app, or a call, holds the microphone.End the call or close the other app, then hold the talk button again.
Could not start talking to the camera. or The camera stopped taking sound.The camera did not open its talk channel, or closed it while someone was talking.Try again. Check that the account has the right to use the audio of the camera, and that no other app is talking through it.
Paused, Disabled or Not in your planThe channel was paused, was not enabled, or is beyond the allowance of the plan.See “What a thumbnail shows” and “Plans and purchases”.
Pictures stop when the app is left or the phone is lockedThis is intended. Every stream stops in the background, talking ends, and the streams connect again when the app returns.No action is needed. A recording that was playing resumes where it stopped.

What is shownLikely causeWhat to do
An orange warning triangle after a button was pressedThe request failed. The cause can be an empty or malformed address, no connection, a timeout after 10 seconds, an https certificate that iOS does not trust, or an answer other than 200 to 299, for example 401, 404 or 500. The screen does not show which one.Check, in this order: the address (it must start with http:// or https:// and name a host), the connection between the phone and the receiving side, and the log of the receiving side. See “Pressing a button and reading the result”.
A green check mark, but nothing movedThe check mark means only that the receiving side answered with a status from 200 to 299.Check the log of the receiving side and the equipment behind it.
No endpoint set under a button in the editorThe address of the button is empty or not valid.Enter the address in the editor of the button; see “Setting up a button”.
Nothing is sent when a panel is tapped on the arrange screenThis is intended. A request is sent only from the wall or from the preview in the tab.Press the button on the wall; see “Pressing a button and reading the result”.
A confirmation dialog appears before the requestThe button has Confirm before firing switched on.Confirm to send, or switch the option off in the editor of the button.
The button works at home and fails elsewhereThe address points into the home network. A request cannot cross to it from outside without a VPN or another route.See “Security notes”.
An address that ends in .local failsSome networks do not resolve such names.Enter the fixed IP address of the receiving side instead.
The buttons do not appear on the Apple Watch, or fail thereThe watch shows only the buttons of the control panels on the LiveView Mix wall of the paired iPhone, and only those that the plan allows.See “Buttons on Apple Watch”.

Disk Health

The Disk Health page reads the state of the disks of devices that report it; see “Disk Health”. A network storage device reports it over SNMP, which has to be set up once. Apple TV has no Disk Health page.

What is shownLikely causeWhat to do
The device page has no Disk Health rowThe device was added through a connection method that cannot read the disks, for example ONVIF or a brand chosen under Connect using, or the device does not report them.See “Disk Health”.
This NAS shares its disk health over SNMP. Set it up once to see S.M.A.R.T. data, temperatures and the state of its volumes. with the button Set Up SNMPNo SNMP community has been entered for this device yet. A code or a backup made with an older version of Cam Hub does not carry it.Tap Set Up SNMP, enter the Community and the Port that are set on the device, and tap Save.
The NAS did not answer SNMP on UDP port 161. Check that SNMP is on in DSM (Control Panel > Terminal & SNMP) and that the community name matches.SNMP is switched off on the device, the community does not match, or the UDP port cannot be reached. A device does not answer a wrong community at all, so all three causes look the same. Only SNMPv1 and v2c are supported, and the port is usually not reachable through a forwarded port or a remote-access service.Switch on SNMP on the device with version v1 or v2c, check the community under SNMP Settings, and use the page on the same network as the device. Then tap Try Again.
Enter a community name and a port from 1 to 65535.A field of SNMP Settings is empty, or the port is out of range.Enter the community and a port, usually 161.
Disk health is not available on this device.The device, or the account in use, does not give out the state of its disks. Some devices give it only to an administrator account.Check the rights of the account on the device; see “Changing the user name and password of a device” to change the account.
Showing the last reading. Pull down to try again.A new reading failed; the page keeps the previous one. The reason is shown above it.Correct the reason, then pull down on the page.
This device does not report S.M.A.R.T. data for this disk, so only its own status is shown.The device gives the state of the disk but not its S.M.A.R.T. table.No action helps. The status of the disk is still shown.
Needs attention or FailingThe disk itself shows signs of wear or failure. The page lists the reasons under the verdict.Read the reasons; back up important recordings and plan a replacement of the disk. See “Disk Health”.

Sharing, import and iCloud backup

What is shownLikely causeWhat to do
Wrong PINThe six digits do not match the PIN that was set when the code was exported.Ask the sender for the digits, then tap Import Cameras again. The number of attempts is not limited. A forgotten PIN cannot be recovered; the sender has to export again.
Wrong passwordThe password does not match. Capitals, spaces and symbols all count.Check the password with the sender, then try again. A forgotten password cannot be recovered; the sender has to export again.
Couldn't read that codeThe text is incomplete or was altered on the way, for example by a message app that cut it.Copy the whole code again from the export screen, and paste it in full. Lines of text before or after the code do no harm.
Update Cam HubThe code was made with a different version of the app.Update the app on both devices, then try again.
The cameras could not be saved. Try again.The devices of the code could not be stored.Try again. When the message persists, restart the app and try once more; see “Reaching the developer”.
After an import or a restore, channels show Not in your plan or DisabledAn import or a restore does not check the number of recorders. On the free plan, channels beyond the allowance stay enabled and show Not in your plan until a plan covers them, also on a new device where the App Store has not reported the plan yet. On a paid plan, channels beyond its allowance are written as disabled.Wait until the plan appears, or tap Restore Purchases. Turn channels on again as described in “Choosing which cameras show” once the allowance is sufficient.
Some passwords could not be saved on this device. Open those devices and use Edit Credentials.The restore brought the devices back, but the passwords of some could not be stored on this device.Open each of those devices and enter the password with Edit Credentials; see “Changing the user name and password of a device”.
Couldn't save the backup. Check that you're signed in to iCloud. or Backup failed. Make sure you're signed in to iCloud and try again.The device is not signed in to iCloud, or iCloud cannot be reached.Sign in to iCloud in the system settings, check the connection, then back up again. See “Backing up to iCloud”.
Cam Hub's backup space in iCloud is full. Delete an older backup or remove some slot images, then try again.All backups of Cam Hub, the named ones and the Apple TV copy, share about 1 MB in iCloud. Pictures in the slots of the wall take most of it.Delete an older backup in the list Backups in iCloud (see “Several named backups: renaming and deleting”), or remove some pictures from the slots of the wall, then back up again.
Saved on this device only. Sign in to iCloud to keep a copy in the cloud.The device is not signed in to iCloud. The backup was kept on this device only and reaches no other device.Sign in to iCloud in the system settings, then back up again.
No backup in iCloud yet. or No backup found in iCloud. Back up from your iPhone first, signed in to the same Apple Account.No backup exists for this Apple Account, the backup has not finished syncing, or it was made to the other destination (My Backup or Apple TV).Back up on the source device first, signed in with the same Apple Account, and choose the matching destination. Wait for iCloud to sync, then open the restore page again. See “Restoring from iCloud”.
A backup is missing from the list of backupsIt was deleted on another device signed in to the same Apple Account, or Delete iCloud Backup in the Settings tab removed all backups, including the Apple TV copy.Make a new backup on the device that holds the devices. See “Several named backups: renaming and deleting”.
This backup couldn't be read. Back up again to replace it.The backup is damaged, or an older version of the app made it.Make a new backup on the original device.
Restore failed. Please try again. or No backup available to restore.No readable backup, or the restore was interrupted.Check that iCloud is signed in and synced, then try again.
The Apple TV shows No backup found in iCloud yetThe backup was made to My Backup, the Apple Account differs, or the app versions on the two devices differ. A backup that an older version made does not appear.Back up again with Apple TV as the destination, on the same app version and the same Apple Account; see Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.
After a restore, the plan is missingPurchases are not part of a backup. They follow the Apple Account.Tap Restore Purchases; see “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”.

A sharing code works for anyone who has it, as often as it is used, and it never expires. Lock a code with a PIN or a password, and send the PIN or password by another route than the code; see “Locking a code”.

Other error sentences

These sentences appear in the failure message over a picture, above the timeline of the recordings panel, in the add-device form and in Edit Credentials. The first four are explained with the checks in “When adding fails: the checklist”.

SentenceMeaningWhat to do
Device unreachable. Check the address and your network.No answer from the device. After an attempt to add, the line below names the open ports that were found, or states No open ports were found at this address.See “When adding fails: the checklist” and “Where to start”.

With a brand chosen under Connect using, the sentence also means that the device answered at none of the stream paths of that brand.Try another connection method under Advanced › Connect using, or RTSP with the stream path of the camera; see “Connection methods”.
This camera is offline.The channel has no signal.See “Live view”.
Could not connect to the video stream.The connection to the video port was refused or timed out. A refused port is reported at once.Check that RTSP is switched on and that the RTSP port is correct (usually 554).
The device refused the video stream (HTTP 404).The device answered the video request with a status other than a sign-in refusal. The number is the status of the device.Check the account rights for live view, the stream settings and the number of viewers of the device.
The recorder answered with HTTP 500.The recorder answered a request with an error status.Try again later, restart the recorder if needed, and check its firmware.

Add it again and choose ONVIF under “Connect using”.The recorder was added through its own protocol, and it encrypts the video sent that way.Delete the device and add it again with ONVIF chosen under Advanced › Connect using.
