Could not save the password securely. Please try again.The new password could not be stored on this device. The previous one was kept.Try again.
The device sent an unexpected reply.The device answered in a form that Cam Hub cannot read.Try again. When it persists, note the model and the firmware version and contact the developer; see “Reaching the developer”.
Surveillance Station refused the request.The network storage device refused the request of the account.Check that the account is allowed to use the recording software of the network storage device. Cam Hub has no field for a verification code, so an account that requires two-step verification cannot be used.
The connection timed out.The device took too long to answer.Check the network, then try again.
No internet connection. or Could not reach the server.The phone has no internet connection, or the server cannot be reached.Check the mobile data or Wi-Fi connection of the phone, then try again.
Something went wrong. Please try again.An unexpected error.Try again, and work through “When adding fails: the checklist”.

Some messages come from the video stream itself and are shown in English whatever the language of the app, for example Connection closed or HTTP 404. They have the same meaning as the sentences above.

Permission requests and system dialogs

Cam Hub asks for as few permissions as possible. It never asks for access to the photo library, notifications, contacts or Bluetooth, and it sends no notifications. The microphone is requested only for talking through a camera.

RequestWhen it appearsWhat to know
Local NetworkThe first time the app contacts an address on the local network: when a device is added, when the connection indicator of the list checks a device, when a scan runs, or when a stream starts. The text reads “Cam Hub connects to cameras and recorders and scans a subnet you choose to find equipment on your local network.”Allow it; without it, no device on the home network can be reached. When it was refused, adding a device fails with Device unreachable. Check the address and your network., pictures do not load, and a scan finds nothing. The procedure below turns the permission on.
MicrophoneThe first time the talk button of a camera is held. The text reads “Cam Hub uses the microphone only while you hold Talk to speak through a camera's speaker.”When it was refused, holding the talk button shows Microphone access is off for Cam Hub. Turn it on in Settings to talk through the camera. Microphone access can be changed in the system settings. See “Two-way talk”.
CameraOnly when Take Photo is chosen for a picture in an empty slot of LiveView Mix. The text reads “Cam Hub uses the camera only when you choose Take Photo for a LiveView Mix slot.”When it was refused, use Choose Photo instead. Camera access can be changed in the system settings.
PhotosNot requested. Choose Photo uses the system picker, and a snapshot is passed on through the share sheet.Cam Hub never writes to the photo library by itself. Save a snapshot from the share sheet.
Location, while in useThe first time the Speedometer of the Tools tab opens; see “Speedometer and compass”.It is used only for the speed and the compass heading, and is neither stored nor shared. There is no access in the background. When it is refused, the Speedometer shows an orange line and the button Open Settings.
iCloudNo request. Backup and restore need a device that is signed in to iCloud with an Apple Account.When backup fails, see “Sharing, import and iCloud backup”.
Purchases, Manage Subscription and Redeem CodeSystem sheets of the App Store, opened from the Settings tab or from the plans page.Confirm with the Apple Account. See “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”.
Share linksA link of the form https://cam-hub.almx.cc/i#… opens the import page of Cam Hub with the code already entered.The code is in the part of the address after the #, which is not sent to a server. See “Importing cameras”.
MailEmail to developer in the device report opens the mail composer of the system, addressed to the developer.Nothing is sent until Send is tapped in the composer. Without a mail account, the screen shows Mail isn't set up on this device; the report is copied and stays on the device, and the copy expires after about 2 minutes. See “Device report (experimental)”.
Rating requestThe system may ask for a rating after a successful backup.The request can be dismissed.

Turning on the Local Network permission after it was refused:

  1. Open the system Settings app and tap Privacy & Security.

    Check: The list of privacy categories is shown.

  2. Tap Local Network.

    Check: The list of apps that asked for local network access is shown, each with a switch.

  3. Switch on Cam Hub.

    Check: The switch next to Cam Hub is on.

  4. Return to Cam Hub and repeat the action that failed.

    Check: The device is reached, or the scan lists devices.

Reaching the developer

The settings of the app have no support row; the row User Manual at the end of the Settings tab opens this manual. The developer can be reached in three ways:

  • Support page: support.html on the website of Cam Hub. It holds notes on compatibility, a list of checks before a connection problem is reported, and the contact address.
  • Email: app-dev@almx.cc. This is the address to which the mail composer of the device report is already addressed.
  • Device report: after a failed attempt to add a device, the experimental report collects technical details and offers to email them; see “Device report (experimental)”.

A message helps the developer most when it states:

  • the version of the app, shown in Settings › About › Version;
  • the model of the iPhone or iPad and the version of its system;
  • the brand and model of the camera or recorder, and the version of its firmware;
  • the connection method that was used;
  • the exact message that the screen showed, and what was tried before.
Never send these items

The password of a camera, the PIN or password of a sharing code, a complete sharing code, an SNMP community, and the public address with which a device is reached over the internet. The developer never needs them.

A device that cannot be supported by design, for example one that works only through the cloud app of its maker, cannot be fixed by a message; see “Requirements and limits”. Questions about charges and refunds go to Apple.

Questions and answers

Why does the app always open on the LiveView Mix tab?

The app always opens on the first tab. In Settings › Open on launch, the Live tab of a chosen device, or the full-screen LiveView Mix wall, can open instead. The choice Last viewed does not restore the last tab. See “LiveView Mix in Settings”.

Why is the app always dark?

Cam Hub has one appearance, and the settings contain no row for it.

Why are there no notifications for motion or alarms?

Cam Hub is a viewer. It sends no push notifications and no local notifications, and it asks for no permission for them.

Can cameras be watched from outside the home?

Cam Hub connects directly to the devices and uses no cloud service of its own. A device outside the home network can be reached only with an address that is reachable from the internet, or through a VPN back to the home network. A private VPN is the safer way, because it keeps the device off the open internet.

Can a recording be saved or exported?

No. Recordings can only be watched. A snapshot is a still image that the device supplies at the moment of the tap; during playback it shows the current live picture. See “What is not available”.

Why is there no sound?

Sound is off until the speaker button is tapped, and the button appears only when the stream carries sound in a supported format. Wall tiles, YouTube and Twitch tiles included, never play sound. See “Live view”.

Can Cam Hub talk through a camera?

Yes, for a camera that has a talk channel which Cam Hub can use: hold the talk button on the camera page and speak. See “Two-way talk”.

Why does SD look like HD?

Some devices serve one stream for every channel. SD and HD then show the same picture. Devices added with a brand chosen under Connect using usually behave this way. See “What works with which method”.

Why do the times of the recordings differ from the clock of the phone?

The times belong to the clock of the device and are never converted. Correct the date, the time and the time zone on the device; see “While a recording plays”.

A camera works in the app of its maker, but not in Cam Hub. What helps?

Try another connection method under Advanced › Connect using (ONVIF, RTSP or a brand from the list), switch on ONVIF and RTSP on the device, create a separate ONVIF user where the device has its own list, and check the video format. Devices that need the cloud of their maker cannot be added. See “Requirements and limits”.

Can a device that accepts only HTTPS be added?

No. Cam Hub controls devices over plain HTTP. A device with HTTP switched off cannot be added. For network storage devices, the port of the HTTP web interface is entered, not the port of the HTTPS one. See “Requirements and limits”.

How are the address or the password of a saved device changed?

The username and the password are changed with Edit Credentials on the device page; see “Changing the user name and password of a device”. The address cannot be changed: a new address creates a new device, so delete the old one first. See “The Add Device form”.

How many cameras can be watched without a plan?

Two enabled channels in the whole app, and one recorder. YouTube live streams and Twitch channels do not count. See “The allowance of each plan”.

Does a plan apply to all devices that use the same Apple Account?

Yes, on every iPhone, iPad and Apple TV that is signed in with the same Apple Account. On a new device, tap Restore Purchases. See “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”.

All data was deleted. Can the cameras be recovered?

Only from an iCloud backup that was made before, with Restore from iCloud; see “Restoring from iCloud”. Without such a backup, the passwords of the cameras cannot be recovered, because they are stored only on the device where they were entered. Plans are not affected by Delete All Data.

Does the device report send the password?

No. The password is never part of the report, and nothing is sent unless the person chooses to email it. See “Device report (experimental)”.

Why does the screen not turn off?

While a live picture or a recording is on the screen, the app keeps the screen awake. Leaving the video, or leaving the app, ends this.

Why does the picture stop when another app is opened?

Every stream stops when the app leaves the foreground, and sound never plays in the background. When the app returns, the streams connect again.

16Supported brands and connection methods

This is the only chapter that names brands. It lists the connection methods of the add-device form, what each one makes possible, what a device must offer, and what to prepare on a device before it is added. Everything else in this manual describes functions without naming a brand.

Connection methods

The list Advanced › Connect using in the add-device form starts with four methods: Auto-detect, ONVIF, Xiongmai (XMEye) and RTSP. Below them, the section Brands lists 71 brands in alphabetical order, with a search field that also finds a brand by other names under which its cameras are sold. Hikvision, Dahua and Synology are not in the list: Auto-detect finds them with their own protocols. The form itself is described in “The Add Device form” and the choice in “Choosing the connection method”.

ChoiceWhat Cam Hub doesSuitable forAccount
Auto-detect (default) First checks, without signing in, which ports are open at the address. Then tries, in this order: on the main web port, a brand recognized there, then the protocol of Hikvision, the protocol of Dahua and the programming interface of Synology Surveillance Station; one of these three recognized on another port, for example the web port 5000 of a Synology NAS; Xiongmai's own protocol on port 34567, at local addresses only; ONVIF on each port where it answered; and plain RTSP on each RTSP port that answered, with the paths of a brand that the device revealed, then the paths that most cameras use, then the paths of every brand in the list. The first way that connects is kept, with its port. A refused sign-in from Hikvision, Dahua, Synology or Xiongmai ends the attempt at once; ONVIF and RTSP end it after the second refusal. A port typed under Advanced is tried first, and a typed port other than 80 or 554 that is open is used alone. Most devices: cameras and recorders of Hikvision, Dahua and Synology, Xiongmai devices in the local network, any device with ONVIF, and cameras that serve RTSP at a common path or at a path of a brand in the list. The account of the device. For Synology: an account of the network storage device that may use Surveillance Station.
ONVIF Skips the detection and uses only the open ONVIF protocol, on the port in HTTP Port. Cam Hub looks for the service at /onvif/device_service and, when that address does not answer, at /onvif/service and /onvif/device. The video is fetched at the address that the device announces. Any camera or recorder with ONVIF; also a Hikvision, Dahua or Synology device that is to be used over ONVIF. The ONVIF user of the device. Where the device keeps a separate list of ONVIF users, a user has to exist in that list.
Xiongmai (XMEye) Uses Xiongmai's own protocol (XMEye / NetSurveillance) on the port in Device Port, 34567 unless it was changed or forwarded. Any address is accepted, also one outside the local network; for such an address the form warns that the protocol does not encrypt the video and that many devices protect the password only weakly. Xiongmai cameras and recorders that Auto-detect does not find, that use another port, or that are reached from outside the local network. The account of the device.
RTSP Connects over plain RTSP and tries the paths that most cameras use, or the path entered. No control interface of the device is contacted. Live view only. A camera of any brand with ONVIF switched off, when its brand is not in the list. The camera account of the device.
A brand from the list (see “The brands in the list”) Connects over plain RTSP, at the stream paths that the maker documents. No control interface of the device is contacted. Live view only. Devices of that brand when ONVIF is switched off or does not work, and recorders of that brand that offer only RTSP. The camera account of the device; for five of the brands a separate account.

Auto-detect is the starting point. ONVIF is the next choice when Auto-detect reports Not a supported device., or when a device is to be used over ONVIF on purpose. Xiongmai (XMEye) is the choice for a Xiongmai device that Auto-detect cannot reach. A brand from the list, or RTSP, is the last choice, for a device with ONVIF switched off. A Xiongmai recorder that reports that it encrypts its video cannot be watched over Xiongmai's own protocol; Auto-detect then moves on to ONVIF, and such a recorder is added with ONVIF. The developer has tested selected Hikvision, Dahua and Synology devices. Whether a particular model works, with any method, depends on its firmware, its settings, its stream format, its account rights and the network.

What works with which method

The table shows what Cam Hub offers for each method. Yes means that the function is offered. If supported means that the function appears only when the device itself offers it. No means that Cam Hub does not offer the function with this method. The notes below the table give the details.

FunctionHikvisionDahuaSynology Surveillance StationXiongmai (XMEye)ONVIFRTSP and brands from the list
Live viewYesYesYesYesIf supportedYes
SD and HDYesYesHiddenYesIf supportedIf supported
Recording playbackYesYesYesYesIf supportedNo
Playback speed 2×, 4×, 8×If supportedIf supportedNoNoIf supportedNo
Days with recordings marked in the calendarIf supportedNoNoNoNoNo
Search for peopleIf supportedNoNoNoNoNo
PTZIf supportedIf supportedIf supportedIf supportedIf supportedNo
Aiming by tapping or drawing a boxIf supportedNoNoNoNoNo
SnapshotYesYesYesYesIf supportedNo
Sound (listening)If supportedIf supportedIf supportedIf supportedIf supportedIf supported
Talking through the cameraIf supportedNoNoNoNoNo
Disk HealthYesYesIf set upNoNoNo
Channel listFor recordersFor recordersYesYesYesTyped number
  • Live view: with ONVIF, the device must announce a stream address; when the device does not name its media service, Cam Hub asks at the usual addresses of that service. Video is fetched over RTSP on TCP, and over UDP when the device refuses TCP.
  • SD and HD: with Synology Surveillance Station, the choice is hidden, and SD uses the low-resolution stream of a camera that has one. With Xiongmai, HD is the main stream and SD the extra stream. With ONVIF, the largest profile of the device is HD and the smallest is SD, and a single profile serves both. With RTSP and the brands from the list, SD uses the second stream that belongs to the path found, where the device serves it; otherwise SD shows the same stream as HD.
  • Recording playback: with Hikvision, a camera with its own storage plays back like a recorder. With Dahua, the recorder's main stream is played, and moving to another time starts the playback again at that moment. With Synology Surveillance Station and Xiongmai, the recording is streamed from the chosen moment. With ONVIF, the device needs the search and replay services that ONVIF defines for playback.
  • Playback speed: with Hikvision, Dahua and ONVIF, the recorder may refuse a faster speed, and Cam Hub then shows a notice. With Synology Surveillance Station and Xiongmai, streamed playback has no speed button.
  • Calendar: a Hikvision recorder that reports which days hold recordings has those days marked in the calendar of the playback date; see “The recording calendar”.
  • Search for people: the recorder needs an index of detected people.
  • PTZ: with Hikvision, a channel needs PTZ switched on; saved positions appear when the device lists them, and the home position is always available. With Dahua, PTZ must be bound to that channel; saved positions are offered, but there is no home position. With Synology Surveillance Station, the controls follow what the system reports for the camera: four directions, and the home position when it is reported. With Xiongmai, a camera with a head gets directions, zoom and saved positions 1 to 16 by number, without a home position. With ONVIF, the axes follow what the device reports; a camera with zoom only gets no direction pad. See “PTZ control: moving the camera”.
  • Aiming: offered when a Hikvision camera reports that it supports positioning by a point or an area of the picture.
  • Snapshot: with Xiongmai, the picture is taken from the first full frame of the live stream. With ONVIF, the device must give a snapshot address.
  • Sound: with Synology Surveillance Station, only G.711 plays over its usual streaming path. Xiongmai devices send G.711.
  • Talking: offered for standalone Hikvision cameras that report a two-way audio channel in G.711; not for the channels of a recorder. See “Two-way talk”.
  • Disk Health: Hikvision reports the state of each disk, with S.M.A.R.T. details where the device provides them. Dahua reports state, capacity and, where available, temperature, but no S.M.A.R.T. details. A Synology NAS is read over SNMP, which must be switched on at the NAS and set up in Cam Hub. See “Disk Health”.
  • Channel list: Hikvision and Dahua list the channels of a recorder with names and signal state, and a device that is not a recorder has one channel. Synology Surveillance Station lists every camera of the system as a channel with its signal state. Xiongmai devices report their number of channels and the names given to them, without a signal state. ONVIF lists one channel for each separate video source and does not report a signal state. RTSP and the brands from the list have no list: the number of cameras is entered (1 to 64), and every channel is shown as online.

Not available with any method: focus and iris control, saving or exporting recordings, logging in to a cloud account, and a connection over HTTPS.

The brands in the list

The brands in the Brands section are connected over plain RTSP. Selecting a brand adds a section named after it, with the field Cameras (1 to 64) and a path field. With 1, the device is added as a camera that is named after the brand; with a larger number, it is added as a recorder with channels CH1 to CHn, and it counts as a recorder for the plan. A blank path field makes Cam Hub try the documented paths in turn and keep the one that the device answers. Only a particular path needs to be entered. The choice RTSP works the same way with the paths that most cameras use.

The 71 brands: 2N, 3S Vision / A-Linking, ACTi, Acumen, AirLive, ANNKE, Apexis / Sumpple, Arecont Vision, Avigilon, AVTECH, Axis, Basler, Beward, Bosch Security, Brickcom, Canon, COMPRO, D-Link, DIGITUS, DynaColor, EDIMAX, eneo, EnGenius, Etrovision, eufy, EverFocus, EZVIZ, FlexWATCH, Foscam, GeoVision, Grandstream, Hanwha Vision (Wisenet), HVIEW, i-PRO (Panasonic), IDIS, Imou, INSTAR, iPUX, IQinVision (IQeye), Jovision, JVC, LILIN, Lorex, Messoa, Milesight, MOBOTIX, NEXCOM, Night Owl, Oncam, Pelco, PiXORD, Reolink, SHANY, Siemens, Sony, Sricam, StarDot, Sunell, Swann, TP-Link (Tapo / VIGI), TRENDnet, TVT, UniFi (Ubiquiti), Uniview (UNV), VIVOTEK, Vstarcam, Wansview, Wyze, Y-cam, YI / Kami, Zavio.

  • Separate account: Axis, TP-Link (Tapo / VIGI), ANNKE, MOBOTIX and 2N need their own camera or ONVIF account, created in the web interface or the app of the maker, before RTSP works. The administrator login alone may be refused.
  • RTSP port: three brands use another default port, which the form fills in when the brand is selected: ACTi 7070, Foscam 88 and Vstarcam 10554.
  • Recorders: a documented recorder form exists for 3S Vision / A-Linking, ANNKE, AVTECH, Beward, DIGITUS, eneo, eufy, GeoVision, Hanwha Vision (Wisenet), IDIS, Imou, Lorex, Milesight, Night Owl, Pelco (encoders), Reolink, Sunell, Swann, TP-Link (Tapo / VIGI) (VIGI recorders), TRENDnet, TVT, Uniview (UNV) and VIVOTEK. For the other brands, the camera paths are used for every channel; only a path that contains a channel number reaches a different camera on each channel.
  • Paths that vary: for many brands, some paths depend on the model or the firmware, so the first attempt may not match. The form shows a note below the path field for these brands.
  • Auto-detect uses the same paths: when no other way connects, Auto-detect tries the paths of every brand in the list by itself and adds the camera as a single camera. Selecting a brand by hand is needed mainly for a recorder, to enter the number of cameras, or to pin one path.

Notes on selected brands:

These paths follow the documentation of each maker and, where a maker publishes none, common references. Results depend on the model and the firmware. A device with ONVIF switched on is better connected with Auto-detect or ONVIF, because Cam Hub then asks the device for its stream address instead of trying paths.

Live view only

A connection through RTSP or one of these brands has no recording playback, no PTZ control, no snapshot and no channel list. The functions are listed in “What works with which method”.

Requirements and limits

TopicRequirement or limit
Plain HTTP onlyCam Hub contacts devices over plain HTTP; Xiongmai devices over their own protocol instead. Video is fetched over RTSP, on TCP first and on UDP when the device refuses TCP. HTTPS and self-signed certificates are not supported for devices. A device with HTTP switched off, or one that accepts HTTPS only, cannot be added. For a network storage device, enter the port of its HTTP web interface, for example 5000, not the port of the HTTPS interface.
ONVIF switched onFor the choice ONVIF, ONVIF must be switched on at the device. Cam Hub looks for the service at /onvif/device_service, /onvif/service or /onvif/device on the port entered in HTTP Port. Some devices have ONVIF switched off in the factory settings.
RTSP switched onVideo is fetched over RTSP. With Auto-detect, Cam Hub finds the RTSP port; otherwise it uses the port entered in RTSP Port (usually 554). A network storage device may use its own streaming path first. Where the device has a setting for RTSP authentication, Digest is the method to select.
A separate ONVIF userSome devices keep a list of ONVIF users that is separate from the users of the web interface, and the administrator login does not work for ONVIF. Create a user in that list. Five brands in the list need their own camera or ONVIF account before RTSP works: Axis, TP-Link (Tapo / VIGI), ANNKE, MOBOTIX and 2N.
Account rightsThe account needs the right to view live video, and for playback the right to read recordings. For Synology, the account must be allowed to use Surveillance Station. Cam Hub has no field for a verification code, so an account that requires two-step verification cannot be used.
Clock of the deviceThe ONVIF sign-in carries a time stamp of the device. A clock that is minutes off makes the sign-in fail. Set the time on the device, for example with network time. The times of recordings are the clock of the recorder.
Same network, no cloudCam Hub connects directly to the address of the device and has no cloud relay. From outside the home network, a device can be reached only through an address that is reachable from the internet, or through a VPN. Devices that work only through the cloud app of their maker cannot be added, and Cam Hub offers no sign-in to a cloud account.
Xiongmai outside the local networkAuto-detect speaks Xiongmai's own protocol only to local addresses. A Xiongmai device behind a forwarded port or a dynamic domain name is added with Xiongmai (XMEye). The protocol does not encrypt the video, and many devices protect the password only weakly, so a VPN is the safer way.
Video formatsCam Hub plays H.264 and H.265, decoded in hardware by the phone. A phone without hardware support for H.265, and a picture size above the limit of the decoder, give no picture. MJPEG is used only as a fallback for live view with one of the families.
SoundFor listening, G.711 (A-law and µ-law) and AAC-LC are played; any other format is silent. Talking through the camera works only with standalone Hikvision cameras that offer two-way audio in G.711.
Locked accountsAfter several wrong attempts, a device can lock the account, often for about 30 minutes. The port check of Auto-detect sends no sign-in. Cam Hub stops at the first sign-in refused by a brand's own protocol and after the second one refused over ONVIF or RTSP, and the device report sends no further sign-in after a refusal.
Adding a device againThe same address, port and username update the stored device instead of creating a second one.

Cameras and recorders

The badge in the device list reads Camera or Recorder. A recorder uses a place in the recorder allowance of the plan, as described in “What uses allowance”. Cam Hub decides as follows.

MethodA device counts as a recorder when
Hikvisionthe device type reported by the device contains NVR or DVR
Dahuathe model name contains NVR, DVR or XVR; otherwise the device is one camera
Synology Surveillance Stationalways; every camera of the system is a channel
Xiongmai (XMEye)the device reports more than one channel, or its device type contains DVR or NVR
ONVIFthe device has more than one separate video source; a camera with several sensors can therefore count as a recorder
RTSP found by Auto-detectnever; the device is added as one camera
RTSP and brands from the list, selected by handthe number in the field Cameras is larger than 1

What to prepare on the device

The following checklist applies to every brand. Items that the device does not have can be skipped.

  • Activate the device and set an administrator password. A new device must be activated before any app can sign in; see “Activating a new device”.
  • Give the device a fixed address in the home network, in the device or as a reservation in the router. Cam Hub keeps the address that was entered; see “A device is added, but it is not reachable”.
  • Place the phone and the device in the same network, without a guest network, a separate VLAN, client isolation or a VPN between them.
  • Switch on the HTTP service of the device and note its port, usually 80.
  • Switch on RTSP and note its port, usually 554. Select Digest for RTSP authentication where the device offers the choice.
  • Switch on ONVIF where the device has the setting, and create a separate ONVIF or camera user where the device keeps its own list or the brand requires one.
  • Set the date, the time and the time zone, for example with network time.
  • Set the video to H.264 or H.265, at a moderate resolution, with a key frame interval of one to two seconds. Use a sub stream with a lower resolution for SD where the device offers one.
  • Use an account that may view live video and, for playback, read recordings of the channels that are to be shown.
  • For playback, check that the device records and that a disk or card is present.
  • For Disk Health of a Synology NAS, switch on SNMP at the NAS.
  • Note the address, the username and the password, which the add-device form asks for, and the ports in case Auto-detect does not find the device.
Devices that cannot be added

A device that works only through the cloud app of its maker, offers no connection on the local network, or accepts HTTPS only, cannot be added to Cam Hub.

Activating a new device

A new or reset device of some brands, Hikvision among them, has no administrator password yet. It must be activated before any app can sign in: activation sets the administrator password. Until then, every sign-in is refused, and adding the device fails with Wrong username or password.

The network scan can show that a Hikvision device is not activated yet:

  • When the device answers the scan's question and reports that it is not activated, its row in Found Devices shows Not activated; see “Finding devices with the network scan”.
  • The add-device form opened from that row starts with the notice This Hikvision device has not been activated yet. Activate it first — with Hikvision's SADP tool or the device's own web page — by setting an admin password.
  • A device that does not answer the scan's question shows no such mark, whether it is activated or not.

To activate a device:

  1. Activate the device with the maker's own tool or on the device's own web page, as its documentation describes, and set the administrator password there.

    Check: The device accepts a sign-in with the administrator account and the new password, for example on its web page.

  2. In the add-device form of Cam Hub, enter the administrator account, usually admin, and the new password, then tap Add.

    Check: The form closes and the device appears in the device list.

If adding still fails, see “When adding fails: the checklist”.

The compatibility reference in the app

Path: Devices › ＋ › Add Device › Compatibility reference. The page Compatibility lists what the developer states as supported and not supported.

  • Supported: Hikvision and Dahua, both marked Recommended, then Synology, Xiongmai (XMEye), SoCatch (iWatch) with the note Local-network (LAN) connection, Most RTSP cameras and Most ONVIF cameras.
  • Not supported: the connection of SoCatch (iWatch) over the wide area, because it runs through the remote-access service of its maker, which is closed to other apps. Such cameras are to be added on the local network.
  • The Hikvision entry has the button How to keep it off the internet, with notes on keeping a camera without a gateway, on blocking its internet access, and on watching from outside the home network through a private VPN. In some regions, the button or one of the notes is not shown.
  • A note at the bottom states that the names are trademarks of their owners, that Cam Hub is developed independently, and that a successful connection means technical compatibility only.
  • The entry Compatibility reference is not shown in a form that was opened from a scan result that named the brand of the device.

About this manual

This manual describes Cam Hub 1.8 on iPhone, iPad and iPhone Duo. Apple TV is covered in Chapter 14, “Apple TV”, and the Apple Watch app in “Buttons on Apple Watch”.

Scope

  • App and devices: Cam Hub 1.8 on iPhone, iPad and iPhone Duo. All three run the same app; the manual notes where they differ, and “iPhone Duo” describes the displays of the iPhone Duo. The Apple TV app is not described screen by screen; Chapter 14, “Apple TV” gives the recommended way to bring a setup to it and lists what differs. The Apple Watch app, which sends the requests of control-panel buttons, is described with the control panels in “Buttons on Apple Watch”.
  • Content: every function that the app offers to the user is described: adding devices, YouTube live streams and Twitch channels, live view and talking through a camera, recording playback, LiveView Mix, control panels, disk health, sharing and backup, plans, tools and settings, with the error messages and permission requests that can appear.
  • What the app does not have: Cam Hub sends no notifications, it has no account of its own, and it uses no cloud service for video. Video and sound travel directly between the device and the iPhone or iPad. Only YouTube live streams and Twitch channels come over the internet, played by those services' own players.
  • Brands: only Chapter 16, “Supported brands and connection methods” names brands of cameras and recorders. All other chapters describe functions by capability, for example “devices that support playback”. YouTube and Twitch are video services, not camera brands, and are named where they are described.

Conventions

  • Figures: all figures show the English interface with sample data.
  • Labels: names of screens, buttons and settings are written as the app shows them, in the language of this manual, for example Devices. A path such as Settings › About › Version names the screens in the order in which they are opened. When the app is set to another language, its labels differ; the language is chosen in the Settings tab.
  • Typed values: addresses, port numbers and text to be typed are set in a fixed-width type, for example 192.168.1.64 or 554.
  • Procedures: each numbered step is one action. A line that begins with “Check:” states what the screen shows afterwards. A procedure starts with its prerequisites where there are any.
  • Cross-references: a reference to another chapter or section gives its title, and it is a link.

Where to get help

  • Messages, empty screens, permission requests and common questions are explained in Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.
  • Failures while adding a device are covered in “When adding fails: the checklist”.
  • How to reach the developer, and what to include in a message, is described in “Reaching the developer”. The support page of the Cam Hub website, support.html, repeats the notes on compatibility and lists the contact address.
  • In the app, the row User Manual at the end of the Settings tab opens this manual.
